docs.text:
Nowcasts and forecasts of confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease cases for the BDBV Modeling Hub.

The BDBV Modeling Hub target is weekly confirmed cases by symptom-onset week, nationally, by province and by health zone, as 100 joint sample trajectories. Two hub models are submitted, seabbs-rwnowcast and seabbs-renewal.

docs.title: Models
docs.text: randomwalknowcast is baselinenowcast (Johnson et al. 2025, Wellcome Open Research) with a random walk on top, and randomwalk is the same walk with no nowcast (Baseline models). The renewal models (renewal, renewalsp and renewalbvd) are built on PyRenew and fit the hub's known and imputed onsets (Renewal models). Each week randomwalknowcast is submitted as seabbs-rwnowcast and the first renewal model to pass its checks as seabbs-renewal (Submission workflow).

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Section What it holds Setup Install the package and run it from a script, a REPL or a notebook. Getting started Forecast, plot and score the two baselines in Python. Methods Data, Baseline models, Renewal models, Evaluation and Implementation. Results Data, nowcast, backtest, simulation checks and comparison with hub forecasts. Submission The workflow, hub specification, opting in and submission log. Development The model building ladder, the development log, contributing, adding a model and the CLI. API reference The Python package.

docs.title: Data credit
docs.text: Surveillance data: Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP) and the Incident Management Support Team (IMST), Democratic Republic of the Congo. Processed by ACCIDDA and the Kinshasa School of Public Health, University of Kinshasa, and distributed through the BDBV Modeling Hub.

docs.title: Sampler
docs.text:
Backtest fits use 2 chains of 500 warm-up and 500 draws at a target acceptance of 0.8. Submission fits use

  • renewalbvd: 2 chains of 500 warm-up and 1000 draws at a target acceptance of 0.95
  • renewalsp: 2 chains of 500 warm-up and 500 draws at a target acceptance of 0.9
  • renewal: 2 chains of 500 warm-up and 500 draws at a target acceptance of 0.9
Convergence by model

Columns are as on the Implementation page.

  title = {{BDBVHubRenewal}: renewal-model nowcasts and forecasts for the {BDBV} Modeling Hub},

docs.title: Citing the data
docs.text: The data come from the BDBV Modeling Hub. Credit them as the hub asks. The surveillance data are from the Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP) and the Incident Management Support Team (IMST), Democratic Republic of the Congo. They are processed by the Atlantic Coast Center for Infectious Disease Dynamics and Analytics (ACCIDDA) and the Kinshasa School of Public Health, University of Kinshasa.

docs.text:
Our models and the forecasts submitted to the hub's weekly round, scored on the same data.

Fitted models' results come from the fit store, fitted at bc134cc.

Fits still running

Fits for this build's code (0e23a93) are still running. Fits of older code are shown for pprandomwalknowcast at 2026-08-18 and 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-24 and 2026-11-01; renewal at 2026-08-18 and 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-24 and 2026-11-01; renewalbvd at 2026-08-18 and 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-24 and 2026-11-01; renewalsp at 2026-08-18 and 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-24 and 2026-11-01.

Scores on the weeks the latest release reports in full, from the release serving each round (how scoring works). A series marked submitted is the file we sent to a round, and one marked main build is the current main branch's forecast for every round, so a round we did not submit to shows only the main build.

docs.title: Negative updates
docs.text:
A count falls when a release reports fewer cases for a place and onset week than the release before it. Each release is compared with the one before it, on the weeks of the earlier release with cases in either. A health zone missing from a release has no cases, so a zone that disappears counts as a fall to zero.

Share of place-weeks that fell (top) and cases removed as a share of all change (bottom), by the onset week's age at the earlier release. The 2026-08-18 to 2026-10-09 comparison spans seven weeks and the others one week. No national or province count fell while its onset week was less than three weeks old. Most falls came between the 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-24 releases, mainly in Nord Kivu.

Over all releases, 8 of 102 national weeks fell, 25 of 357 province weeks and 85 of 2738 health zone weeks. Falls removed 24 cases nationally against 2684 added, 1% of all change. They were 2% of all change for provinces and 4% for health zones. No fall was larger than 8 cases.

docs.title: Missing onsets
docs.text:
The hub publishes, for every vintage, the cases in each province and onset week with an imputed onset. How the hub imputes them is on the methods page.

Imputed share of cases by onset week, by vintage. Point size grows with the week's count. It varies over time and between provinces. Share of all cases with an imputed onset in each release. Nationally it stays between 15% and 17%. In Nord Kivu it fell from 24% to 14% between the 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-24 releases, as cases gained an onset. Sud Ubangi's few cases all have an imputed onset.

The change between vintages approximates the cases reported without an onset. It is net of cases that gain an onset later, so it can be negative.

Cases added between vintages, by onset status. In Nord Kivu between 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-24, imputed onsets fell by 174 while known onsets rose by 379, so many cases gained an onset after their first report. docs.title: Getting started¶
docs.text:
Forecast with two baselines, load the renewal model's stored fit at the same origin, then plot and score all three.

Every figure and table below comes from the Python code shown above it, which calls the package's functions directly. Setup installs the package and shows how to run this code in a REPL, a notebook or a script. The tidy data in data/ are committed, and task fit-store fetches the stored renewal fit. This page is a notebook, and task getting-started runs it again.

docs.title: Load the data¶
docs.text: load_target reads the weekly confirmed cases by onset week of every hub vintage. load_daily reads the daily onsets of every hub release, which the baselines need. load_delays reads the reporting delays the hub published, which the renewal models use.

docs.title: Build the forecast task¶
docs.text: The origin is the second newest release. The newest release scores it. The task holds what a model sees at the origin, including the daily onsets of every release up to it, and the weeks to forecast. Its reference date is the Saturday after the origin, and the forecast weeks run from four weeks before it to three weeks after it. origin_tasks builds the task of every real origin as the fit store fits it, so the baselines and the stored renewal fit see the same task.

docs.title: Forecast with the baselines¶
docs.text: get_model returns a model from the registry by name. randomwalk carries the last complete week forward with random walk noise on the log scale. randomwalknowcast nowcasts the recent weeks first (Baseline models). randomwalknowcast is the baseline we submit to the hub as seabbs-rwnowcast. run_forecasts runs each model, checks the samples, adds the national total and returns 100 trajectories per location.

docs.title: Fit the renewal model¶
docs.text:
The renewal model is fitted by MCMC (NUTS), which takes about half an hour, so this page does not fit it. The fit store fits it in CI at every real origin and stores the result. This is how it is fitted, with the sampler settings of the submission:

fitted = store.fit(
    "renewal", task, store.code_digest(), store.samplers()["renewal"]
)
store.write_fit("output/fit-store", fitted)

The page loads the stored fit instead.

docs.title: Load the stored renewal fit¶
docs.text: bdbvhubrenewal fit-store load (task fit-store) fetches the store and records the fit it uses for each model and origin in results/fit-store.json. That is the fit for this code and data, or, until that fit is made, the newest fit of older code. Each stored fit is a gzipped JSON file, which read_fit reads into tables. Its forecasts table has the same columns as the baselines' forecasts.

docs.title: Plot the nowcast¶
docs.text: Recent weeks are still being reported, so the weeks before the reference date are nowcasts. The first figure keeps only those weeks, to show what the nowcast adds to the data at the origin. Each panel shows the data at the origin and as later reported, with the forecast fans (reading the figures). The panels are the national total and the three provinces with the most cases. save_light_dark writes a light and a dark version of each figure.

docs.title: Plot the forecast¶
docs.text: The second figure adds the reference week and the three forecast weeks.

docs.title: Score¶
docs.text: Each forecast is scored on what each later release reported (how scoring works). release_backtest maps the forecast of final counts to the counts a later release would report, using the reporting delays fitted at the origin. It scores the mapped samples with the weighted interval score (WIS) and interval coverage. The table gives each model's mean WIS relative to randomwalk, for the national total and over the provinces. as reported uses the data at the origin as the forecast.

docs.title: Next steps¶
docs.text: The API reference documents every function used here, grouped by task. The CLI page lists the commands the submission workflow runs. They fetch the data, run the backtest, forecast from the latest vintage and write the hub file.

docs.title: Delay and spread
docs.text:
The growth to final of each onset day by its age at the latest release, and the observation model by weeks back. A place using its parent's estimate is labelled with the parent. How both are fitted is on the Baseline models page.

The renewal models fit the onset-to-report delay with the cases (delays). Each row is one fit at its latest origin: renewal and renewalbvd fit one delay for all provinces, and renewalsp one per province it fits. renewal and renewalbvd give nearly the same delay, so their lines overlap. The left panel gives the share of onsets in the last week reported by each day since onset, with 90% intervals. It stops the day before the longest delay, where the model puts all later reports. The dashed line is randomwalknowcast's share reported by age at the same release. The right panel gives the mean delay by onset week, with 90% intervals.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Install uv, which manages Python and the packages for you.

curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

Clone the repository and install the package and its dependencies into .venv/.

git clone https://github.com/seabbs/BDBVHubRenewal.git
cd BDBVHubRenewal
uv sync

Run every command below from the BDBVHubRenewal folder. The hub data are committed in data/, so nothing needs downloading. uv run bdbvhubrenewal data fetches the latest hub data when you want it.

docs.title: Work interactively
docs.text:
uv run runs a command inside the project's environment.

To Run Open a Python REPL uv run python Open an IPython REPL uv run --with ipython ipython Open Jupyter Lab uv run --with jupyterlab jupyter lab Run a script uv run python my_forecast.py

In VS Code, open the folder and pick .venv/bin/python as the interpreter or notebook kernel. VS Code offers to install ipykernel the first time you run a notebook cell.

docs.title: Run a forecast from a script
docs.text:
Save this as my_forecast.py in the BDBVHubRenewal folder. It forecasts with the random walk nowcast from one release, scores the forecast against later releases and saves a table and a figure. Getting started walks through the same steps, and the API reference documents each function.

import dataclasses
from pathlib import Path

from bdbvhubrenewal.data import (
    delays_for_vintage,
    load_daily,
    load_delays,
    load_target,
)
from bdbvhubrenewal.evaluation import backtest as bt
from bdbvhubrenewal.evaluation.nowcast import relative_wis, release_backtest
from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters import NATIONAL
from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.chain import Settings
from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.randomwalk import RandomWalk, RandomWalkNowcast
from bdbvhubrenewal.reporting.plots import plot_location_grid

# Settings to change.
ORIGIN = "2026-10-17"  # the release to forecast from
N_SAMPLES = 200  # sample trajectories per location
WALK_WEEKS = 6  # weeks of data that set the random walk's spread
OUT = Path("output/my-forecast")

target, daily, delays = load_target(), load_daily(), load_delays()
real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]

config = dataclasses.replace(
    bt.load_config("config/backtest.toml"), min_horizon=-6, n_samples=N_SAMPLES
)
task = bt.make_tasks(
    real.loc[real["vintage"] == ORIGIN],
    delays_for_vintage(delays, ORIGIN)[0],
    config,
    history=real,
    daily=daily,
)[0]

models = [
    RandomWalk(),
    RandomWalkNowcast(settings=Settings(walk_weeks=WALK_WEEKS)),
]
forecasts = bt.run_forecasts(models, [task])
scores = release_backtest(
    [task], daily, target, models=(), stored=forecasts
).scores

OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
forecasts.to_csv(OUT / "forecasts.csv", index=False)
table = relative_wis(scores.loc[scores["target"] == "reported"])
table.to_csv(OUT / "relative-wis.csv", index=False)
fig = plot_location_grid(forecasts, real, [NATIONAL, "CD-IT"])
fig.savefig(OUT / "forecast.png", dpi=150)
print(table)

Run it.

uv run python my_forecast.py

To change a setting, edit it at the top of the script and run it again. ORIGIN takes any release date in real["vintage"]. get_model("randomwalknowcast") builds the same model with its default settings, and bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.list_models() lists every model. The renewal models fit with a sampler and take minutes per task (see Renewal models).

docs.title: Where outputs land
docs.text:
Output Folder The script above output/my-forecast/ uv run bdbvhubrenewal backtest forecasts and scores in results/ uv run bdbvhubrenewal nowcast the hub file in output/submission/ uv run bdbvhubrenewal report the docs figures and tables in docs/figures/ and docs/generated/

output/ is not committed, so anything there is yours to delete.

docs.title: Adding a model
docs.text:
Adding a model to the registry, so every evaluation includes it.

A model is a class with a name and a forecast(task) method. task is a ForecastTask: the target rows and delay data of one vintage, the provinces and weeks to forecast, the number of samples and a seed. forecast returns one row per location, week and sample, with columns location, target_end_date, sample and value.

from dataclasses import dataclass

import pandas as pd

from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters import ForecastTask, register_model


@dataclass
class MyModel:
    name: str = "my_model"

    def forecast(self, task: ForecastTask) -> pd.DataFrame: ...


register_model("my_model", MyModel, "One line describing it.")

Import the module in bdbvhubrenewal/forecasters/__init__.py. The backtest, the Backtest and Nowcast pages, compare-hub and nowcast --model my_model then include it. The backtest adds the national total, the horizons and the vintage kind.

For the leave-one-province-out check, set supports_mask = True and drop the provinces in task.mask from the likelihood while still forecasting them.

docs.title: Renewal variants
docs.text:
A new renewal variant is one entry in VARIANTS in forecasters.renewal. It names a base ModelConfig and the fields it changes. Fitted variants are not run by the docs build or the smoke tests. The fit store fits them once a variant is on main.

A run with --models replaces only those models' rows, and BDBV_RENEWAL_SAMPLER sets the NUTS settings.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
The bdbvhubrenewal command.

Paths to the tidy data default to $BDBV_DATA_DIR or data/. bdbvhubrenewal <command> --help lists each command's options.

Command What it does data Download the hub data and write the tidy tables to data/. backtest Run the development backtest, the evaluation on the real releases (results/nowcast-*.csv) and the recovery check. Fitted models are never run: their rows in results/ come from the fit store and are kept. With --models, only those models run and the others' rows are kept. backtest --evaluate-holdout Score every held-out vintage under the model chosen at the time, with the other models alongside. backtest --lopo Leave one province out: forecast each province with its counts masked, for the variants that take a mask. backtest --scenarios-only Run only the scenarios calibrated to the real data, from --scenario-as-of and --scenario-dates. bvd Cache the BVDOutbreakSize releases each vintage may use. compare-hub [--fetch] Score our retrospective forecasts and the hub's submitted ones on the same truth and weeks. nowcast Forecast from a real vintage, write the hub file and check it. With --config and --fit, forecast from a fit configuration. zone-backtest Score randomwalk, randomwalknowcast and pprandomwalknowcast run at zone level on the real vintages. fit-store plan, fit, load List the fits the fit store lacks, make one, or load the stored fits into results/. fit Fit a configuration and write the fit directory and its diagnostics, for the submission CI. plot-submission Plot a submitted hub file. plot-ppc Plot a fit's posterior predictive checks (ppc.json). coherence Compare the national data with the sum of the provinces. validate Run the hub's checks on files. metadata Write and check a model's metadata YAML. hub-id Print the hub model id that submissions use. freeze-round Write a round's docs page to the ledger once its pull request has merged. report Make the docs figures and tables.

--version prints the package version.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text:
task backtest           # development backtest, real releases and recovery check
task backtest-lopo      # leave one province out
task backtest-scenarios # simulated scenarios calibrated to the real data
task backtest-zones     # random walk models at health-zone level
task backtest-heldout   # score the held-out vintages
task results            # every derived file in results/, as the Pages build makes them
task docs               # build the site into _site/ (runs task results, about 25 min)
task serve              # serve the site (run task results once first)

--models runs some models and keeps the others' rows in results/. The files in results/ are not committed, apart from development-log.csv, ladder.csv and model-choice.yml. The Pages build makes the rest with the steps of task results, from the code, the data and the fit store.

docs.title: Fit store
docs.text:
Each forecast of a fitted model is a fit, so the backtest and the docs build never run them. The Fit store workflow (.github/workflows/fit-store.yml) fits each fitted model once at each real origin and commits the result to the fit-store branch, as <model>/<origin>/<key>.json.gz. The key hashes the model and forecaster code, config/backtest.toml, uv.lock, the model's sampler table in ci/policy.toml and the releases up to the origin. The renewal variants use the sampler of the submission candidate that runs them; pprandomwalknowcast uses its own. A code or sampler change refits every origin, and a new hub release adds one fit per model. The workflow runs on pushes to main that change these inputs, and every 6 hours for new hub releases. A push cancels a running refit, and fits already stored are kept. A fit that fails is stored as failed and is not retried until its inputs change. On a pull request it only lists the fits the change would need. When it stores fits it rebuilds the docs.

task fit-store-plan  # the fits the store lacks for this code and data
task fit-store       # load the stored fits into results/

task backtest loads the store first. Where the store has no fit for the current key, load uses the newest stored fit of that model and origin. Each page with fitted-model results says which commits its fits come from, and which fits for the current code are still running. A full refit is 20 fits (4 models at 5 origins), run in parallel: about 50 minutes of wall time and 8 runner-hours. A new release adds 4 fits, about 2 runner-hours.

The comparison with hub forecasts downloads other teams' files, so it is run on its own:

uv run bdbvhubrenewal compare-hub --fetch

docs.title: Hub files
docs.text:
bdbvhubrenewal nowcast writes model-output/<model_id>/<reference_date>-<model_id>.csv under output/submission/. The model id is seabbs- plus the model's model_abbr in config/hub.toml. When the reference date is an open round in tasks.json, it checks the file with submission.validate, the Python port of the hub's checks:

  • column names and order free, no extra columns;
  • one reference date, listed in tasks.json;
  • known locations, the one target and sample output only;
  • target weeks listed in tasks.json;
  • exactly 100 samples per location, and every sample covers the same weeks;
  • integer sample ids, finite non-negative values, no duplicate rows.

It skips the submission window and the model metadata, which bdbvhubrenewal metadata checks. For any other reference date it prints a note and skips the checks.

task validate-hub then runs the hub's own hubValidations::validate_submission() in R against a fresh clone of the hub.

bdbvhubrenewal metadata writes hub/model-metadata/<model id>.yml and checks it against the hub's schema.

Sample ids

Sample ids run from 1 to 100 and are shared across locations, so hubValidations reads samples as joint across locations.

The CLI reference documents main and build_parser.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Setting up, checking and documenting changes to the package.

Task What it does task setup Install the package with the dev and docs groups. task test Run the tests with coverage. task test-slow Run the parameter recovery fit. task lint Lint with ruff, check formatting and type-check with mypy. task format Format and fix lint where safe. task docs Build the docs strictly into _site/. task ci-test Lint, type-check and test the submission CI scripts in ci/.

Pre-commit hooks run the same checks on each commit. The docs build, not pytest coverage, runs the reporting code end to end. New behaviour comes with a test, and docs follow UK English with one sentence per line. The docs read generated tables, so build them with task docs, not mkdocs build. New models are added as on Adding a model.

docs.title: Baseline models
docs.text:
randomwalknowcast, its partially pooled variant pprandomwalknowcast, and randomwalk, their comparison model.

The data and notation are on the Data methods page. The renewal models are on the Renewal models page. randomwalknowcast is baselinenowcast12 with a random walk on top. randomwalk is the same walk with no nowcast. Both run at province and zone level (Health zones), and national is the sum of the provinces.

docs.title: Daily release snapshots
docs.text:
Both models use the daily onsets of each hub release. \(N_{p,r}(t)\) is the known plus imputed onsets in province \(p\) on day \(t\) at release \(r\), which sum over a hub week to the weekly target. A forecast is made from the vintage of its date, whose latest release is \(o\). Release \(r\) has a cut-off \(c_r\), the cut-off the release states where it gives one and otherwise its latest onset day over all places. Day \(t \le c_r\) is observed at \(r\) and is \(a = c_r - t\) days old. Cells after the cut-off are not observed. Hub weeks run Sunday to Saturday and are labelled by the Saturday. \(Y_{p,r}(w)\) is the sum of \(N_{p,r}\) over the days of week \(w\). \(w\) is \(k\) weeks back when it is \(k\) weeks before the week holding the release cut-off.

A pair of consecutive releases \((r, r + 1)\) has gap \(s = c_{r+1} - c_r\) days. \(D = 42\) days is baselinenowcast's max_delay, and a pair is in window when \(1 \le s \le D\). Only in-window pairs inform the delay. A pair outside the window keeps its counts in the data. A model raises if the vintage has no snapshots or no in-window pair.

docs.title: Delay
docs.text:
The delay follows baselinenowcast12 on the daily snapshots, with one extension. Releases are batched reports of one daily delay. With \(g_p(j) \ge 0\) the daily log development factor at age \(j\), and \(g_p(j) = 0\) for \(j \ge D\), a day of age \(x\) at release \(r\) grows to release \(r + 1\) by \(\exp \sum_{j=x}^{x+s-1} g_p(j)\). For each gap \(s\) and age \(x = 0, \dots, D - 1\),

\[ \log \frac{\sum N_{p,r+1}(t)}{\sum N_{p,r}(t)} = \sum_{j=x}^{x+s-1} g_p(j), \]

summed over the in-window pairs of gap \(s\) and over days \(t\) of age \(x\) at \(r\) that both releases observe. \(g_p\) is the non-negative least squares fit of all these equations, each weighted by its denominator \(\sum N_{p,r}(t)\), with no smoothing over age. With a gap of 1 only, \(\exp g_p(x)\) is baselinenowcast's chain ladder factor. Cells a release does not observe are skipped, not filled, and a gap and age with a zero denominator give no equation. The parent of a province is the country, whose counts are the sum of its provinces. Only onset days less than \(1.5 D = 63\) days before the cut-off of the latest release used contribute to the sums, as baselinenowcast's default n_history_delay, and a retrospective fit uses the cut-off of its own release. Before the sums, each day's increments between its releases go through baselinenowcast's preprocess_negative_values, so a downward revision is set to zero and taken from the earlier increments of that day and no ratio falls below 1. This applies to the delay only, because the removals below still allow negative revisions. The preprocessing runs along releases for each onset day, where baselinenowcast runs it along the delay columns of a reporting triangle.

The growth of a day's count from age \(a\) to final is

\[ G_p(a) = \exp \sum_{j=a}^{D-1} g_p(j), \qquad G_p(a) = 1 \text{ for } a \ge D, \]

and \(1 / G_p(a)\) is the share of it reported. There is no growth past \(D\), so an equation whose ages run past \(D\) puts that growth on its ages below \(D\).

docs.title: Nowcast
docs.text:
Each hub week is a reference time of a weekly reporting triangle, with a column every 7 days after \(c_o\) and a last one at \(c_o + D\), where \(F = 1\). The share of week \(w\) reported by column \(j\) is

\[ F_{p,j}(w) = \frac{1}{n_w} \sum_{t \in w,\ t \le c_o} \frac{1}{G_p(c_o - t + 7j)}, \]

with \(n_w\) the days of \(w\) observed at \(o\). baselinenowcast's apply_delay fills the row from \(x_0 = Y_{p,o}(w)\), adding at each column

\[ x_j = x_{j-1} + \frac{x_{j-1} + 1 - F_{p,j-1}(w)}{F_{p,j-1}(w)} \big(F_{p,j}(w) - F_{p,j-1}(w)\big), \]

and the last column is the nowcast mean \(\mu_p(w)\). The \(+1\) is baselinenowcast's. It gives a week with 0 reported the mean \(1 / F_{p,0}(w) - 1 - \sum_{j \ge 1} (F_{p,j}(w) - F_{p,j-1}(w)) / F_{p,j}(w)\), about 2 to 3 cases at \(F_{p,0}(w) = 0.22\), and it adds less to a week the more complete it is. With \(\text{rem} = \mu_p(w) - Y_{p,o}(w) \ge 0\) the count still to come, the final count is new reports minus removals, as in epinowcast,

\[ X_{p,i}(w) = \max\big\{0,\ Y_{p,o}(w) + A - B\big\}, \qquad A \sim \text{NB}\big(\text{rem},\ \phi_{p,k}\big), \qquad B \sim \text{Poisson}\big(b_{p,k}\, Y_{p,o}(w)\big). \]

\(A\) is baselinenowcast's negative binomial on the remaining count, with mean \(\text{rem}\) and size \(\phi_{p,k}\). \(B\) removes a share \(b_{p,k}\) of the count reported, so counts can be revised down. Before the floor the mean is \(\mu_p(w) - b_{p,k} Y_{p,o}(w)\). Weeks with no day younger than \(D\) at \(o\) have \(\text{rem} = 0\) and \(b_{p,k} = 0\), so they keep their reported count. Sample \(i\) is one draw of \(X_{p,i}(w)\) per week.

Fit. For each earlier release \(r < o\) with an in-window pair among the releases up to \(r\), a nowcast \(\hat y_p(w)\) is made from the data up to \(r\), with the delay of \(r\). It is the same weekly fill from \(c_r\), with the \(g_p\) of \(r\) and the shares taken relative to the count at \(c_o\), so its last column is at \(c_o\). For weeks back \(k\) with a day younger than \(D\) at \(r\), and where \(Y_{p,r}(w) > 0\) or \(\hat y_p(w) > 0\), the count of \(w\) on days up to \(c_r\) is compared between releases \(r\) and \(o\). A rise is the new reports \(A_{p,r}(w)\) and a fall the removals \(B_{p,r}(w)\), so both are weekly, as the forecast is. With \(\widehat{\text{rem}} = \hat y_p(w) - Y_{p,r}(w)\),

\[ \phi_{p,k} = \arg\max_\phi \sum \log \text{NB}\big(A_{p,r}(w);\ \widehat{\text{rem}},\ \phi\big), \qquad b_{p,k} = \frac{\sum B_{p,r}(w)}{\sum Y_{p,r}(w)}, \]

summed over the kept releases. \(\phi_{p,k}\) is fitted by maximum likelihood on \([0.1, 1000]\), one size per \(k\), as baselinenowcast does. A week with \(\widehat{\text{rem}} = 0\) says nothing about \(\phi\), so it is left out of that fit. The weeks in the fit of \(\phi_{p,k}\) are the errors at \(k\). \(b_{p,k}\) is the Poisson maximum likelihood estimate of the removals. Where the estimate chosen by the pooling rule has fewer than 3 errors at \(k\), \(\phi_{p,k} = 1000\), the Poisson end of the range.

docs.title: Own or pooled estimates
docs.text: The delay \(g_p(x)\) is own or parent by age. A place uses its own \(g_p(x)\) when its denominator \(\sum N_{p,r}(t)\) at age \(x\), summed over the pairs, is at least 10 cases. Otherwise it uses its parent's at that age (zone, province, country). The country uses its own. The size \(\phi_{p,k}\) and the spread of the walk \(\sigma_p\) use one rule with a threshold of 10 cases a week and 3 errors. The removal rate \(b_{p,k}\) is each place's own, so a place with no falls has none. \(\ell_p\) is the mean of \(Y_{p,o}(w)\) over weeks 3 to 6 back, in cases a week. A place with \(\ell_p \ge 10\) uses its own estimate. For \(\phi_{p,k}\) it also needs at least 3 errors at \(k\). Otherwise it uses the pooled estimate of its nearest parent that meets the same rule, and otherwise the country's. Only that last fallback can have fewer than 3 errors at \(k\). A pooled estimate uses the errors and weekly changes of the place's children with \(\ell \ge 10\) together. A place's counts are the sum of its children's, so the place itself is pooled only when none of its children has \(\ell \ge 10\).

docs.title: Walk
docs.text:
randomwalk and randomwalknowcast run the same walk from a start week \(w_0\) with start value \(x_i\) in sample \(i\). For \(h \ge 1\),

\[ \log\{1 + \lambda_i(w_0 + h)\} = \max\Big(0,\ \log\{1 + x_i\} + \sum_{j=1}^{h} \epsilon_{i,j}\Big), \qquad \epsilon_{i,j} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_p^2), \] \[ \tilde y_i(w_0 + h) \sim \text{Poisson}\big(\lambda_i(w_0 + h)\big). \]

Steps are summed within a sample, so each sample is one trajectory.

A place with no case reported in the 9 weeks up to the cut-off week is silent. A silent place is 0 until its first introduction, which comes in each week with probability \(q_p\). In both models this holds from the week after the start week of randomwalk, so randomwalknowcast does not nowcast a silent place's recent weeks. A silent place's walk has spread 0, so from its introduction its rate stays at 1 case a week. The introduction week has at least 1 case. \(q_p\) is the share of weeks with a case among the weeks that follow 9 weeks with none, over the place and its siblings (the zones of its province, or the provinces of the country), in weeks up to the start week of randomwalk. It is estimated at each origin from the counts reported then. National is the sum of the provinces, sample by sample.

\(\sigma_p\) is the sample standard deviation of the weekly changes of \(\log\{1 + Y_{p,o}(w)\}\) over the 9 weeks ending at the start week of randomwalk, so up to 8 changes. With fewer than 2 changes it is 0. Both models use reported counts for \(\sigma_p\).

docs.title: Random walk
docs.text:
randomwalk makes no nowcast. Its start week \(w_0\) is the latest week with

\[ \pi_p(w) = \frac{1}{7} \sum_{t \in w,\ t \le c_o} \frac{1}{G_p(c_o - t)} \ge 0.95, \]

the estimated share of the week's final count reported, under the delay above. If any place has no week with \(\pi_p(w) \ge 0.95\), randomwalk raises (NoCompleteWeek) and gives no forecast for the vintage, with nothing in its place. \(x_i = Y_{p,o}(w_0)\) for every sample. Weeks up to \(w_0\) are the reported counts. Later weeks with data are walk draws, floored at the reported count.

docs.title: Random walk on a nowcast
docs.text: randomwalknowcast starts each sample from its own nowcast \(X_{p,i}\) of the latest week with all 7 days on or before \(c_o\), so \(x_i = X_{p,i}(w_0)\). Weeks up to \(w_0\) are the nowcast draws. If the week after \(w_0\) holds \(c_o\) and is partial, \(n\) days of it have no data. Its value is its nowcast draw plus Poisson\((n \lambda_i / 7)\), with \(\lambda_i\) the walk rate of that week. Later weeks are walk draws.

docs.title: Health zones
docs.text:
randomwalk and randomwalknowcast run on each zone's own release snapshots with the same code as for provinces. The hierarchy is zone, province, country, and each zone takes its delay, size and walk spread by the rules above. Zone samples sum to their province's samples, sample by sample and week by week. Province sample \(Y^{(k)}(w)\) is apportioned over the zones in proportion to the zone model's own sample \(x^{(k)}_z(w)\) of the same id and week:

\[ y^{(k)}_z(w) \approx Y^{(k)}(w)\, \frac{x^{(k)}_z(w)}{\sum_{z'} x^{(k)}_{z'}(w)}. \]

Largest remainders make the values whole numbers that sum to \(Y^{(k)}(w)\). Where every \(x^{(k)}_z(w)\) is 0 the split uses the Dirichlet mean shares of the Renewal models page.

docs.title: Partially pooled variant
docs.text:
pprandomwalknowcast is randomwalknowcast with the delay \(g_p\), the walk spread \(\sigma_p\), the size \(\phi_{p,k}\) and the removal rate \(b_{p,k}\) partially pooled over zones, provinces and the country, in place of the own-or-pooled rule. The nowcast draws, the walk and the zone reconciliation are the same. Each is fitted in numpyro with NUTS (2 chains of 500 warm-up and 500 draws, target acceptance 0.9).

Each parameter \(\theta\) of place \(p\) is its parent's plus an offset for the place's level,

\[ \theta_p = \theta_{\mathrm{pa}(p)} + \tau_{\ell(p)}\, z_p, \qquad z_p \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1), \qquad \tau_\ell \sim \mathcal{N}^+(0, 0.5^2), \]

with \(\ell(p)\) the level of \(p\) (province or zone) and one \(\tau_\ell\) for each level and parameter. \(\theta\) is \(\log g_p(j)\) for each age \(j\), \(\log \sigma_p\), and \(\log \phi_{p,k}\) and \(\log b_{p,k}\) for each week back \(k\). The country's values have priors \(\mathcal{N}(-3, 2^2)\), \(\mathcal{N}(\log 0.2, 1)\), \(\mathcal{N}(0, 1.5^2)\) and \(\mathcal{N}(\log 0.005, 1.5^2)\). A place's counts are the sum of its children's, so for the walk spread and the nowcast uncertainty only the places forecast (the provinces, or the zones at zone level) enter the likelihood, and their parents are latent centres.

  • Delay. For each gap \(s\) and age \(x\) with \(\sum N_{p,r}(t) > 0\), the increment is Poisson,

$$ \sum N_{p,r+1}(t) - \sum N_{p,r}(t) \sim \text{Poisson}\Big(\sum N_{p,r}(t)\, \big(e^{\sum_{j=x}^{x+s-1} g_p(j)} - 1\big)\Big), $$

with the sums, window and preprocessing of the delay. With one place and a gap of 1 its maximum likelihood estimate is baselinenowcast's chain ladder factor. A place's increments at age \(x\) enter only where its denominator there, summed over the pairs, is at least 10 cases, the threshold of the own-or-pooled rule, and the country's always do. Below it a day often has no cases at one release and some at the next, which a factor cannot give, so the few days with cases would give too fast a delay. Those ages take their parent's value through the pooling. The rule and threshold are those randomwalknowcast uses to choose between a place's own factor and its parent's, applied here to which increments enter the likelihood. A parent's increments are its children's summed, so a case at an age where both fit their own enters the likelihood once for each level. It is fitted at the origin and at each earlier release that gives errors. - Walk spread. The weekly changes of \(\log\{1 + Y_{p,o}(w)\}\) over the walk window are \(\mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_p^2)\). A change between two weeks with no cases sits at the walk's floor, so it is left out. - Nowcast uncertainty. The new reports \(A_{p,r}(w)\) are \(\text{NB}(\widehat{\text{rem}}, \phi_{p,k})\) and the removals \(B_{p,r}(w)\) are \(\text{Poisson}(b_{p,k} Y_{p,r}(w))\), on the errors of the fit, made with the pooled delay of each earlier release.

The posterior medians of \(g_p\), \(\sigma_p\), \(\phi_{p,k}\) (kept in \([0.1, 1000]\)) and \(b_{p,k}\) replace the estimates of randomwalknowcast. So the forecasts carry the pooled point estimates, not their posterior spread. It is scored on the real releases at province and zone level, but not on the simulated recovery check, whose 15 vintages of 45 to 101 releases each would take about 1000 NUTS fits.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
While the release history in the delay window is shorter than \(D\), no chain to the final count can be checked against a final count. Each delay factor rests on one onset day per age per pair, and the youngest ages rest on few cases even nationally. The onset clock assumes a constant lag from the latest onset day to extraction, but the lag varies between releases. The chain ladder treats reporting speed as fixed by age and step, but speed and backlogs vary between releases. The observation model is learnt from the earlier releases, which may be few. Counts include the hub's imputed onsets, which are re-drawn as cases gain onsets, so changes between releases mix reporting with imputation. Places are sampled independently, so a shock to a whole release is not shared, and the national band is a sum of independent provincial bands. The walk has no drift, and its spread comes from 8 weekly changes, which for small places include Poisson noise. pprandomwalknowcast plugs in posterior medians, so the uncertainty in its pooled estimates does not widen its forecasts.

  1. Johnson KE, Tang M, Tyszka E, Nemcova B, Wolffram D, Ergas R, Reich NG, Funk S, Mellor J, Bracher J, Abbott S (2025). Baseline nowcasting methods for handling delays in epidemiological data. Wellcome Open Research. doi:10.12688/wellcomeopenres.25027.2. ↩↩

  2. Johnson KE, Tyszka E, Bracher J, Funk S, Abbott S (2025). baselinenowcast: Methods for baseline nowcasting right-truncated epidemiological data. https://github.com/epinowcast/baselinenowcast/. ↩↩

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Extraction of the hub data, its vintages, and the synthetic vintages used in testing.

What the data show is on the Data results page.

docs.title: Target and notation
docs.text: The target is \(y_{p}(w)\), the final count of confirmed cases in province \(p\) with symptom onset in epi week \(w\) (Sunday to Saturday, labelled by its Saturday). It includes onsets the hub imputes for cases reported without one. A vintage \(v\) is the data published on date \(T_v\). It gives, for each \(p\) and \(w\), known onsets \(K_{p,v}(w)\), imputed onsets \(I_{p,v}(w)\) and their total \(Y_{p,v}(w) = K_{p,v}(w) + I_{p,v}(w)\). A forecast made from vintage \(v\) serves the round with reference date \(r_v\), the first Saturday whose submission window (Sunday to Tuesday, Kinshasa time) closes on or after \(T_v\). Horizon \(h\) is the number of weeks from \(r_v\) to \(w\). Backtest forecasts cover \(h = -4, \dots, 3\).

docs.title: Extraction
docs.text:
Hub file What it holds Vintages target-data/time-series.csv Weekly confirmed cases by onset week, by province and nationally. Also health zone totals. All, in one file auxiliary-data/daily-confirmed-case.csv Daily cases by onset day, observed and imputed, nationally and by province and health zone. The observed and imputed split of the weekly target comes from here. All, in one file auxiliary-data/weekly-reporting-delays-by-province.csv One row per known-onset case: province, onset week and onset-to-report delay. Latest only; earlier ones from the archive folder and git history auxiliary-data/locations.csv Location codes, names, types and parents. Static auxiliary-data/health-zone-code-mapping.csv Health zone codes mapped to P-codes and DHIS2 codes. Static hub-config/*.json Rounds, tasks, output types, hub settings and the metadata schema. Copied at download

The hub does not publish deaths, suspected cases, counts by report date or populations. Province populations are the Institut National de la Statistique's 2019 figures (Annuaire statistique RDC 2020), and province centres the WorldPop-weighted centres of BVDOutbreakSize.

docs.title: Vintages
docs.text: Each hub release is a vintage, labelled by its as_of date and of kind real or simulated. From the 2026-11-01 release on, as_of is the extraction date, a day after the last reported case, while earlier releases were labelled by the last reported case (hub issue 90). We keep each release's published label, map a rewritten label back to it, and take its last report day as the extraction date less a day. Recent weeks are revised in later releases, so each forecast is made from one vintage and scored on the counts later releases report.

docs.title: Release snapshots
docs.text: auxiliary-data/daily-confirmed-case.csv holds, for each release, the daily onsets known at that release. The count of a day is its known plus imputed onsets, and the counts of a week sum to the hub's weekly target. A release has an as_of date and a data cut-off, its latest onset day over all places, or the cut-off a simulated release states. A release observes the days up to its cut-off, and a day in range with no row counts 0. The age of day \(t\) at release \(r\) is the cut-off minus \(t\), the onset clock. Counts of a day are compared across releases on this clock. A release and the next release give one pair of releases. Its step is the difference of the two cut-offs in days.

docs.title: Delay and missingness data
docs.text: The hub imputes an onset for each case reported without one by subtracting a delay drawn from the pooled published delays (hub issue 61). So the share of cases without an onset is measured at every vintage.

docs.title: Simulated vintages
docs.text:
Simulated vintages come from the model's own renewal with known parameters. The default scenario uses:

  • expected onsets from the model's renewal and generation interval, with a national Rt that turns from 1.6 to 0.85 around day 120, fixed province offsets, gravity-kernel importation (\(\varepsilon = 0.01\)) and susceptible depletion;
  • Poisson confirmed cases, with ascertainment rising from 0.5 to 0.75;
  • a missing-onset share by report day rising from 5% to 25% and falling to 12%;
  • a double censored Gamma delay whose mean falls from 12 to 6 days;
  • a lag from report to publication, 85% uniform on 0 to 3 days and 15% uniform on 4 to 60 days, as late entries in the real delay files;
  • 30% of cases reported with no onset get one 7 to 42 days after publication, so imputed counts of past weeks fall and known counts rise, as between real vintages.

Vintages are published as the hub does, with missing onsets imputed from the known delays reported so far. Daily releases are published on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays. Their weekly sums are the weekly target. Each is cut off by the lag of the latest real release on that weekday, or the median lag of the real releases where none fell on that weekday. The truth is every confirmed case by its true onset week.

The calibrated scenarios copy one real vintage. Each province's expected onsets follow its real weekly totals, spread over the days and smoothed over 7 days, up to 4 weeks before the vintage. Rt is the ratio of onsets to the force of infection, capped at 3, and onsets above what it explains are seeds. From 4 weeks before the vintage, Rt is the mean of its last 3 weeks times 0.75, 1 or 1.25 (falling, flat or rising), for 10 weeks past the vintage. Ascertainment is 1, there is no importation and the whole population is at risk. The delay is the real delay by onset week, completed for right truncation from weeks with full follow-up. The missing-onset share is the real national imputed share by onset week, \((I + 1)/(Y + 2)\), averaged over 5 weeks and moved later by the mean delay. Zones take the real share of each province's cases. Late entries and onset backfill are as in the default, and 2% of cases are removed 7 to 42 days after publication. Their truth is the last simulated vintage.

docs.title: BVDOutbreakSize estimates
docs.text: renewalbvd uses the Rt estimates in the public results-<run> releases of BVDOutbreakSize (MIT licence, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20312758). These are the national \(R_T\) draws, the patch summaries from 23 October with the national \(R_T\) row they are relative to, and the release's data cut-off. Early releases give only the growth rate \(r\), which is turned into \(R_T = (1 + r\theta)^k\) with BVDOutbreakSize's Gamma generation interval (mean 15.3 days, SD 9.3 days, shape \(k\), scale \(\theta\)). Each forecast uses the newest release whose files were all last updated by the forecast's cut-off, whose data end by the forecast date and whose fit converged. The cut-off is the end of the Sunday that opens the round's submission window, Kinshasa time, or the end of the vintage date if that is later. The joint fit's worst R-hat must be at most 1.1 ([bvd] max_rhat in config/backtest.toml), and effective sample sizes are ignored. The R-hat is read from the fit diagnostics table in the release's rendered site (site.zip), and a release without a readable table is passed over for the next older one. Each fit records the release it used, its R-hat and why newer releases were skipped. Their use is on the Renewal models page.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text: Scoring, and the evaluations.

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text: Every model is scored on the count each later real release reports, with its final-count forecast turned into a forecast of that count (Real releases). The release scores never compare a final count with a count still being reported. Complete weeks of the latest release are a secondary check (Real releases). Simulated forecasts are scored against the simulated final counts.

docs.title: Scores
docs.text:
Scores follow scoringutils and BVDOutbreakSize. With sample quantiles \(q_\tau\) at 23 levels, \(\tau \in \{0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.10, \dots, 0.95, 0.975, 0.99\}\),

\[ \text{WIS}(F, y) = \frac{1}{K + 1/2} \sum_{\tau} \left(\mathbb{1}\{y < q_\tau\} - \tau\right)\left(q_\tau - y\right), \qquad K = 11. \]

It splits into dispersion, overprediction and underprediction. WIS on the log scale is the WIS of the transformed target, \(\text{WIS}(\log(1 + x), \log(1 + y))\), never the log of WIS. WIS on the natural scale is dominated by the places with the most cases. On the log scale it approximates a score of the relative error, close to a score of the growth rate, so every place counts on a similar footing1.

\[ \text{Bias} = 1 - \big(P(X \le y) + P(X \le y - 1)\big), \qquad \text{rWIS}_m = \frac{\overline{\text{WIS}}_m}{\overline{\text{WIS}}_b}. \]

Positive bias is overprediction. Relative WIS is a ratio of means against a baseline \(b\) over the forecasts both made, and below 1 beats it. Relative WIS on the log scale is the same ratio of mean WIS on the log scale. The baseline is randomwalk. Coverage is whether \(y\) falls in the central 50% and 90% sample intervals.

docs.title: Energy score
docs.text:
The energy score scores one forecast of a vector \(\mathbf{y}\). For an origin, a release and a scale, \(\mathbf{y}\) holds every place at that scale in every scored week, and national holds the weeks only. It uses only the place-week cells that every compared model forecasts. Sample \(i\) of a model is its draws with sample index \(i\), \(\mathbf{X}_i\). We use the fair form over \(m\) samples,

\[ \text{ES}(F, \mathbf{y}) = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{i} \lVert \mathbf{X}_i - \mathbf{y} \rVert - \frac{1}{2m(m - 1)} \sum_{i \ne j} \lVert \mathbf{X}_i - \mathbf{X}_j \rVert. \]

The energy score on the log scale is the energy score of \(\log(1 + \mathbf{y})\) against \(\log(1 + \mathbf{X}_i)\), never the log of the score. Relative energy scores are ratios of means against randomwalk over the origins and releases both have, and \(n\) counts those. The score rewards a joint pattern across places only where draws are joint. renewal and renewalbvd draws are joint across provinces, one posterior draw per sample index. renewalsp fits each province on its own, so its draws are independent across provinces. Zones split each province draw, so zones are joint within a province for every renewal model. randomwalk and randomwalknowcast draw each place independently. Hub teams' samples are joint across weeks within a place only, as the hub's sample format sets, so pairing their indices across places scores them as independent across places.

docs.title: Backtest design
docs.text:
Each vintage is a forecast task, and every registered model forecasts every task.

Run Vintages Truth Development backtest Real up to the latest model choice date, except the latest real vintage As for real releases Recovery check Simulated Simulated final counts Simulated scenarios The four weekly simulated vintages up to the latest real vintage, from outbreaks calibrated to it with Rt after the data scaled by 0.75, 1 or 1.25 Complete weeks of the simulated final counts, and the counts as reported two weeks after each vintage Rolling held-out evaluation Real vintages after each model choice As for real releases Real releases Every real release up to the latest model choice date with a later release The count each later release shows, and the latest release's count for its complete weeks Comparison with hub forecasts Real where one serves the round As for real releases

docs.title: Real releases
docs.text:
Each real release up to the latest model choice date with a later release is an origin. The random walk models forecast from the releases up to the origin only. The renewal models' stored forecasts from the origin are scored with them. So are hub teams' forecasts for a round, at the latest release serving it. An origin with no pair of releases whose gap is within the delay window, \(D = 42\) days, has no delay factor and no forecast. It is listed with no forecasts and nothing replaces it. Two targets are scored.

Reported. The count each later release \(o'\) shows for every forecast week it reports. Every model forecasts the final count \(X\) of week \(w\). Day \(t\) is \(a = c - t\) days old at a cut-off \(c\), and the share of its final count reported then is \(\pi(a) = 1 / G(a)\), with \(G(a)\) the growth from age \(a\) to \(D\) under the daily delay of the origin (Baseline models). Days after the cut-off have \(\pi = 0\), and a week's share \(\pi_w\) is the mean over its seven days. With \(R_o\) the count reported at the origin, the count outstanding there, \(X - R_o\), is thinned binomially, so each sample becomes a draw of the count reported at \(o'\),

\[ R_o + \text{Binomial}(X - R_o, q), \qquad q = \frac{\pi_w(c_{o'}) - \pi_w(c_o)}{1 - \pi_w(c_o)}, \]

with the sign carried when \(X < R_o\), and a week fully reported at the origin has \(q = 1\). Only the delay fitted at the origin is used. Its mean is the growth over the gap to \(o'\) for randomwalknowcast, and the floor maps to itself.

Complete weeks. The count the latest release shows for the weeks it reports in full. A week is complete when it is at least 4 weeks back from the week holding the latest release's cut-off and grew by less than 2% since the release before.

The floor is the count reported at the origin, scored on both targets as a forecast with no spread. Scores are WIS, 50% and 90% coverage and bias, by model, origin, weeks back from the origin's week and place. Relative WIS is against randomwalk on the forecasts both made, for national and the provinces pooled, over all origins and by origin, and by origin and place. Every table counts its forecasts, \(n\), so a model with fewer forecasts was scored on fewer weeks or places. The run stops if an origin has no release snapshots or two models run here give identical samples.

docs.title: Reading the figures
docs.text: Fans show 100 sample trajectories, the 50% and 90% bands and the median. In point-and-line figures, points are medians, thick lines 50% intervals and thin lines 90% intervals. The data at the origin are dashed, shown when the origin is not the latest vintage, and the data as later reported are solid. The dotted vertical line is the reference date. Weeks still being reported are shaded, with hollow points. The vertical axis of a fan ends at the top of its 90% band. Horizon is weeks from the reference week, so negative horizons are nowcasts, 0 is the reference week and positive horizons are forecasts.

docs.title: Rolling held-out evaluation
docs.text: Each model choice is logged with its date, and the development set rolls forward with them. Development runs use every vintage up to the latest choice date. Each real vintage after a choice is forecast by the model chosen then, the latest choice dated before it. It is also forecast by randomwalk and randomwalknowcast, and by every fitted model from its stored fit. The run supplies the fitted models' forecasts to the Nowcast and Comparison pages, and has no page of its own.

docs.title: Leave-one-province-out
docs.text: One province's likelihood is masked while it stays in the model, so coupling still acts on it. Its onsets are scored on every week against the latest real vintage. It runs on development vintages for the models that support the mask, renewal and renewalbvd.

docs.title: Health zones
docs.text: randomwalk and randomwalknowcast run on each zone's own release snapshots, for every zone with cases at the vintage. Zones use the same models as provinces. A week with no onsets in a zone has a count of 0. Each zone takes its delay and spreads by the rules of the Baseline models page. Each model's zone samples are made to sum to its province samples, as in the submitted file, and are scored in that form. Each real vintage before the latest is forecast, and origins with no pair of releases within the delay window are skipped, as for provinces. Zones are scored on the reported target as for real releases, with the zone delays fitted at the origin, so a zone count is never scored against a count still being reported. Relative WIS is against randomwalk in the same form. On the Nowcast page the fitted models' zone samples at the latest release are those of their stored fits, where they have one.

docs.title: Comparison with hub forecasts
docs.text:
For each hub reference date, our unfitted models forecast from the latest real vintage serving the round. Fitted models use their stored backtest or held-out forecasts for the same round. Where we submitted to a round, our submitted file is a series of its own beside these main-build forecasts. Every model is scored on the weeks it forecast as for real releases, from the vintage serving the round. WIS is relative to randomwalk on the weeks both forecast, on the comparison page. A round is pending until a later real release exists.

  1. Bosse NI, Abbott S, Cori A, van Leeuwen E, Bracher J, Funk S (2023). Scoring epidemiological forecasts on transformed scales. PLOS Computational Biology 19(8): e1011393. doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011393. ↩

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text: How the models are built in code, computed and sampled.

docs.title: Code
docs.text: The model extends PyRenew, pinned to a commit, and runs in JAX with NumPyro. Its code is in bdbvhubrenewal.model and the variants are in forecasters.renewal. The model is configured by ModelConfig. The model diagrams are mermaid blocks in docs/methods/model.md.

docs.title: PyRenew and what is built here
docs.text:
Component PyRenew piece Built here Pooled \(R_p(t)\) BaseSubpopulationInfections, WeeklyTemporalProcess NonCentredRandomWalk, for the frozen seeding weeks, the separate forecast steps and their reversion. Renewal with importation and depletion BaseSubpopulationInfections, subclassed coupled_renewal, called from _infections_from_rt, and Importation, which gives the mixing matrix as PyRenew's mobility_matrix_rv does. Ascertainment \(\alpha(s)\) IndependentAscertainment with a temporal process None. Onset-to-report delay \(f_s(d)\) None HazardDelay. Missing onsets \(\pi_p(t)\) None MissingOnsetFraction, a pooled walk of the same form as \(R_p\) with its own parameters. Known and imputed onsets BaseObservationProcess with temporal_pmf_rv for the infection-to-onset pmf (the incubation period, a CensoredPMF with a random mean and SD), NegativeBinomialNoise, compute_prop_already_reported for the publication lag OnsetStreams. Delays of known-onset cases None DirichletMultinomialNoise, a noise model in the form of PyRenew's CountNoise for counts by delay given weekly totals. BVDOutbreakSize Rt None RtPseudoObservation, a RandomVariable the latent process calls, as it holds both \(R\) and infections. Provinces with no cases None An importation-only component.

PyRenew pieces that give a different model, sample less well, or would only rename one line, are not used.

  • The RandomWalk temporal process puts the step SD in the step distribution, so it is centred in the SD.
  • ARProcess gives the same walk, log density and gradient, but NUTS needs more tree steps with it, so the walk samples its steps as one vectorised site.
  • AR1 draws its first state from the stationary distribution, and DifferencedAR1 is AR(1) on the differences. Here walks start at a fixed value and stay there over the seeding weeks.
  • SubpopulationInfections samples one deviation process per province and subtracts their mean, which leaves a direction the data do not identify. Here the \(P - 1\) coordinates on the sum-to-zero basis \(Q\) are sampled.
  • HierarchicalNormalPrior has no sum-to-zero constraint. On the basis coordinates it is the same prior, but it would replace one sample statement.
  • GammaGroupSdPrior gives each province its own SD with a floor, where here the provinces share one half-normal SD.
  • CountObservation and SubpopulationCounts take one fixed delay pmf and one truncation pmf. Here the delay varies with onset day, and known and imputed onsets are separate streams.
  • MobilitySubpopulationInfections uses a fixed mobility matrix, \(R\) by location and depletion capped at the susceptibles. Here a share of transmission is sent from each origin through a fixed gravity kernel, and depletion is exponential in the pool \(\nu\).

PyRenew has no delay that varies with time, no Dirichlet-multinomial count and no pseudo-observation of \(R\).

The table compares the two ways of sampling the walk steps on the recovery fit of the simulated outbreak, with 2 chains of 300 warm-up and 300 draws.
