docs.title: Baseline models
docs.text:
The baselines are in forecasters.randomwalk and forecasters.chain, on a JAX port of baselinenowcast 0.2.2 in bdbvhubrenewal.baselinenowcast. The port is checked against fixtures from the R package, and has one named extension, the chain ladder of release snapshots, which skips unobserved cells and fits one daily delay shared by pairs of any gap. The models use the port's chain ladder on snapshots. The observation model is in forecasters.obs, and fits and draws its new reports with the port's fit_by_horizon, fit_nb and sample_nb.

Part Where Snapshots as arrays [location, release, day] data.snapshots Pair sums, the daily delay fit and growth baselinenowcast.snapshots, pair sums jit with locations on the leading axis Own or pooled source of each estimate forecasters.pooling New reports minus removals forecasters.obs One random walk for both models forecasters.walk Backtest on real releases evaluation.nowcast

Shapes are fixed within an origin, so each new origin compiles once. Pandas only builds the inputs and the output frames.

docs.title: Numerics
docs.text:
The model runs in single precision (float32), JAX's default.

  • Depletion is carried on \(\log S\), which needs no subtraction, and \(1 - e^{-y}\) is computed with expm1.
  • The generation interval and the incubation period are double interval censored in closed form, \(G(d + 1) - 2G(d) + G(d - 1)\) with the integrated cdf (model.censored). The generation interval is computed once, in float64, and the incubation period in float32 at each draw of its mean and SD (CensoredPMF); both match primarycensored.
  • The simulator's delays use the same closed form, truncated at their maximum delay and renormalised as primarycensored's \(D\). In float32 they are within \(3 \times 10^{-5}\) of primarycensored, and within \(10^{-8}\) in float64.
  • The negative binomial concentration is capped at \(\phi \le 1000\), which is Poisson for these counts. The Dirichlet-multinomial concentration is capped at \(\psi \le 10^4\).
  • The hub imputation sums are products of banded \(7 \times 7k\) blocks for each onset week, so the cost grows with the number of weeks and not its square.

The tests check the renewal and the imputation against a NumPy reference, tests/model/numpy_reference.py.

docs.title: Sampling
docs.text:
PyRenew's PyrenewBuilder builds each model as a MultiSignalModel, and NumPyro's NUTS fits it. Chains run vectorised unless a fit's settings say otherwise. Backtest fits (config/backtest.toml) and CI submission fits (ci/policy.toml) both run their chains in parallel. Without other settings, NUTS runs 4 chains of 1000 warm-up and 1000 draws, with target acceptance 0.9 and maximum tree depth 10. Chains start from the median of 15 prior draws. Submission fits take their settings from ci/policy.toml, which override JSON settings in BDBV_RENEWAL_SAMPLER. Backtest and leave-one-province-out fits take theirs from config/backtest.toml when BDBV_RENEWAL_SAMPLER is unset. A per-location model has one fit per location with enough cases. Each fit reports its largest R-hat over parameters and the share of draws at the maximum tree depth.

The parameterisation is as follows.

  • Every walk, the pooled \(\log R(t)\) included, samples its steps non-centred, as standard normals scaled by the step SD.
  • Province deviations sum to zero through an orthonormal basis \(Q\) of the sum-to-zero subspace, so the \(P - 1\) free processes are unconstrained.
  • The starting offsets of the \(\log R\) deviations are sampled centred, and those of the missing-onset fraction non-centred.
  • Walk steps after the fit axis are not sampled by NUTS. They are drawn from the prior given each posterior draw when forecasting.

docs.title: Renewal models
docs.text:
The three renewal models, with the maths of each.

The data and notation are on the Data methods page. How the models are built in code and sampled is on the Implementation page.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
renewalsp fits a renewal model to each province on its own. renewal fits the provinces together, pools them and links them by importation. renewalbvd is renewal with a down-weighted likelihood term on the Rt of BVDOutbreakSize. seabbs-renewal submits the first of renewalbvd, renewalsp, renewal, randomwalknowcast and randomwalk, in that order, to pass its checks (Submission workflow). The sections below build up from renewalsp, and each gives only the maths it adds. Every time-varying part is a weekly random walk or AR(1), so it stays near constant unless the data show change.

flowchart TD
    SP["<b>renewalsp</b><br/>each province on its own<br/>Rt walk<br/>generation interval<br/>onsets and delay<br/>missing onsets<br/>three data streams"]
    RN["<b>renewal</b><br/>provinces fitted together<br/>+ pooled log R walk<br/>+ sum-to-zero AR(1)<br/>province deviations<br/>+ importation<br/>+ share at risk<br/>+ shared delay<br/>+ shared ascertainment<br/>+ zeros in provinces<br/>with no cases"]
    BV["<b>renewalbvd</b><br/>+ BVDOutbreakSize Rt,<br/>down-weighted (ζ = 0.5)"]

    SP -- "pool the provinces" --> RN
    RN -- "add external Rt" --> BV

docs.title: Single patch (renewalsp)
docs.text:
renewalsp runs the model once for each province \(p\) with cases, on that province's known and imputed onsets and delays alone. Nothing is pooled across provinces.

flowchart TD
    subgraph TR["Transmission"]
        RT["log R<sub>p</sub>(t)<br/>weekly random walk"]
        GI["Generation interval g(τ)"]
        INF["Infections per resident x<sub>p</sub>(t)"]
    end
    ONS["Expected cases<br/>by onset day<br/>λ<sub>p</sub>(s) = α(s) N<sub>p</sub> (x<sub>p</sub> ∗ η)(s)"]
    INC["Incubation period η(u)<br/>log-normal, uncertain mean and SD,<br/>0 to 28 days"]
    DEL["Onset-to-report delay<br/>f<sub>s</sub>(d)<br/>hazard shifted by γ(s),<br/>a weekly walk on onset day<br/><i>renewal: shared</i>"]
    MISS["Share reported<br/>without onset π<sub>p</sub>(t)<br/>weekly walk"]
    subgraph OB["Data streams at vintage T"]
        KN["Known onsets<br/>onsets × delay to report<br/>× share with an onset<br/>× published by T"]
        IM["Hub-imputed onsets<br/>reports without an onset,<br/>spread back by the hub's<br/>published delays"]
        DC["Known-onset delays<br/>by onset week and delay"]
    end
    subgraph LK["Likelihood"]
        LKN["Negative binomial<br/>by week"]
        LKI["Negative binomial<br/>by week"]
        LKD["Dirichlet-multinomial<br/>by onset week"]
    end
    FC["Forecast<br/>log R reverts to 0<br/>final known plus imputed onsets"]

    RT --> INF
    GI --> INF
    INF --> ONS
    INC --> ONS
    ONS --> OB
    DEL --> OB
    MISS --> OB
    KN --> LKN
    IM --> LKI
    DC --> LKD
    LK --> FC

A province with at least 20 cases in its last 6 data weeks, an outbreak province, gets this model. A province with cases but too few for its own fit, \(y_w\) in each of its \(n_w\) data weeks, has

\[ \lambda_p \sim \text{Gamma}\Big(\tfrac{1}{2} + \sum_w y_w,\ n_w\Big), \qquad \tilde y_p(w) = \max\{y_w, z_p(w)\}, \qquad z_p(w) \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda_p), \]

with one \(\lambda_p\) per trajectory and \(y_w\) the count reported at the origin (0 for weeks without data), as in randomwalk. Provinces with no cases get no forecast.

docs.title: Time axis
docs.text: The data weeks start one week before weekly onsets, summed over the modelled provinces, first reach 5, or their peak if lower. In renewalsp the modelled province is \(p\) alone, so each fit has its own axis. The data weeks end with the week that holds \(T\), the release's last report day (Data). The model axis starts 42 days (6 weeks) earlier, the length of the generation interval, for seeding. Every weekly walk is held at its starting value over the 6 seeding weeks and the first data week. The fit axis is the data weeks.

docs.title: Reproduction number
docs.text:
\[ \log R_p(t) = \log R_p(t - 1) + \sigma_R z(t), \qquad \sigma_R \sim \mathcal{N}^+(0, 0.2^2), \]

with standard normal steps \(z(t)\), sampled non-centred, and a start \(\mathcal{N}(0, 0.5^2)\).

docs.title: Renewal
docs.text:
The renewal runs on infections per resident, dated by infection:

\[ x_p(t) = R_p(t) \sum_{\tau \ge 1} x_p(t - \tau)\, g(\tau). \]

\(g\) is BVDOutbreakSize's Gamma generation interval (mean 15.3, SD 9.3 days), double interval censored as \(G(d + 1) - 2G(d) + G(d - 1)\) with \(G\) the integrated cdf, on lags 1 to 42 and renormalised (mean 14.8, SD 8.4 days), as primarycensored's dpcens(1:42, L = 1, D = 43)12. Seeds are \(e_p \sim \text{LogNormal}(0, 1.5^2)\) infections per day that will be confirmed, or \(I_{0,p} = e_p / (\alpha_0 N_p)\) infections per resident, on the first data day. The seed is projected back over the seeding weeks at the growth rate implied by \(R_p\) and \(g\), clipped to \([-0.05, 0.3]\) per day.

docs.title: Ascertainment
docs.text:
Onsets follow infections after the incubation period \(\eta\), and expected confirmed onsets are

\[ \lambda_p(s) = \alpha(s)\, N_p \sum_{u = 0}^{28} x_p(s - u)\, \eta(u), \qquad \operatorname{logit} \alpha(s) = \operatorname{logit} \alpha_0 + a(s), \]

with \(N_p\) the province population, \(\alpha_0 = 0.6\) fixed and \(a\) a weekly random walk from zero with step SD \(\mathcal{N}^+(0, 0.03^2)\). \(\eta\) is a log-normal incubation period for Bundibugyo virus disease with BVDOutbreakSize's priors (onset_incidence_model) on its mean \(\mu_\eta \sim \mathcal{N}(6.3, 0.54^2)\) and SD \(\sigma_\eta \sim \mathcal{N}(3.5, 0.8^2)\), both truncated below at 1 day. The mean prior reproduces the 95% CI of 5.2 to 7.3 days from the 2007 Uganda outbreak3. MacNeil et al. give no interval on the spread, so the SD prior is BVDOutbreakSize's weakly informative choice around 3.5 days. Each draw of \(\eta\) is double interval censored in the same way on lags 0 to 28, the 99.9% quantile at the prior means, as dpcens(0:28, plnorm, D = 29). BVDOutbreakSize keeps lags 0 to 15 of its incubation period, up to its 98% quantile. We keep lags 0 to 28.

docs.title: Delays
docs.text:
The onset-to-report delay \(f_s(d)\), on days \(d\) from 0 to 60, comes from a discrete hazard that varies with onset day:

\[ \operatorname{logit} h_s(d) = \beta(d) + \gamma(s), \qquad f_s(d) = h_s(d) \prod_{j < d}\{1 - h_s(j)\}, \qquad h_s(60) = 1. \]
  • \(\beta\) is a random walk over delay, \(\beta(0) \sim \mathcal{N}(-2, 1)\) with step SD \(\mathcal{N}^+(0, 0.4^2)\), so the shape is smooth but not parametric.
  • \(\gamma\) is a weekly random walk over onset day from zero, with step SD \(\mathcal{N}^+(0, 0.15^2)\), shifting all hazards together.

docs.title: Missing onsets
docs.text: Cases reported on day \(t\) without an onset are a share \(\pi_p(t)\) of reports, with \(\operatorname{logit} \pi_p(t) = b(t)\). \(b\) is a weekly random walk with start \(\mathcal{N}(-2, 1)\) and step SD \(\mathcal{N}^+(0, 0.3^2)\).

docs.title: Known onsets
docs.text:
A case reported on day \(t\) is in the vintage published at \(T\) with probability \(c(t) = F_\ell(T - t)\), with \(F_\ell\) the cdf of the report-to-publication lag. The lag is uniform on 0 to 3 days. Expected known onsets, right truncated by vintage, are

\[ \mathrm{known}_{p,T}(s) = \lambda_p(s) \sum_{d} f_s(d)\, \{1 - \pi_p(s + d)\}\, c(s + d). \]

docs.title: Hub imputation
docs.text:
The hub gives each case reported without an onset one by subtracting a delay drawn from a fit to its published delays (imputation details). We model that procedure, bias included:

\[ M_p(t) = \pi_p(t) \sum_s \lambda_p(s)\, f_s(t - s), \qquad \mathrm{imputed}_{p,T}(s) = \sum_{t = s}^{T} \hat f_T(t - s)\, c(t)\, M_p(t). \]

\(M_p(t)\) are the cases reported on day \(t\) without an onset. The hub draws a report hour from \(\mathrm{Unif}(0, 24)\) and subtracts a generalised gamma delay in hours fitted to the non-negative delays published at 2026-10-17. \(\hat f_T\) is the daily pmf this implies, \(\hat f_T(k) = \int_0^1 \{F_T(k + u) - F_T(k - 1 + u)\}\, du\) with \(F_T\) the delay cdf in days, on 0 to 60 days, and is data. Up to the 2026-10-24 release the hub fitted the delays as exact, and from 2026-11-01 as double interval censored (hub issue 75). We refit both, so \(F_T\) is the fit the hub used for release \(T\).

docs.title: Likelihood
docs.text:
• Weekly \(\mathrm{known}_{p,T}\) and \(\mathrm{imputed}_{p,T}\) are negative binomial, each stream with \(1/\sqrt{\phi} \sim \text{HalfNormal}(0.25)\) and \(\phi\) capped at 1000.
  • Known-onset delays, by onset week and delay on 0 to 60 days, are Dirichlet-multinomial given each week's total. Their probabilities come from \(\lambda\), \(f\), \(\pi\) and \(c\), with \(1/\sqrt{\psi} \sim \text{HalfNormal}(0.1)\) and \(\psi\) capped at \(10^4\). Delays below 0 count as 0 and delays above 60 as 60.

docs.title: Forecasts
docs.text: The random walks carry \(\alpha\), \(f\) and \(\pi\) to the forecast horizon, and each of 100 trajectories is one posterior draw. Past the fit axis \(\log R_p\) reverts towards 0 with a half-life of 2 weeks, \(\log R_p(t) = 2^{-1/2} \log R_p(t - 1) + \sigma_R z(t)\). This stops the unanchored walk from compounding growth over the horizon. The half-life is fixed, not fitted, since no data inform the forecast weeks. The reversion leaves the fit unchanged. A trajectory is the final known plus final imputed counts. Final known counts are those reported by the cut-off plus a negative binomial draw of those reported later, as in epinowcast. Final imputed counts are a negative binomial draw centred on the current imputed count plus those expected later, since the hub re-imputes each vintage. The national trajectory is the sum of the provinces plus an unassigned component, \(\max\{0, Y_{CD}(w) - \sum_p Y_p(w)\}\) in data weeks and \(\rho \sum_p \tilde y_{p,k}(w)\) after, with \(\rho\) its share over the last 4 data weeks and \(\tilde y_{p,k}\) trajectory \(k\) of province \(p\).

docs.title: Partially pooled (renewal)
docs.text:
renewal fits every province with cases in one model, on the axis set by their summed onsets. The provinces share the trend \(\log R(t)\), the deviation SD \(\sigma_\delta\) and half-life \(h\), the start spread \(\sigma_v\), ascertainment \(\alpha\), the delay \(f_s\), the trend \(b\) of the missing-onset share, the share at risk \(\nu\) and the importation share \(\varepsilon\). Each province has its own deviations \(\delta_p\) and \(\omega_p\) and its own seed. Provinces are linked by importation through \(W\), and provinces with no cases by \(\mu_q\). Known-onset delays are pooled over provinces. Leaving a province out removes its known and imputed terms and its delays but keeps it in the latent process.

flowchart TD
    LR["Pooled log R(t)<br/>weekly random walk"]
    DV["Province deviations δ<sub>p</sub>(t)<br/>sum-to-zero AR(1)"]
    RP["log R<sub>p</sub>(t) = log R(t) + δ<sub>p</sub>(t)"]
    K["Gravity kernel<br/>K<sub>qp</sub> ∝ N<sub>p</sub> exp(−D<sub>qp</sub> / 300 km)"]
    W["Importation<br/>W = (1 − ε) I + ε diag(1/N) K<sup>T</sup> diag(N)"]
    CORE["<b>Renewal core</b><br/>see above<br/>with a share at risk ν"]

    LR --> RP
    DV --> RP
    K --> W
    RP --> CORE
    W --> CORE

docs.title: Pooled reproduction number
docs.text:
\[ \log R_p(t) = \log R(t) + \delta_p(t). \]

The pooled trend \(\log R(t)\) is the unweighted mean of \(\log R_p(t)\), not the national Rt, and is the walk of renewalsp. The province deviations sum to zero. They are \(\delta_p(t) = \sum_j Q_{pj}\, \eta_j(t)\), with \(Q\) an orthonormal basis of the sum-to-zero subspace and \(P - 1\) weekly AR(1) processes \(\eta_j\) that decay towards 0, the pooled trend:

\[ \eta_j(t) = \phi\, \eta_j(t - 1) + \sigma_\delta z_j(t), \qquad \phi = 2^{-1/h}, \qquad h \sim \text{LogNormal}(\log 6, 0.6^2)\ \text{weeks}, \qquad \sigma_\delta \sim \mathcal{N}^+(0, 0.1^2). \]

The shared \(\sigma_\delta\) and \(h\) pool the provinces. The starting offsets are \(\eta_j(0) = u_j\), with \(u_j \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_v^2)\) and \(\sigma_v \sim \mathcal{N}^+(0, 0.3^2)\), so \(\delta_p(0) = \sum_j Q_{pj} u_j\). Past the fit axis the pooled trend reverts as in renewalsp, and the deviations keep their AR(1).

docs.title: Importation and depletion
docs.text:
The renewal of renewalsp gains importation and a share at risk:

\[ y_p(t) = R_p(t) \sum_q W_{pq} \sum_{ au \ge 1} x_q(t - au)\, g( au), \qquad x_p(t) = S_p(t) ig\{1 - e^{-y_p(t)/ u} ig\}, \qquad S_p(t + 1) = S_p(t)\, e^{-y_p(t)/ u}. \]
  • \(W = (1 - \varepsilon) I + \varepsilon\, \mathrm{diag}(1/N) K^ op \mathrm{diag}(N)\) mixes transmission between provinces, with \(\varepsilon \sim ext{Beta}(1, 100)\).
  • \(K\) is a row-normalised gravity kernel, \(K_{qp} \propto N_p e^{-D_{qp}/300\, ext{km}}\) for \(q e p\), with \(D\) the great-circle distance between population-weighted province centres.
  • \( u \sim ext{LogNormal}(\log 0.05, 0.75^2)\) is the share at risk. \(S_p\) starts at \( u\) less the seed, so infections never exceed \( u N_p\).

Provinces with cases in the first data week are seeded at the start. Later provinces start at \(10^{-6}\) of that level and add \(I_{0,p}\) to \(y_p(t)\) each day for 7 days. These 7 days start 5 days before the province's first case week. That lead puts the most onsets of a week of seeded infections in the first case week (67%, with 9% before it) at the prior mean incubation period.

docs.title: Missing-onset deviations
docs.text:
The missing-onset share gains sum-to-zero province deviations \(\omega_p\) on the same basis \(Q\):

\[ \operatorname{logit} \pi_p(t) = b(t) + \omega_p(t). \]

The deviations are random walks, not AR(1). They start with province spread \(\mathcal{N}^+(0, 0.5^2)\), sampled non-centred, and have step SD \(\mathcal{N}^+(0, 0.1^2)\).

docs.title: Provinces with no cases
docs.text: Provinces \(q\) without cases have an importation-only component. Their weekly zeros are Poisson with mean \(\mu_q(s) = \kappa \sum_p K_{pq}\, \lambda_p(s)\), \(\kappa \sim \text{LogNormal}(\log 10^{-3}, 2^2)\). In the forecast they draw Poisson importations after the cut-off, which spread at the infection-weighted national Rt without depletion.

docs.title: BVDOutbreakSize-informed (renewalbvd)
docs.text:
Every renewal model takes from the BVDOutbreakSize main model its generation interval, the prior on the half-life of the province deviations and the sum-to-zero basis for them. renewalbvd also takes the Rt estimates of one BVDOutbreakSize release, chosen as on the Data methods page. Without such a release renewalbvd is renewal.

flowchart TD
    REL["BVDOutbreakSize release<br/>data cut-off a<sub>b</sub>"]
    NAT["National log Rt draws<br/>mean μ<sub>N</sub>, SD σ<sub>N</sub>"]
    PAT["Patch medians and<br/>90% intervals"]
    AL["Aligned to infection day<br/>s<sub>b</sub> = a<sub>b</sub>"]
    CORE["<b>Renewal core, pooled</b><br/>see above<br/>infection-weighted R<sub>N</sub>(s<sub>b</sub>), R<sub>k</sub>(s<sub>b</sub>)"]
    LK["Normal terms<br/>down-weighted, ζ = 0.5"]

    REL --> NAT
    REL --> PAT
    NAT --> AL
    PAT --> AL
    AL --> LK
    CORE --> LK

From the release it takes the posterior draws of the national \(\log R\) and, where the release has province estimates, each patch's median and 90% interval with the hub provinces the patch covers. With \(a_b\) the release's data cut-off, the estimates are aligned to \(s_b = a_b\), as both models date Rt by infection. The fit axis extends to the end of the week of \(s_b\) when that week is after the data. For the nation \(N\) and each patch \(k\) with a modelled province, the model's Rt is weighted by infections over the data week that holds \(s_b\),

\[ R_G(s_b) = \frac{\sum_{p \in G} O_p\, R_p(s_b)}{\sum_{p \in G} O_p}, \qquad O_p = N_p \sum_{t \in \text{week}(s_b)} x_p(t), \qquad G \in \{N, k\}. \]

With the term down-weighted by \(\zeta = 0.5\), the likelihood gains

\[ \mu_N \sim \mathcal{N}\big(\log R_N(s_b),\, \sigma_N^2/\zeta\big), \qquad m_k - m_N \sim \mathcal{N}\big(\log R_k(s_b) - \log R_N(s_b),\, \tau_k^2/\zeta\big), \qquad \tau_k^2 = \max(\sigma_k^2 - \sigma_N'^2,\, 0.05^2). \]

\(\mu_N\) and \(\sigma_N\) are the mean and SD of the release's national log Rt draws. \(m_k\) and \(\sigma_k\) are each patch's log median and SD, the SD from the 90% interval. \(m_N\) and \(\sigma_N'\) are the same summaries of the national row in the patch table, or \(\mu_N\) and \(\sigma_N\) if it has none. Leaving a province out drops the national term and the patch that holds it. The term adds no parameters, and \(\zeta = 0\) gives renewal. It is down-weighted because BVDOutbreakSize is fitted to largely the same data, so at full weight those data would count twice.

docs.title: Health zones
docs.text: Zone samples sum to their province's samples, sample by sample and week by week, and the national value stays the sum of the provinces. The random walk baselines run at zone level and their samples set the zone shares of the province samples (Baseline models). Every other model's province forecast is split across the zones.

docs.title: Split of province samples
docs.text:
For province \(p\) with zones \(z\), let \(o_z(w)\) be zone \(z\)'s published count for week \(w\) and \(O(w) = \sum_z o_z(w)\). Each province sample \(k\) draws its zone shares once, for all weeks:

\[ \theta^{(k)} \sim \text{Dirichlet}(a), \qquad a_z = r_z + n_0\, \frac{l_z + a_0}{\sum_{z'} (l_{z'} + a_0)}. \]

\(r_z\) is the zone's onsets over the 2 weeks before the vintage and \(l_z\) those over the 16 weeks before it. Recent shares are shrunk towards longer-run shares by \(n_0 = 100\) pseudo-cases. The floor \(a_0 = 1/2\) gives a zone with no cases a small share. Province samples are rounded. Each zone keeps its published count and the rest of the province sample \(Y^{(k)}(w)\) is split:

\[ y^{(k)}_z(w) = o_z(w) + m_z, \qquad m \sim \text{Multinomial}\big(Y^{(k)}(w) - O(w),\ \theta^{(k)}\big). \]

A sample below the published total is drawn from the published zone counts without replacement instead.

docs.title: Development log
docs.text:
Model and evaluation decisions, newest first.

Date Area Decision Reason Evidence 2026-11-03 evaluation The held-out run at 11-01 is committed without the fitted renewal variants; it scores nothing until a later release exists. A held-out run with fits of renewal, renewalsp and renewalbvd at 11-01 stopped on a loaded host with nothing written, so it is a note and not a result. The fits wait for the renewalsp and renewalbvd fixes. heldout-run.yml 2026-11-03 evaluation The 2026-10-28 entry on the first model choice no longer holds as stated: its relative WIS of 0.69 came from earlier code. With every model scored against the 11-01 truth and the NB minus Poisson observation model, randomwalknowcast's complete-week WIS on development origins is 6.76 against randomwalk's 7.87. On the count each later release reports it is 1.22 times randomwalk's on provinces and 0.78 nationally from 10-17, and 1.55 and 2.49 from 10-24. nowcast-scores.csv 2026-11-03 evaluation Every model, hub teams included, is scored on the count each later release reports. Final-count samples X map to R + q (X - R), with R the count reported at the origin and q the share of the outstanding count the later release is expected to report under the origin's delay. The latest-release target is removed, and complete weeks are a secondary check. Sam's decision: scoring final counts against counts still being reported makes no sense. 1cc7cbe 2026-11-03 evaluation Six ladder rungs the script no longer runs were dropped from the ladder results. Their rows described models that no longer exist. 010afdf 2026-11-03 submission A plausibility check rules a candidate out. Every week from the nowcast to the last horizon needs a median under 5 times and a 97.5% quantile under 15 times the largest of the last 4 observed weeks, floored at 20, and a median above a twentieth of it. renewalsp's Ituri forecast had a 97.5% quantile 40 to 50 times the recent maximum. ci/policy.toml 2026-11-03 submission The renewal track falls back from most to least complex: renewalbvd, renewalsp, renewal, randomwalknowcast, randomwalk. Sam's decision. ci/policy.toml 2026-11-02 submission seabbs-renewal opted in to submit each round, carrying renewal. Sam's decision. config/hub.toml 2026-10-30 model randomwalknowcast ages release weeks by release date and leaves out weeks ending after a release; development factors are fitted to the growth between any consecutive releases; the change still to come is Skellam with a spread fitted by age to retrospective nowcasts, and totals are floored at zero. Sam's decisions. Negative changes between releases occur at 1 to 2 of 8 to 13 points per age from 5 weeks old. The fitted Skellam has Pearson dispersion 0.97 on the retrospective errors (Poisson difference without the extra spread: 2 to 230), so a difference of negative binomials is not needed. National at +4 weeks from 10-24 has a 95% bound of 476 (4241 before, driven by the 5.3-fold factor the Friday release gave week ages 0). The 10-09 release mixes weeks 6 days old with weeks 0 days old at age 0, so f_0 is 1.65 at 10-24, against 3.5 between 10-17 and 10-24; the latest week is now underpredicted (10-17 origin: bias -1 at ages 0, 7 and 14 days). 25 2026-10-30 model randomwalknowcast nowcasts on the hub's release triangle (totals by onset week and release): development factors from releases a week apart, own above 50 cases a week and pooled otherwise, and negative binomial sizes from nowcasts made at earlier releases. The delay-file nowcast is removed. Sam's decision, replacing the delay-file triangle, which missed late entries. Real data allow a release nowcast only from 10-17 (truth 10-24): there, ages 0, 7 and 14 days score national WIS 394, 64 and 9 against 42, 15 and 43 for the delay-file nowcast, overshooting the youngest weeks because the 10-09 release fell on a Friday and its latest week was barely reported (k = 0 factor 9.2). Reconstructed vintages: national nowcast WIS 19.5 against 63.3, forecast 58.2 against 248.1. Scenarios: national nowcast 28.8 against 34.0, forecast 100.7 against 88.5. At 10-24 each size rests on one release of 8 provinces. 25 2026-10-30 model randomwalknowcast keeps the delay-file nowcast; a nowcast on the hub's release triangle waits for more weekly releases. Sam's decision (option a). With releases on 08-18, 10-09, 10-17 and 10-24 each week is seen at only about three consecutive weekly delays, so the release triangle has no complete row beyond 2 weeks and no retrospective nowcasts. baselinenowcast cannot estimate a delay or its uncertainty from it. 25 2026-10-30 model randomwalk counts a week as complete once 95% of its final total is published, from the hub's releases (90% before); the delay-quantile fallback uses the 95th centile. Sam's decision. Real as-of-T national WIS: forecast 35.4 to 32.9, nowcast weeks 49.3 to 34.6 (90% coverage 0.42 to 0.67); province nowcast weeks 9.2 to 7.3. Reconstructed and scenarios are worse (national forecast WIS 99.5 to 122.5 and 172.0 to 203.0), as the walk starts a week earlier during growth. 25 2026-10-30 model randomwalk and randomwalknowcast share one random walk (log-scale Gaussian steps, Poisson draws, spread pooled below 10 cases a week); randomwalknowcast's empirical-step walk and low-count rate walk are removed. randomwalk takes its last complete week from the hub's releases. Sam's decision. Real as-of-T national forecast WIS: randomwalk 37.5 to 35.4, randomwalknowcast 95.2 to 103.7 (90% coverage 0.56 to 0.75). RandomWalk nowcast weeks worsen slightly (national 46.3 to 49.3). On reconstructed vintages and scenarios randomwalk is worse (national forecast WIS 69.6 to 99.5 and 119.3 to 172.0): the release completeness is 3 weeks against about 2 from the delays, so its walk starts earlier, and the early reconstructed vintages give 6. Only the 10-17 real vintage has two releases a week apart before it. 25 2026-10-30 model Both baselines pool the walk spread only for places under 10 cases a week; randomwalknowcast keeps 50 delays a week for its own delay. Sam's correction: a 50 a week limit pooled almost every province, giving small ones the narrow spread of large ones. With 10, real as-of-T province forecast 90% coverage is 0.85 for randomwalk (0.62 at 50, 0.81 with no pooling) and 0.77 for randomwalknowcast (0.69 at 50), with WIS 15.2 and 19.2 (15.0 and 17.8 at 50). 22 2026-10-30 model randomwalk uses the pooled spread for provinces under 50 cases a week, the same rule randomwalknowcast uses for its delay and steps. Sam's decision: one pooling rule for both baselines. Province scores move little but coverage falls, as small provinces get the narrower spread of the large ones: real as-of-T province forecast WIS 14.5 to 15.0 and 90% coverage 0.81 to 0.62; reconstructed WIS 19.8 to 19.6 and coverage 0.92 to 0.82; scenarios 3.60 to 3.61 and 0.89 to 0.86. 22 2026-10-30 model randomwalknowcast's longest delay D is 84 days (13 onset weeks). 0.8% of delays exceed 35 days, 0.2% exceed 60 and 0.07% exceed 90. Of D = 35, 56 and 84 days, 84 scores best on real vintages (as-of-T national forecast WIS 97.1, 109.2, 80.6; province nowcast WIS 8.1, 7.6, 6.9). On scenarios, 56 and 84 are close (national forecast WIS 88.9 and 92.0). 23 2026-10-30 model randomwalknowcast is plain baselinenowcast on the report-date triangle: no publication lag, no late tail, and each week's share is its cases in the delay file over its chain-ladder nowcast. Sam's decision, replacing the 0 to 3 day lag and its tail. On real vintages, as-of-T, national nowcast WIS rises from 25.1 to 35.9, and national bias at ages 7 and 14 days goes from -0.38 and -0.86 to -0.97 and -1.00, with 90% coverage 0 at both. The latest week improves (national WIS 25.3 against 50.6). Scenario nowcast WIS rises from 19.2 to 34.0. 23 2026-10-30 model randomwalknowcast keeps the 0 to 3 day publication lag with its 10% tail. Issue #23. Taking each week's share from the triangle itself, as its cases in the file over its chain-ladder nowcast, needs no lag but nowcasts worse: real as-of-T national nowcast WIS 38.6 against 25.1, scenarios 38.6 against 19.2, real 90% coverage 0.33 against 0.79. With no lag, the weekly growth between real vintages is underpredicted (national mean log ratio -0.11 against -0.04), and a 0 to 6 day lag doubles the real national nowcast WIS (52.7 against 24.9). 23 2026-10-30 model randomwalknowcast's walk starts from each sample's own nowcast of the latest week. Sam's decision (issue #25). Against the share-weighted 3-week centre, calibrated scenarios score better (national forecast WIS 83 against 119, 90% coverage 0.71 against 0.33). On real vintages with a delay file it is no worse (national forecast WIS 12 against 13 at 10-09, 8 against 3 at 10-17). It is worse at 08-18, which has a reconstructed delay file (171 against 51 at horizon 0), and on reconstructed vintages (national forecast WIS 125 against 62), whose latest week is nowcast poorly. 25 2026-10-30 model randomwalknowcast's reporting triangle uses the delays as reported in the vintage's file, and the first-publication delays are removed. Issue #25. The rows the 10-24 file added for old weeks were onsets filled in for imputed cases, not late reports: Nord-Kivu's known onsets for 09-12 rose from 143 to 168 while its total stayed at 194. Counted as late reports they set the retrospective negative binomial sizes at horizons 2 and 3 to 0.3 to 0.5, so the national 90% interval for the week ending 10-10 was 455 to 859 against 413 published. With reported delays it is 429 to 456. On the development vintages, which predate that file, scores are unchanged (real as-of-T national nowcast WIS 24.7 against 24.9). 25 2026-10-28 model randomwalknowcast keeps each place's own walk steps; a parent level can pass its pooled steps to places without delays. Shrinking each place's step spread toward a pooled spread scored worse at every strength (real as-of-T national forecast WIS 22.8 to 27.1 against 18.9). 09414a5 2026-10-28 model randomwalknowcast's publication lag gets a 10% tail spread over 4 to 28 days. Nowcasts of weeks 4 to 24 days old were biased low on every real and reconstructed origin (real national mean log ratio -0.11, Nord-Kivu -0.30). With the tail the real bias is -0.03 to -0.04 and nowcast-week WIS falls from 30.8 to 24.7, but forecast-week WIS on the 3 real origins rises from 21.4 to 28.1 (reconstructed 82.5 to 79.6). 3cedf37 2026-10-28 model randomwalknowcast's walk takes steps from every nowcast week, with no 50% cut, and keeps the share-weighted centre. Issues #17 and #18. Steps from all weeks are not worse than the 50% rule (real as-of-T forecast-week WIS 18.9 against 18.0; reconstructed 83.4 against 85.5). An equal-weight centre (20.8 real, 92.9 reconstructed) and centring on the latest week alone (60.6 real) scored worse, so the latest week enters weighted by its share reported. 4030b50 2026-10-28 model Sparse places borrow the walk steps of places with their own delay, and below 10 cases a week walk a Poisson rate. Bas-Uele's own log steps from counts near zero gave 97.5% quantiles in the hundreds; pooled log steps from zero then collapsed to 1. The rate walk gives 3 to 5 a week for 7 cases in 6 weeks. 479b342 2026-10-28 model randomwalknowcast's reporting triangle is indexed by first publication. Nord-Kivu publishes batches late (246 rows for weeks up to 10-03 added between 10-17 and 10-24). Counting each delay to the first delay file holding the case lets the chain ladder and its retrospective sizes learn them, as baselinenowcast intends. e4646cb 2026-10-28 model randomwalknowcast nowcasts every week, the latest included, scaling each published total by the share reported. Sam's decision. The share averages the delay cdf over onset days and a publication lag uniform on 0 to 3 days, as in the renewal model, which fits first reports on real data better than a fixed 3 days (29% reported at age 0 against 22% and 11%). On reconstructed vintages the latest week scores worse (WIS 172 against 47 for randomwalk) because they are built with a fixed 3-day lag; judged on real data, where it scores 22 against 41. 1e88ab8 2026-10-28 evaluation randomwalknowcast recorded as the first model choice, and held-out scoring covers randomwalk and randomwalknowcast on every held-out vintage. randomwalknowcast is submitted as seabbsbaseline. On complete weeks of the three real development origins its WIS is 0.69 times that of randomwalk. The baselines need no fit, so both are always scored beside the chosen model. results/model-choice.yml 2026-10-28 evaluation Health-zone forecasts split the province forecasts across zones. Against 2026-10-24 over the three earlier real vintages, zones split from randomwalk have WIS 0.83 and log WIS 0.88 times those of zone randomwalk, lower at every horizon from -2. Split from randomwalknowcast the ratios are 0.93 and 0.90, lowest in the nowcast weeks and near one from horizon 0. b795523 2026-10-28 model A BVDOutbreakSize release is used only if its joint R-hat is at most 1.1. Releases that had not converged would pass a poor Rt to renewalbvd. b32b7e0 2026-10-28 evaluation The held-out set rolls forward with each model choice, and the placeholder choice is removed. Sam's decision: models are tuned on all data up to each choice, and only vintages after a choice are held out. results/model-choice.yml 2026-10-28 docs The package renamed to bdbvhubrenewal. It follows the repository name. e491a54 2026-10-28 model The publication lag default reverted to a fixed 0 to 3 days. The empirical lag counted onset backfill as late reporting, so it over-predicted. 167698f 2026-10-28 model The fallback variant is removed. The chain is renewal, its retry, renewalsp, randomwalknowcast and randomwalk. Sam's decision. 6142f10 2026-10-28 submission Every fit uses 2 chains of 500 warm-up and 500 draws, in the CI and the backtest. Sam's decision: one setting for all work, sized for the CI runners. 4e852dc 2026-10-28 evaluation Primary scores use complete weeks only: weeks that ended at least K = 3 weeks before the truth vintage. By 21 days 96% of a week's final count is published in the delay data, so these weeks are close to final for every model. 91e4e94 2026-10-28 model A late province is seeded over its first case week, not the week before. Seeding the week before put cases where the data have none. f1f1751 2026-10-28 model Missingness offsets of the imputed share sampled non-centred. The centred offsets did not mix: R-hat 1.68 with a bulk ESS of 1.5 in a 2 x 200 fit. b8c001d 2026-10-10 evaluation RandomWalk recorded as the placeholder model choice. Only the randomwalk baseline existed. The split was fixed before any held-out scoring, after the 2026-10-09 vintage and the reconstructed vintage of 2026-10-10, so the 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-24 vintages and every later one were held out. results/model-choice.yml

docs.title: Model building
docs.text:
How the renewal model was built, one component at a time, with the checks at each step.

The model was built as a ladder of rungs, following a Bayesian workflow. Each rung adds one component to the one before, from a single national renewal to the full province model. Each is fitted to a simulated outbreak with known parameters and to a real vintage. The real-vintage columns come from forecasts at one origin, the 2026-10-09 vintage, scored against the 2026-10-24 vintage as reported. They are a check on each step, not a comparison of models. The Backtest compares the models. A component is kept only if the sampler stays healthy, the simulated parameters are recovered, and the real forecasts are no worse. The rungs and their settings are in bdbvhubrenewal.model.model.LADDER, and scripts/ladder.py runs them into results/ladder.csv. The Renewal models page describes the result.

docs.title: Rungs
docs.text:
What each rung adds, and what was decided.

Step Rung Adds Decision 0 randomwalk The last complete week carried forward, as the reference. Reference only. 1 S0 national renewal One renewal on the national total, no truncation. Dropped as a candidate: national scores no better than randomwalk, and it gives no provinces. 2 S1 + provinces (pooled Rt) A renewal per province with case, Rt a national walk plus pooled deviations. Kept: province forecasts and pooling, with national scores as S0. 3 S2 + truncation (hub delay) Right truncation of the total by the hub's own delay. Kept: the largest gain, national CRPS down by about three quarters on simulated data and by a third on real. 4 S3 + delays, missingness, imputation Known and imputed onsets as two streams, with time-varying delays and missingness and the hub's imputation modelled. Kept on the fuller-model rule: level with S2 on real data and worse on simulated national, and it models the imputed stream and changing delays the target depends on. 5 S4 + coupling and importation Gravity importation between provinces and an importation-only part for provinces with no cases. Kept on the fuller-model rule: scores level, it learns across provinces and forecasts spread to new ones. 6 S5 + depletion (main) Susceptible depletion; this is renewal. Kept and chosen as renewal: fewer wild prior draws (0.44 to 0.32), with scores level with S3 and S4 and a little behind S2. 7 renewalbvd BVDOutbreakSize Rt as a tempered pseudo-observation. Heads the submission chain: best on simulated data with a truth-based BVD summary, worse on the one real vintage. 8 renewalsp An independent single-patch renewal per location, the nation included. Second in the submission chain, after renewalbvd.

docs.text:
The Python API of bdbvhubrenewal, grouped by task. See Setup to install it and Getting started for a worked example.

Task Pages Start with Data Data load_target, load_daily, load_delays, delays_for_vintage Models Forecasters, Renewal model, Baselinenowcast get_model, list_models, ForecastTask, ForecastModel.forecast Evaluation Evaluation make_tasks, run_forecasts, score_forecasts, release_backtest Reporting Figures and tables, Submission plot_location_grid, plot_forecasts, to_hub_table, write_submission CLI CLI bdbvhubrenewal --help

docs.title: A forecast in five steps
docs.text:
Run from the repository root after bdbvhubrenewal data has written the tidy tables to data/.

import dataclasses

from bdbvhubrenewal.data import (
    delays_for_vintage,
    load_daily,
    load_delays,
    load_target,
)
from bdbvhubrenewal.evaluation import backtest as bt
from bdbvhubrenewal.evaluation.nowcast import release_backtest
from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters import get_model
from bdbvhubrenewal.reporting.plots import plot_location_grid

# 1. Load the data.
target, daily, delays = load_target(), load_daily(), load_delays()
real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]

# 2. Build the task a model sees at one release.
config = dataclasses.replace(
    bt.load_config("config/backtest.toml"), min_horizon=-6
)
vintage = "2026-10-17"
task = bt.make_tasks(
    real.loc[real["vintage"] == vintage],
    delays_for_vintage(delays, vintage)[0],
    config,
    history=real,
    daily=daily,
)[0]

# 3. Forecast with models from the registry.
models = [get_model("randomwalk"), get_model("randomwalknowcast")]
forecasts = bt.run_forecasts(models, [task])

# 4. Score against later releases.
scores = release_backtest(
    [task], daily, target, models=(), stored=forecasts
).scores

# 5. Plot.
fig = plot_location_grid(forecasts, real, ["CD"])

docs.title: bdbvhubrenewal.baselinenowcast

JAX port of R baselinenowcast 0.2.2 with one extension.

Reporting triangles are (triangle, mask) pairs. mask is True where R has an observed cell and False where R has NA. The extension (E1) skips unobserved cells in the chain ladder ratio of sums for release snapshots (snapshots.py).

R truncates only the first ncol cells in column-major order because of an upstream indexing slip. Non-integer inputs therefore differ from R. Unobserved cells stay zero.

def preprocess_negative_values(
    triangle: Any, mask: Any, validate: bool = True
) -> Array:
    """Move negative reports onto earlier delays (R preprocess.R:47).

    Scanning each row from the last delay back, a negative value is set
    to zero and its amount is taken from the next earlier observed
    cell.
    Every cell is truncated to an integer.
    R truncates only the first ``ncol`` cells in column-major order
    because of an upstream indexing slip.
    Non-integer inputs therefore differ from R.
    Unobserved cells stay zero.

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : array_like
        Reporting triangle, reference times by delays.
    mask : array_like of bool
        True where a cell is observed.
    validate : bool, default True
        Check the triangle and mask first.

    Returns
    -------
    jax.Array
        The triangle with no negative cells.
    """
    values, m = coerce(triangle, mask)
    if validate:
        validate_reporting_triangle(m)
    return _preprocess(values, jnp.asarray(m))

def truncate_to_rows(
    triangle: Any,
    mask: Any,
    n: int | None = None,
    validate: bool = True,
) -> list[Triangle]:
    """Drop 1..n rows from the bottom (R truncate.R:182).

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : array_like
        Reporting triangle, reference times by delays.
    mask : array_like of bool
        True where a cell is observed.
    n : int, optional
        Most rows to drop. Defaults to the number of rows without a
        missing cell minus one.
    validate : bool, default True
        Check the triangle and mask first.

    Returns
    -------
    list of Triangle
        Element ``t - 1`` has its last ``t`` rows removed.
    """
    values, m = coerce(triangle, mask)
    if validate:
        validate_reporting_triangle(m)
    if n is None:
        n = m.shape[0] - n_unobserved_rows(m) - 1
    assert_integerish(n, "n", lower=0)
    out: list[Triangle] = []
    for t in range(1, int(n) + 1):
        n_obs = m.shape[0]
        if t >= n_obs:
            raise ValueError(
                "The as of time point is greater than or equal to the "
                "number of rows in the original triangle."
            )
        out.append((values[: n_obs - t], m[: n_obs - t]))
    return out

def apply_reporting_structure(
    triangle: Any,
    mask: Any,
    structure: Any = 1,
    validate: bool = True,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the mask with a reporting structure applied.

    R apply_reporting_structure.R:79.
    The last row keeps ``structure[0]`` delays, the next row up keeps
    ``structure[0] + structure[1]``, and so on.
    A scalar structure is expanded to groups of that many delays.
    Values under the new False cells are zero in
    ``triangle * mask``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : array_like
        Reporting triangle, reference times by delays.
    mask : array_like of bool
        True where a cell is observed.
    structure : int or array_like of int, default 1
        Delays added per row, from the last row up.
    validate : bool, default True
        Check the triangle and mask first.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray of bool
        The new mask.
    """
    _, m = coerce(triangle, mask)
    if validate:
        validate_reporting_triangle(m)
    rows, cols = m.shape
    s = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(structure, dtype=float))
    if s.size == 1:
        vec = _expand_structure_vec(float(s[0]), cols)
    else:
        vec = s
        if np.any(vec < 0) or not np.all(np.isfinite(vec)):
            raise ValueError("All elements of `structure` must be positive")
        if vec.sum() >= cols:
            raise ValueError(
                "Sum of structure vector must not be greater than or equal "
                "to the number of columns in matrix"
            )
    if vec.size > rows:
        raise ValueError("`structure` has more groups than the triangle rows")
    cutoff = np.cumsum(vec).astype(int) + 1
    out = m.copy()
    for i in range(vec.size):
        out[rows - i - 1, cutoff[i] - 1 :] = False
    return out

def get_reporting_structure(mask: Any) -> float | np.ndarray:
    """Infer the reporting structure of a triangle.

    R reporting_triangle-getters.R:331.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mask : array_like of bool
        True where a cell is observed.

    Returns
    -------
    float or numpy.ndarray
        0 when nothing is missing, a scalar when the structure is a
        regular grouping and a vector otherwise.
    """
    m = np.asarray(mask, dtype=bool)
    n_row_nas = n_unobserved_rows(m)
    if n_row_nas == 0:
        return 0.0
    n_prev = 0.0
    structure = []
    for i in range(1, n_row_nas + 1):
        n_nas = float(m[m.shape[0] - i].sum()) - n_prev
        structure.append(n_nas)
        n_prev += n_nas
    struct = np.asarray(structure)
    expanded = _expand_structure_vec(struct[0], m.shape[1])
    if expanded.shape == struct.shape and np.array_equal(expanded, struct):
        return float(struct[0])
    return struct

def allocate_reference_times(
    mask: Any,
    scale_factor: float = 3,
    prop_delay: float = 0.5,
    n_min_retro_nowcasts: int = 2,
    validate: bool = True,
) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Split reference times between delay and uncertainty estimation.

    R allocate_reference_times.R:57.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mask : array_like of bool
        True where a cell is observed.
    scale_factor : float, default 3
        Reference times to use, as a multiple of the maximum delay.
    prop_delay : float, default 0.5
        Share of them used to estimate the delay.
    n_min_retro_nowcasts : int, default 2
        Fewest retrospective nowcasts to leave for the uncertainty.
    validate : bool, default True
        Check the mask first.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of int
        ``(n_history_delay, n_retrospective_nowcasts)``.
    """
    m = np.asarray(mask, dtype=bool)
    if validate:
        validate_reporting_triangle(m)
    max_delay = m.shape[1] - 1
    _validate_allocation(scale_factor, prop_delay, n_min_retro_nowcasts)

    n_ref_times = m.shape[0]
    n_min_delay = n_unobserved_rows(m) + 1
    n_required = n_min_delay + n_min_retro_nowcasts
    n_target = round(scale_factor * max_delay)

    # .check_against_requirements (allocate_reference_times.R:189)
    if n_target <= n_ref_times and n_target >= n_required:
        n_used = n_target
    elif n_target > n_ref_times:
        if n_ref_times >= n_required:
            warnings.warn(
                f"{n_ref_times} reference times available and {n_target} "
                f"are specified. All {n_ref_times} will be used.",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
            n_used = n_ref_times
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{n_ref_times} reference times available and {n_required} "
                f"are needed, {n_min_delay} for delay estimation and "
                f"{n_min_retro_nowcasts} for uncertainty estimation."
            )
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{scale_factor * max_delay} reference times specified and "
            f"{n_required} are needed, {n_min_delay} for delay estimation "
            f"and {n_min_retro_nowcasts} for uncertainty estimation."
        )

    # .assign_allocation_from_ns (allocate_reference_times.R:278)
    if n_used >= n_target:
        n_history_delay = max(math.floor(n_used * prop_delay), n_min_delay)
        n_retro = n_used - n_history_delay
    else:
        n_remaining = n_used - n_min_delay
        n_retro = math.ceil(n_remaining * (1 - prop_delay))
        n_history_delay = n_used - n_retro
    if n_retro < n_min_retro_nowcasts:
        n_retro = n_min_retro_nowcasts
        n_history_delay = n_used - n_retro
    return int(n_history_delay), int(n_retro)

def rolling_sum(
    values: Array, mask: Array | np.ndarray, k: int
) -> tuple[Array, np.ndarray]:
    """Trailing sum over ``k`` rows, as ``zoo::rollsum(align = "right")``.

    The first ``k - 1`` rows are dropped.
    A window with any unobserved cell is unobserved.
    Use ``functools.partial(rolling_sum, k=7)`` as a
    ``ref_time_aggregator``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    values : jax.Array
        Matrix with reference times as rows.
    mask : jax.Array or numpy.ndarray of bool
        True where a cell is observed.
    k : int
        Window length in rows.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple
        The summed values and their mask, each with ``k - 1`` fewer rows.
    """
    v = jnp.asarray(values)
    m = np.asarray(mask, dtype=bool)
    n = v.shape[0]
    if k < 1 or k > n:
        raise ValueError("`k` must be between 1 and the number of rows")
    vm = jnp.where(jnp.asarray(m), v, 0.0)
    out = sum(vm[i : n - k + 1 + i] for i in range(k))
    ok = np.stack([m[i : n - k + 1 + i] for i in range(k)]).all(axis=0)
    return jnp.where(jnp.asarray(ok), out, 0.0), ok

def estimate_delay(
    triangle: Any,
    mask: Any,
    n: int | None = None,
    validate: bool = True,
) -> Array:
    """Estimate the delay pmf from the last ``n`` rows.

    R estimate_delay.R:51.

def apply_delay(
    triangle: Any,
    mask: Any,
    delay_pmf: Any,
    validate: bool = True,
) -> Array:
    """Fill the unobserved cells with expected counts (R apply_delay.R:43).

    Rows are independent, so only the rows with a missing cell are
    passed to the kernel.

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : array_like
        Reporting triangle, reference times by delays.
    mask : array_like of bool
        True where a cell is observed.
    delay_pmf : array_like
        Probability of each delay, as from `estimate_delay`.
    validate : bool, default True
        Check the triangle and mask first.

    Returns
    -------
    jax.Array
        The point nowcast matrix, with no missing cells.
    """
    values, m = coerce(triangle, mask)
    if validate:
        validate_reporting_triangle(m)
    pmf = jnp.asarray(delay_pmf, dtype=values.dtype)
    _validate_delay_and_triangle(m, pmf)
    k = n_unobserved_rows(m)
    if k == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "`reporting_triangle` doesn't contain any missing values, "
            "there is nothing to nowcast."
        )
    n_rows = m.shape[0]
    filled = _apply_kernel(
        values[n_rows - k :], jnp.asarray(m[n_rows - k :]), pmf
    )
    return jnp.concatenate([values[: n_rows - k], filled], axis=0)

def estimate_and_apply_delay(
    triangle: Any,
    mask: Any,
    n: int | None = None,
    delay_pmf: Any = None,
    validate: bool = True,
) -> Array:
    """Estimate the delay (unless given) and nowcast.

    R estimate_and_apply_delay.R:44.

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : array_like
        Reporting triangle, reference times by delays.
    mask : array_like of bool
        True where a cell is observed.
    n : int, optional
        Rows used to estimate the delay. Defaults to all rows.
    delay_pmf : array_like, optional
        A delay to use instead of estimating one.
    validate : bool, default True
        Check the triangle and mask first.

    Returns
    -------
    jax.Array
        The point nowcast matrix, as from `apply_delay`.
    """
    values, m = coerce(triangle, mask)
    if validate:
        validate_reporting_triangle(m)
    if n is None:
        n = m.shape[0]
    if n > m.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError(
            "The number of observations (rows) specified for delay "
            "estimation must be less than or equal to the number of rows "
            "of the reporting triangle."
        )
    if not np.any(m[m.shape[0] - n :].all(axis=1)):
        raise ValueError(
            "The rows used for delay estimation in the reporting triangle "
            "must contain at least one row with no missing observations."
        )
    if delay_pmf is None:
        delay_pmf = estimate_delay(values, m, n=n, validate=False)
    return apply_delay(values, m, delay_pmf, validate=False)

def baselinenowcast(
    triangle: Any,
    mask: Any,
    key: Array | None = None,
    scale_factor: float = 3,
    prop_delay: float = 0.5,
    output_type: Literal["samples", "point"] = "samples",
    draws: int = 1000,
    uncertainty_model: Callable[..., Array] = fit_by_horizon,
    uncertainty_sampler: Sampler = sample_nb,
    delay_pmf: Any = None,
    uncertainty_params: Any = None,
    preprocess: Callable[..., Array] | None = preprocess_negative_values,
    structure: Any = None,
    ref_time_aggregator: RefTimeAggregator = identity,
    delay_aggregator: DelayAggregator = row_sums,
    validate: bool = True,
) -> Array:
    """Nowcast a reporting triangle.

    Estimates the delay and its uncertainty from the triangle, fills
    the unobserved cells and, for samples, draws the counts still to
    be reported.

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : array_like
        Reporting triangle, reference times by delays.
    mask : array_like of bool
        True where a cell is observed.
    key : jax.Array, optional
        Random key. Needed for ``output_type="samples"``.
    scale_factor, prop_delay : float
        Passed to `allocate_reference_times`.
    output_type : {"samples", "point"}, default "samples"
        Draws, or the point nowcast.
    draws : int, default 1000
        Number of draws.
    uncertainty_model : callable, default fit_by_horizon
        Fits the uncertainty parameters.
    uncertainty_sampler : Sampler, default sample_nb
        Draws counts given a mean and the parameters.
    delay_pmf, uncertainty_params : array_like, optional
        Use these instead of estimating them.
    preprocess : callable or None, default preprocess_negative_values
        Applied to the triangle first.
    structure : int or array_like, optional
        Reporting structure. Defaults to `get_reporting_structure`.
    ref_time_aggregator : RefTimeAggregator, default identity
        Aggregates reference times, such as `rolling_sum`.
    delay_aggregator : DelayAggregator, default row_sums
        Sums over delays.
    validate : bool, default True
        Check the triangle and mask first.

    Returns
    -------
    jax.Array
        For ``"point"``, the point nowcast per reference time (row sums
        of the filled triangle). For ``"samples"``, draws of shape
        ``(draws, n_aggregated)``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import jax
    >>> import numpy as np
    >>> from bdbvhubrenewal.baselinenowcast import baselinenowcast
    >>> rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
    >>> triangle = rng.poisson(10, size=(20, 4)).astype(float)
    >>> mask = np.add.outer(np.arange(20), np.arange(4)) < 20
    >>> draws = baselinenowcast(
    ...     triangle * mask, mask, key=jax.random.key(1), draws=100
    ... )
    >>> draws.shape
    (100, 20)
    """
    values, m = coerce(triangle, mask)
    if validate:
        validate_reporting_triangle(m)
    if output_type not in ("samples", "point"):
        raise ValueError("`output_type` must be 'samples' or 'point'")
    n_req = 2 if output_type == "samples" else 0
    n_history_delay, n_retro = allocate_reference_times(
        m,
        scale_factor=scale_factor,
        prop_delay=prop_delay,
        n_min_retro_nowcasts=n_req,
        validate=False,
    )
    processed = values
    if preprocess is not None:
        processed = preprocess(values, m, validate=False)
    if delay_pmf is None:
        delay_pmf = estimate_delay(
            processed, m, n=n_history_delay, validate=False
        )
    pt = apply_delay(processed, m, delay_pmf, validate=False)
    if output_type == "point":
        return jnp.sum(pt, axis=1)
    if key is None:
        raise ValueError("`key` is required for output_type='samples'")
    if uncertainty_params is None:
        uncertainty_params = estimate_uncertainty_retro(
            processed,
            m,
            n_history_delay=n_history_delay,
            n_retrospective_nowcasts=n_retro,
            structure=structure,
            uncertainty_model=uncertainty_model,
            ref_time_aggregator=ref_time_aggregator,
            delay_aggregator=delay_aggregator,
            validate=False,
        )
    return sample_nowcasts(
        key,
        pt,
        processed,
        m,
        uncertainty_params,
        draws=draws,
        uncertainty_sampler=uncertainty_sampler,
        ref_time_aggregator=ref_time_aggregator,
        delay_aggregator=delay_aggregator,
    )

def fit_nb(x: Any, mu: Any) -> Array:
    """Fit the negative binomial size by maximum likelihood.

    R estimate_uncertainty.R:445.
    Minimises the negative log likelihood on [0.1, 1000] with Brent's
    method, as ``optimize`` does.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : array_like
        Observed counts.
    mu : array_like
        Their predicted means.

    Returns
    -------
    jax.Array
        The size, or NaN for empty input.
    """
    xa = jnp.atleast_1d(jnp.asarray(x))
    mua = jnp.atleast_1d(jnp.asarray(mu, dtype=xa.dtype))
    if xa.size == 0:
        return jnp.asarray(jnp.nan)
    if bool(jnp.any(xa < 0)):
        raise ValueError(
            "Negative values detected in observations for uncertainty "
            "estimation. fit_nb() requires non-negative integer "
            "observations."
        )
    if bool(jnp.any(mua < 0)):
        raise ValueError(
            "Negative values detected in predictions for uncertainty "
            "estimation. fit_nb() requires non-negative predictions."
        )
    assert_integerish(np.asarray(xa), "x")
    return _fit_nb_kernel(xa, mua)

def fit_by_horizon(obs: Any, pred: Any, fit_model: FitModel = fit_nb) -> Array:
    """Fit one uncertainty parameter per horizon (column).

    R estimate_uncertainty.R:291.

    Parameters
    ----------

        Their predictions, the same shape.
    fit_model : FitModel, default fit_nb
        Fits one column.

    -------

        One parameter per horizon.

    o, p = _check_obs_and_pred(obs, pred)
    return jnp.stack(
        [jnp.asarray(fit_model(o[:, i], p[:, i])) for i in range(o.shape[1])]
    )

def estimate_uncertainty(
    point_nowcast_matrices: Sequence[Any],
    truncated_reporting_triangles: Sequence[Triangle],
    retro_reporting_triangles: Sequence[Triangle],
    n: int | None = None,
    uncertainty_model: Callable[..., Array] = fit_by_horizon,
    ref_time_aggregator: RefTimeAggregator = identity,
    delay_aggregator: DelayAggregator = row_sums,
    validate: bool = True,
) -> Array:
    """Estimate uncertainty parameters per horizon.

    R estimate_uncertainty.R:71.

    Parameters
    ----------
    point_nowcast_matrices : sequence of array_like or None
        Retrospective point nowcasts, ``None`` for failed ones.
    truncated_reporting_triangles : sequence of Triangle
        The ``(triangle, mask)`` pairs those nowcasts were made from.
    retro_reporting_triangles : sequence of Triangle
        The same rows as later observed.
    n : int, optional
        Nowcasts to use. Defaults to all.
    uncertainty_model : callable, default fit_by_horizon
        Fits the parameters from observed and predicted counts.
    ref_time_aggregator : RefTimeAggregator, default identity
        ``ref_time_aggregator(values, mask)`` returns aggregated values
        and mask, where a cell is unobserved if any input cell is.
    delay_aggregator : DelayAggregator, default row_sums
        ``delay_aggregator(values)`` sums over delays, with unobserved
        cells already zero.
    validate : bool, default True
        Check the inputs first.

    Returns
    -------
    jax.Array
        One parameter per horizon.
    """
    if n is None:
        n = len(point_nowcast_matrices)
    assert_integerish(n, "n", lower=0)
    n = int(n)
    _check_list_length(point_nowcast_matrices, "point_nowcast_matrices", n)
    _check_list_length(
        truncated_reporting_triangles, "truncated_reporting_triangles", n
    )
    _check_list_length(
        retro_reporting_triangles,
        "retro_reporting_triangles",
        n,
        empty_check=False,
    )
    keep = [i for i in range(n) if point_nowcast_matrices[i] is not None]
    n_iters = len(keep)
    ncs = [jnp.asarray(point_nowcast_matrices[i]) for i in keep]
    obs_list = [coerce(*truncated_reporting_triangles[i]) for i in keep]
    rt_list = [coerce(*retro_reporting_triangles[i]) for i in keep]
    obs_list = [(v, m) for v, m in obs_list]
    if validate:
        for _, m in obs_list:
            validate_reporting_triangle(m)
        for _, m in rt_list:
            validate_reporting_triangle(m)
    if n_iters == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "No valid retrospective nowcasts were found, therefore "
            "uncertainty can not be estimated using the reporting "
            "triangle passed in."
        )
    if any(bool(jnp.any(jnp.isnan(x))) for x in ncs):
        raise ValueError("`point_nowcast_matrices` contains NAs")
    if all(m.all() for _, m in obs_list):
        warnings.warn(
            "`truncated_reporting_triangles` does not contain any NAs",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    if any(x.shape != v.shape for x, (v, _) in zip(ncs, obs_list, strict=True)):
        raise ValueError(
            "Dimensions of the first `n` matrices in `point_nowcast_matrices` "
            "and `truncated_reporting_triangles` are not the same."
        )

    # Count horizons on the aggregated retrospective triangle, which
    # equals R's daily count for rolling sums.
    n_possible_horizons = int(
        np.sum(~np.asarray(ref_time_aggregator(*rt_list[0])[1]).all(axis=1))
    )
    n_iters = _count_retro_times(
        obs_list, n_possible_horizons, ref_time_aggregator
    )
    if n_iters == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "No valid retrospective nowcast times after reference time "
            "aggregation."
        )
    if n_iters < n:
        warnings.warn(
            f"Only the first {n_iters} retrospective nowcast times were used.",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    agg_first = ref_time_aggregator(*obs_list[0])
    if agg_first[0].shape[1] != obs_list[0][0].shape[1]:
        raise ValueError(
            "`ref_time_aggregator` must return a matrix with the same "
            "number of columns as the input observations"
        )

    exp_to_add = np.zeros((n_iters, n_possible_horizons))
    already_observed = np.zeros((n_iters, n_possible_horizons))
    h = n_possible_horizons
    for i in range(n_iters):
        nowcast_i = ncs[i]
        obs_v, obs_m = obs_list[i]
        rt_v, rt_m = rt_list[i]
        agg_obs, agg_obs_m = ref_time_aggregator(obs_v, obs_m)
        agg_nc, _ = ref_time_aggregator(
            nowcast_i, np.ones(nowcast_i.shape, dtype=bool)
        )
        _, agg_rt_m = ref_time_aggregator(rt_v, rt_m)
        if h > agg_obs.shape[0]:
            raise ValueError(
                f"n_possible_horizons ({h}) exceeds matrix rows "
                f"({agg_obs.shape[0]})"
            )
        pred_h, obs_h = _horizon_sums(
            agg_nc[-h:],
            agg_obs[-h:],
            jnp.asarray(~agg_rt_m[-h:]),
            jnp.asarray(agg_obs_m[-h:]),
            delay_aggregator,
        )
        if pred_h.shape != (h,) or obs_h.shape != (h,):
            raise ValueError(
                "`delay_aggregator` must return a vector of length "
                f"{h}, got {pred_h.shape}"
            )
        exp_to_add[i] = np.asarray(pred_h)[::-1]
        already_observed[i] = np.asarray(obs_h)[::-1]

    obs = jnp.asarray(already_observed, dtype=ncs[0].dtype)
    pred = jnp.asarray(exp_to_add, dtype=ncs[0].dtype)
    _check_obs_and_pred(obs, pred)
    return jnp.asarray(uncertainty_model(obs, pred))

def estimate_uncertainty_retro(
    triangle: Any,
    mask: Any,
    n_history_delay: int,
    n_retrospective_nowcasts: int,
    structure: Any = None,
    delay_pmf: Any = None,
    validate: bool = True,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> Array:
    """Estimate uncertainty from retrospective nowcasts.

    R estimate_uncertainty_retro.R:51.

    Truncates the last ``n_retrospective_nowcasts`` rows one at a time,
    applies the reporting structure, nowcasts each and compares with
    what was later observed.
    A retrospective nowcast that raises ``ValueError`` is skipped
    (R's ``.safelydoesit``).

    Parameters
    ----------
    triangle : array_like
        Reporting triangle, reference times by delays.
    mask : array_like of bool
        True where a cell is observed.
    n_history_delay : int
        Rows used to estimate each delay.
    n_retrospective_nowcasts : int
        Retrospective nowcasts to make.
    structure : int or array_like, optional
        Reporting structure. Defaults to `get_reporting_structure`.
    delay_pmf : array_like, optional
        A delay to use instead of estimating one for each nowcast.
    validate : bool, default True
        Check the triangle and mask first.
    **kwargs
        Passed to `estimate_uncertainty`.

    Returns
    -------
    jax.Array
        One parameter per horizon.
    """
    values, m = coerce(triangle, mask)
    if validate:
        validate_reporting_triangle(m)
    if structure is None:
        structure = get_reporting_structure(m)
    n_ref = m.shape[0]
    min_ref_times_delay = int(np.sum(~m.all(axis=1))) + 1
    _validate_inputs_uncertainty(
        n_ref, min_ref_times_delay, n_history_delay, n_retrospective_nowcasts
    )
    truncated = truncate_to_rows(
        values, m, n=n_retrospective_nowcasts, validate=False
    )
    retro: list[Triangle] = []
    for v, tm in truncated:
        new_mask = apply_reporting_structure(v, tm, structure, validate=False)
        retro.append((jnp.where(jnp.asarray(new_mask), v, 0.0), new_mask))
    pmfs = (
        list(delay_pmf)
        if isinstance(delay_pmf, list)
        else [delay_pmf] * len(retro)
    )
    if len(pmfs) != len(retro):
        raise ValueError(
            "List of `delay_pmf` is not the same length as the retrospective "
            "reporting triangles."
        )
    nowcasts: list[Array | None] = []
    for (v, rm), pmf in zip(retro, pmfs, strict=True):
        try:
            nowcasts.append(
                estimate_and_apply_delay(
                    v, rm, n=n_history_delay, delay_pmf=pmf, validate=False
                )
            )
        except ValueError as err:
            warnings.warn(
                "Point nowcast matrix could not be generated for a "
                f"retrospective nowcast: {err}",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
            nowcasts.append(None)
    if all(x is None for x in nowcasts):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Errors occurred in all {len(retro)} reporting triangles. "
            "Check if input triangles have valid data structure or contain "
            "zeros in the first column."
        )
    return estimate_uncertainty(
        nowcasts,
        truncated,
        retro,
        n=n_retrospective_nowcasts,
        validate=False,
        **kwargs,
    )

def sample_nb(key: Array, pred: Any, uncertainty_params: Any) -> Array:
    """Negative binomial draws with mean ``pred`` and size ``params``.

    R sample_distrib.R:18 (``rnbinom(size, mu)``), drawn as a gamma
    mixed Poisson.

    Parameters
    ----------
    key : jax.Array
        Random key.
    pred : array_like
        Means.
    uncertainty_params : array_like
        Sizes, of length 1 or matching ``pred``.

    Returns
    -------
    jax.Array
        One draw per mean.
    """
    mu = jnp.asarray(pred, dtype=jnp.result_type(pred, jnp.float32))
    size = jnp.asarray(uncertainty_params, dtype=mu.dtype)
    if size.ndim > 0 and size.size not in (1, mu.size):
        raise ValueError(
            "`uncertainty_params` must have length 1 or match length(pred)."
        )
    size = size.reshape(()) if size.size == 1 else size.reshape(mu.shape)
    k_gamma, k_pois = jax.random.split(key)
    lam = jax.random.gamma(k_gamma, size, mu.shape, dtype=mu.dtype) * mu / size
    draw = jax.random.poisson(k_pois, lam).astype(mu.dtype)
    # R's rnbinom gives NaN for a NaN mean or size, not a count.
    ok = jnp.isfinite(mu) & jnp.isfinite(size)
    return jnp.where(ok, draw, jnp.nan)

    With a rolling aggregator the leading rows R pads with NA are
    dropped, so the columns are the last ``n_aggregated`` reference
    times.

    Parameters
    ----------
    key : jax.Array
        Random key.
    point_nowcast_matrix : array_like
        The filled triangle, as from `apply_delay`.
    triangle : array_like
        Reporting triangle, reference times by delays.
    mask : array_like of bool
        True where a cell is observed.
    uncertainty_params : array_like
        One parameter per horizon.
    draws : int, default 1000
        Number of draws.
    uncertainty_sampler : Sampler, default sample_nb
        Draws counts given a mean and the parameters.
    ref_time_aggregator : RefTimeAggregator, default identity
        Aggregates reference times.
    delay_aggregator : DelayAggregator, default row_sums
        Sums over delays.

    Returns
    -------
    jax.Array
        Shape ``(draws, n_aggregated)``.
    """
    if draws < 1:
        raise ValueError("`draws` must be at least 1")
    prep = _prepare(
        point_nowcast_matrix,
        triangle,
        mask,
        uncertainty_params,
        ref_time_aggregator,
        delay_aggregator,
    )
    keys = jax.random.split(key, draws)
    drawn = jax.vmap(lambda k: _draw(k, prep, uncertainty_sampler))(keys)
    return prep.obs_counts[None, :] + drawn

docs.title: bdbvhubrenewal.baselinenowcast.snapshots
docs.text:
Snapshot data extension (E1) and the hub week aggregator.

R's estimate_delay needs a report in every delay cell of the triangle or a right truncation. Release snapshots are published on a few days only, so most cells of the triangle are unobserved. E1 is the one named extension of the port. It takes the chain ladder ratio of sums over the cells observed in both releases of a pair and skips the others, which are not filled. Pairs of any gap share one daily log development factor per age (log_factors), and growth sums it between two ages.

Axes. counts is (n_loc, n_release, n_day), the count of onset day t in release r. observed is (n_release, n_day), True where day t has data in release r, and cut[r] is the index of the latest onset day of release r. The age of day t in release r is cut[r] - t. Pair p is releases (pairs[p], pairs[p] + 1) with step cut[r + 1] - cut[r].

docs.text:
log_factors(num: Any, den: Any, gaps: Any) -> np.ndarray

Daily log development factors shared by all pairs (extension E1).

A day of age \(a\) at release \(r\) is age \(a + s\) at release \(r + 1\), with \(s\) the pair's gap in days. Releases are batched reports, so its growth over the gap is \(\exp \sum_{j=a}^{a+s-1} g(j)\), with \(g(j) = 0\) from max_delay. The pairs of each gap are summed by age before the ratio, as baselinenowcast sums over reference times. Every gap and age with a denominator gives one equation \(\log(\sum \mathrm{num} / \sum \mathrm{den}) = \sum g\), weighted by \(\sum \mathrm{den}\), and \(g \ge 0\) is the non-negative least squares fit. With a gap of 1 only, \(g(a)\) is the log of the chain ladder factor.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default num array_like

(n_loc, n_pair, max_delay), from pair_sums.

required den array_like

(n_loc, n_pair, max_delay), from pair_sums.

required gaps array_like of int

Each pair's gap in days.

required

Returns:

Type Description ndarray

\(g\), (n_loc, max_delay).

Source code in src/bdbvhubrenewal/baselinenowcast/snapshots.py 
def log_factors(num: Any, den: Any, gaps: Any) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Daily log development factors shared by all pairs (extension E1).

    A day of age $a$ at release $r$ is age $a + s$ at release $r + 1$,
    with $s$ the pair's gap in days.
    Releases are batched reports, so its growth over the gap is
    $\exp \sum_{j=a}^{a+s-1} g(j)$, with $g(j) = 0$ from ``max_delay``.
    The pairs of each gap are summed by age before the ratio, as
    baselinenowcast sums over reference times.
    Every gap and age with a denominator gives one equation
    $\log(\sum \mathrm{num} / \sum \mathrm{den}) = \sum g$,
    weighted by $\sum \mathrm{den}$, and $g \ge 0$ is the
    non-negative least squares fit.
    With a gap of 1 only, $g(a)$ is the log of the chain ladder factor.

    Parameters
    ----------
    num, den : array_like
        ``(n_loc, n_pair, max_delay)``, from `pair_sums`.
    gaps : array_like of int
        Each pair's gap in days.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        $g$, ``(n_loc, max_delay)``.
    """
    num, den = np.asarray(num, float), np.asarray(den, float)
    gaps = np.asarray(gaps, int)
    n_loc, _, d = num.shape
    uniq = np.unique(gaps)
    member = (gaps[:, None] == uniq[None, :]).astype(float)
    n_sum = np.einsum("lpa,ps->lsa", num, member)
    d_sum = np.einsum("lpa,ps->lsa", den, member)
    age = np.arange(d)
    j = np.arange(d)[None, None, :]
    lo = age[None, :, None]
    rows = ((j >= lo) & (j < lo + uniq[:, None, None])).reshape(-1, d)
    g = np.zeros((n_loc, d))
    for n in range(n_loc):
        w = d_sum[n].ravel()
        # A zero denominator gives a row of weight 0, so no equation.
        seen = w > 0
        y = np.log(np.where(seen, n_sum[n].ravel() / np.where(seen, w, 1), 1))
        root = np.sqrt(w)
        g[n] = nnls(rows * root[:, None], y * root)[0]
    return g

def growth(g: Any, start: Any, stop: Any) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Growth $\exp \sum_{j=\mathrm{start}}^{\mathrm{stop}-1} g(j)$.

    Parameters
    ----------
    g : array_like
        Daily log factors, ``(n_loc, max_delay)``, from `log_factors`.
    start, stop : array_like of int
        Ages that broadcast together, clipped to ``0 .. max_delay``, so
        growth from ``max_delay`` on is 1.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        ``(n_loc, *shape)``.
    """
    g = np.asarray(g, float)
    d = g.shape[1]
    total = np.concatenate([np.zeros((g.shape[0], 1)), np.cumsum(g, 1)], 1)
    a, b = np.broadcast_arrays(
        np.clip(np.asarray(start, int), 0, d),
        np.clip(np.asarray(stop, int), 0, d),
    )
    return np.exp(total[:, b] - total[:, a])

Each later column \(j\) adds \((x_{j-1} + 1 - F_{j-1}) / F_{j-1}\, (F_j - F_{j-1})\), with \(x_{j-1}\) the count up to column \(j - 1\) (R .calc_modified_expectation). The \(+1\) gives a row with nothing reported yet a positive count.

def fill_row(x: Any, cdf: Any) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Return a row's count by its last column, as R's ``apply_delay``.

    Each later column $j$ adds $(x_{j-1} + 1 - F_{j-1}) / F_{j-1}\,
    (F_j - F_{j-1})$, with $x_{j-1}$ the count up to column $j - 1$
    (R ``.calc_modified_expectation``).
    The $+1$ gives a row with nothing reported yet a positive count.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : array_like
        Count reported by the first column.
    cdf : array_like
        Share reported by each column, the first that of ``x``, on the
        last axis. It broadcasts with ``x`` on the others.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        The count by the last column.
    """
    cdf = np.asarray(cdf, float)
    total = np.asarray(x, float)
    for j in range(1, cdf.shape[-1]):
        prev = cdf[..., j - 1]
        total = total + (total + 1 - prev) / prev * (cdf[..., j] - prev)
    return total

def window_pairs(cut: Any, max_delay: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Pairs whose step is at most ``max_delay``, and their steps.

    A longer step has no age inside the window to attach a factor to.
    Its releases stay in the data and in the counts.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cut : array_like of int
        Each release's cut-off day.
    max_delay : int
        Longest step kept, in days.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of numpy.ndarray
        The first release index and the step of each pair.
    """
    steps = np.diff(np.asarray(cut, dtype=int))
    keep = np.flatnonzero((steps >= 1) & (steps <= max_delay))
    return keep, steps[keep]

Hub weeks run Sunday to Saturday and carry the Saturday's date. A first week that starts after its Sunday keeps the days present. No onset day is dropped. The last week keeps only the days present, so the cut-off week is partial unless the last day is a Saturday.

def hub_week_matrix(
    first_onset: Any, n_days: int
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """0/1 matrix of hub weeks (weeks by days) and the Saturday labels.

    Hub weeks run Sunday to Saturday and carry the Saturday's date.
    A first week that starts after its Sunday keeps the days present.
    No onset day is dropped.
    The last week keeps only the days present, so the cut-off week is
    partial unless the last day is a Saturday.

    Parameters
    ----------
    first_onset : datetime.date or str
        Date of the first day.
    n_days : int
        Number of days.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of numpy.ndarray
        The matrix, weeks by days, and the weeks' Saturdays.
    """
    start = np.datetime64(first_onset, "D")
    days = start + np.arange(n_days)
    # numpy weekday: 1970-01-01 was a Thursday; Sunday = 0 below.
    dow = (days.astype(int) + 4) % 7
    sat = days + (6 - dow)
    saturdays = np.unique(sat)
    w = (sat[None, :] == saturdays[:, None]).astype(float)
    return w, saturdays
