def sample(
    self,
    infections: Array,
    first_day_dow: int,
    cutoff: int,
    hub_delay_pmf: Array,
    known: Array | None = None,
    imputed: Array | None = None,
    delay_counts: Array | None = None,
    inactive: Array | None = None,
    import_kernel: Array | None = None,
    forecast: bool = False,
    vintage: Array | None = None,
    as_of: int | None = None,
) -> ObservationSample:
    """Score or sample the two onset streams.

    Parameters
    ----------
    infections : Array
        Infections by province, `(n_total, P)`.
    first_day_dow : int
        Day of week of element 0 of the model axis.
    cutoff : int
        Vintage cut-off $T$ as an index on the model axis.
    hub_delay_pmf : Array
        The hub's empirical delay pmf for this vintage.
    known, imputed : Array, optional
        Weekly counts on the model's week grid, `(n_weeks, P)`, NaN
        where unobserved.
    delay_counts : Array, optional
        Known-onset cases by onset week and delay, pooled over
        provinces, `(n_weeks, D + 1)`.
    inactive : Array, optional
        Weekly total counts in provinces with no cases, `(n_weeks, Q)`.
    import_kernel : Array, optional
        Kernel rows from the modelled provinces to those with no
        cases, `(P, Q)`. Needed with `import_scale_rv`.
    forecast : bool, optional
        Record the sum of the final draws of both streams.
    vintage : Array, optional
        Known and imputed vintage counts, `(2, n_weeks, P)`, NaN
        where unobserved or held out. With `forecast`, the final
        draws add the cases still to be reported to these.
    as_of : int, optional
        With `forecast`, a later cut-off on the model axis: the
        "final" draws are then the counts as reported by it (the
        vintage counts plus the cases reported between the two
        cut-offs), for scoring against a later vintage as reported.

    Returns
    -------
    ObservationSample
        Sampled known counts and the weekly expected known counts.
    """
    n, n_prov = infections.shape
    alpha = jnp.asarray(self.ascertainment_rate_rv())
    alpha = alpha[:, None] if alpha.ndim == 1 else alpha
    onsets = alpha * self._predicted_obs(infections)
    delay = self.delay_rv(n_timepoints=n, first_day_dow=first_day_dow)
    if self.weekly_axis and (n % 7 or first_day_dow != self.start_dow):
        raise ValueError("Week blocks need an axis of whole weeks.")
    if self.missing_fraction_rv is None:
        pi = jnp.zeros_like(onsets)
    else:
        pi = self.missing_fraction_rv(
            n_timepoints=n, n_groups=n_prov, first_day_dow=first_day_dow
        )
    lag = self.publication_lag
    if isinstance(lag, RandomVariable):
        lag = lag()
    exp = onset_expectations(
        onsets,
        delay,
        pi,
        jnp.asarray(hub_delay_pmf),
        cutoff,
        forecast,
        publication_lag=lag,
        weekly=self.weekly_axis,
    )
    weekly = {k: self._weekly(v, first_day_dow) for k, v in exp.items()}
    if as_of is not None:
        later = onset_expectations(
            onsets,
            delay,
            pi,
            jnp.asarray(hub_delay_pmf),
            as_of,
            False,
            publication_lag=lag,
            weekly=self.weekly_axis,
        )
        weekly["known_final"] = self._weekly(later["known"], first_day_dow)
        weekly["imputed_final"] = self._weekly(
            later["imputed"], first_day_dow
        )
    for key, value in weekly.items():
        self._deterministic(f"expected_{key}", value)
    self._deterministic("expected_daily", onsets)

    if self.missing_fraction_rv is None:
        total = None
        if known is not None and imputed is not None:
            total = known + imputed
        draws = self._score(
            "total",
            self.known_noise,
            weekly["known"],
            weekly["known_final"],
            total,
        )
        final = _nowcast(draws, None if vintage is None else vintage.sum(0))
    else:
        draws = self._score(
            "known",
            self.known_noise,
            weekly["known"],
            weekly["known_final"],
            known,
        )
        imputed_draws = self._score(
            "imputed",
            self.imputed_noise,
            weekly["imputed"],
            weekly["imputed_final"],
            imputed,
            centre=None if vintage is None else vintage[1],
        )
        seen = (None, None) if vintage is None else vintage
        final = _nowcast(draws, seen[0]) + _recentred(
            imputed_draws, seen[1]
        )
        if delay_counts is not None:
            self._score_delays(
                weekly["triangle"], jnp.asarray(delay_counts)
            )
    if self.import_scale_rv is not None and import_kernel is not None:
        self._score_imports(
            onsets, jnp.asarray(import_kernel), inactive, first_day_dow
        )
    if forecast:
        self._deterministic("final_total", final)
    return ObservationSample(observed=draws[0], predicted=weekly["known"])

class MissingOnsetFraction(RandomVariable):
    r"""Time-varying probability that a case is reported without an onset.

    $$\operatorname{logit} \pi_p(t) = b(t) + \delta_p(t),$$

    from `pooled_walk`, indexed by report day $t$. With small innovation
    SDs it stays near its starting values, so it reduces to a constant
    $\pi_p$ when the data show no change.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        Prefix for the sample sites.
    initial_rv : RandomVariable
        Starting logit values, scalar or one per province.
    baseline_process, deviation_process : TemporalProcess
        Temporal processes for the national and province parts.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        initial_rv: RandomVariable,
        baseline_process: TemporalProcess,
        deviation_process: TemporalProcess,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(name=name)
        self.initial_rv = initial_rv
        self.baseline_process = baseline_process
        self.deviation_process = deviation_process

    def sample(
        self,
        n_timepoints: int,
        n_groups: int,
        first_day_dow: int | None = None,
        **kwargs: object,
    ) -> Array:
        r"""Sample $\pi_p(t)$.

        Parameters
        ----------
        n_timepoints : int
            Days to sample.
        n_groups : int
            Number of provinces.
        first_day_dow : int, optional
            Weekday of the first day, passed by PyRenew.
        **kwargs
            Ignored, for the PyRenew interface.

        Returns
        -------
        ArrayLike
            Shape `(n_timepoints, n_groups)`, values in (0, 1).
        """
        _, logit_pi = pooled_walk(
            self.baseline_process,
            self.deviation_process,
            self.initial_rv(),
            n_timepoints,
            n_groups,
            self.name,
            first_day_dow,
        )
        pi = jax.nn.sigmoid(logit_pi)
        numpyro.deterministic(self.name, pi)
        return pi

def backsample(missing: Array, pmf: Array) -> Array:
    r"""Spread missing-onset cases back from report day with a delay pmf.

    $a(s) = \sum_d m(s + d) \hat f(d)$, the hub's back-sampling in
    expectation (`bdbvhubrenewal.data.delays.expected_imputed_onsets`).
    Mass that would fall before day 0 is lost.

    Parameters
    ----------
    missing : Array
        Missing-onset cases by report day, shape `(n,)`.
    pmf : Array
        Delay pmf on 0..D.

    Returns
    -------
    Array
        Expected cases by onset day, shape `(n,)`.
    """
    n = missing.shape[0]
    return jnp.convolve(missing[::-1], pmf, mode="full")[:n][::-1]

def skew(x: Array, width: int) -> Array:
    r"""Shift row $s$ of `x` right by $s$: `out[s, s + d] = x[s, d]`.

    Pad, flatten and reshape, so the adjoint is also a reshape and needs
    no scatter. Requires `width >= n + D` for `x` of shape `(n, D + 1)`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    x : jax.Array
        Shape `(n, D + 1)`.
    width : int
        Columns of the output, at least `n + D`.

    Returns
    -------
    Array
        Shape `(n, width)`.
    """
    n, k = x.shape
    padded = jnp.pad(x, ((0, 0), (0, width + 1 - k)))
    return padded.reshape(-1)[: n * width].reshape(n, width)

def unskew(b: Array, k: int) -> Array:
    """Inverse of `skew`: `out[s, d] = b[s, s + d]` for `d < k`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    b : jax.Array
        A skewed matrix, as from `skew`.
    k : int
        Columns to return.

    Returns
    -------
    Array
        Shape `(n, k)`.
    """
    n, width = b.shape
    flat = jnp.pad(b.reshape(-1), (0, n))
    return flat.reshape(n, width + 1)[:, :k]

    onsets: Array,
    delay: Array,
    missing: Array,
    hub_delay: Array,
    cutoff: int,
    final: bool = True,
    publication_lag: ArrayLike = NO_LAG,
    weekly: bool = False,

Compute expected known and imputed onsets by the cut-off and eventually.

With \(A_{st} = f_s(t - s)\) the onset-by-report-day delay matrix and \(H_{st} = \hat f(t - s)\) the hub's back-sampling matrix, both banded and of shape (n, n + D), and \(\pi\) extended to report days past the end (last row repeated), and \(c\) the share of reports published by \(T\) (PyRenew's compute_prop_already_reported):

  • known by \(T\): \(\lambda \odot (A_{:, \le T} (c (1 - \pi))_{\le T})\);
  • missing by report day: \(M = \pi \odot A^\top \lambda\);
  • imputed by \(T\): \(H_{:, \le T} (c M)_{\le T}\), zero past \(T\).

Every term is a dense matrix product, so autodiff needs no gather or scatter adjoints. Equal to the direct version in tests/reference_kernels.py.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default onsets Array

\(\lambda_p(s)\), shape (n, P).

required delay Array

\(f_s(d)\), shape (n, D + 1).

required missing Array

\(\pi_p(t)\) by report day, shape (n, P).

required hub_delay Array

The hub's imputation pmf \(\hat f\).

required cutoff int

Cut-off day \(T\) on the same axis. Static.

required final bool

Also compute the final counts. Fitting does not need them, and skipping them saves about a fifth of the gradient cost.

True publication_lag Array

Pmf of the report to publication lag on \(0..L\). The default, all mass at lag 0, publishes every report on its report day.

NO_LAG weekly bool

The axis starts on a week boundary and has whole weeks. Then _weekly_blocks gives the same values at a cost linear, not quadratic, in the length of the outbreak.

False

Type Description dict

known and imputed by \(T\), known_final and imputed_final once all reports are in (all (n, P); equal to the counts by \(T\) when final is false), and triangle, the expected known cases by onset day and delay published by \(T\), summed over provinces, (n, D + 1).

Source code in src/bdbvhubrenewal/model/observation.py 
def onset_expectations(
    onsets: Array,
    delay: Array,
    missing: Array,
    hub_delay: Array,
    cutoff: int,
    final: bool = True,
    publication_lag: ArrayLike = NO_LAG,
    weekly: bool = False,
) -> dict[str, Array]:
    r"""Compute expected known and imputed onsets by the cut-off and eventually.

    With $A_{st} = f_s(t - s)$ the onset-by-report-day delay matrix and
    $H_{st} = \hat f(t - s)$ the hub's back-sampling matrix, both banded
    and of shape `(n, n + D)`, and $\pi$ extended to report days past the
    end (last row repeated), and $c$ the share of reports published by
    $T$ (PyRenew's `compute_prop_already_reported`):

    - known by $T$: $\lambda \odot (A_{:, \le T} (c (1 - \pi))_{\le T})$;
    - missing by report day: $M = \pi \odot A^\top \lambda$;
    - imputed by $T$: $H_{:, \le T} (c M)_{\le T}$, zero past $T$.

    Every term is a dense matrix product, so autodiff needs no gather or
    scatter adjoints. Equal to the direct version in
    `tests/reference_kernels.py`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    onsets : Array
        $\lambda_p(s)$, shape `(n, P)`.
    delay : Array
        $f_s(d)$, shape `(n, D + 1)`.
    missing : Array
        $\pi_p(t)$ by report day, shape `(n, P)`.
    hub_delay : Array
        The hub's imputation pmf $\hat f$.
    cutoff : int
        Cut-off day $T$ on the same axis. Static.
    final : bool, optional
        Also compute the final counts. Fitting does not need them, and
        skipping them saves about a fifth of the gradient cost.
    publication_lag : Array, optional
        Pmf of the report to publication lag on $0..L$. The default, all
        mass at lag 0, publishes every report on its report day.
    weekly : bool, optional
        The axis starts on a week boundary and has whole weeks. Then
        `_weekly_blocks` gives the same values at a cost linear, not
        quadratic, in the length of the outbreak.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        `known` and `imputed` by $T$, `known_final` and `imputed_final`
        once all reports are in (all `(n, P)`; equal to the counts by $T$
        when `final` is false), and `triangle`, the
        expected known cases by onset day and delay published by $T$,
        summed over provinces, `(n, D + 1)`.
    """
    if weekly:
        return _weekly_blocks(
            onsets, delay, missing, hub_delay, cutoff, final, publication_lag
        )
    n, n_d = delay.shape
    width = n + n_d - 1
    pi_ext = missing[jnp.minimum(jnp.arange(width), n - 1)]
    keep = 1 - pi_ext
    a = skew(delay, width)
    h = skew(jnp.broadcast_to(hub_delay, (n, n_d)), width)
    t1 = cutoff + 1
    a_t = a[:, :t1]
    c = compute_prop_already_reported(jnp.asarray(publication_lag), t1, 0)
    c = c[:, None]
    seen = c * keep[:t1]
    known = onsets * (a_t @ seen)
    missing_by_t = c * pi_ext[:t1] * (a_t.T @ onsets)
    imputed = h[:, :t1] @ missing_by_t
    if final:
        known_final = onsets * (a @ keep)
        imputed_final = h @ (pi_ext * (a.T @ onsets))
    else:
        known_final, imputed_final = known, imputed
    # Expected known cells published by T, summed over provinces, as a
    # band on (onset, report day), then back to (onset, delay).
    band = a_t * (onsets @ seen.T)
    band = jnp.pad(band, ((0, 0), (0, width - t1)))
    return {
        "known": known,
        "imputed": imputed,
        "known_final": known_final,
        "imputed_final": imputed_final,
        "triangle": unskew(band, n_d),
    }

Noise models for counts split into categories with known totals.

Written as PyRenew's count noise models (pyrenew.observation.noise), for the share of each total that falls in each category, such as cases by reporting delay given cases by onset week.

  • MultinomialNoise: multinomial counts. No parameters.
  • DirichletMultinomialNoise: overdispersed relative to the multinomial. Takes concentration_rv (higher concentration is less overdispersed, more multinomial-like).

class CompositionNoise(ABC):
    """
    Abstract base for noise models of counts split into categories.

    Defines how counts in each category are distributed given the
    category probabilities and the total of each row.
    """

    @abstractmethod
    def validate(self) -> None:
        """
        Check the noise parameters.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a parameter is out of range.
        """
        pass  # pragma: no cover

    @abstractmethod
    def sample(
        self,
        name: str,
        probs: ArrayLike,
        total_count: ArrayLike,
        obs: ArrayLike | None = None,
        mask: ArrayLike | None = None,
    ) -> ArrayLike:
        """
        Sample category counts given probabilities and totals.

        Parameters
        ----------
        name
            Numpyro sample site name.
        probs
            Category probabilities, the last axis summing to one.
        total_count
            Total count of each row, the shape of ``probs`` without its
            last axis.
        obs
            Observed counts for conditioning, or None for prior sampling.
        mask
            Boolean mask of the rows to include in the likelihood. If
            None, all rows are included.

        Returns

        """
        pass  # pragma: no cover

The category probabilities are Dirichlet with concentration concentration * probs, so the mean share of each category is probs and the variance of the counts exceeds the multinomial's. The log density is evaluated on the non-zero cells of the observed counts only (ObservedCellsDirichletMultinomial), which gives the same value at a fraction of the cost for sparse tables.

class DirichletMultinomialNoise(CompositionNoise):
    """
    Dirichlet-multinomial noise for overdispersed category counts.

    The category probabilities are Dirichlet with concentration
    ``concentration * probs``, so the mean share of each category is
    ``probs`` and the variance of the counts exceeds the multinomial's.
    The log density is evaluated on the non-zero cells of the observed
    counts only (``ObservedCellsDirichletMultinomial``), which gives the
    same value at a fraction of the cost for sparse tables.

    Parameters
    ----------
    concentration_rv
        Concentration (must be > 0). Higher values reduce
        overdispersion; as it grows the noise approaches the multinomial.
    """

    def __init__(self, concentration_rv: RandomVariable) -> None:
        """
        Initialize Dirichlet-multinomial noise.

        Parameters
        ----------
        concentration_rv
            Concentration (must be > 0).

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If ``concentration_rv`` is not a ``RandomVariable``.
        """
        if not isinstance(concentration_rv, RandomVariable):
            raise TypeError(
                "concentration_rv must be a RandomVariable, got "
                f"{type(concentration_rv).__name__}."
            )
        self.concentration_rv = concentration_rv

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Return string representation."""
        return (
            "DirichletMultinomialNoise("
            f"concentration_rv={self.concentration_rv!r})"
        )

    def validate(self) -> None:
        """
        Check that the concentration is positive.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the concentration is not positive.
        """
        concentration = jnp.asarray(self.concentration_rv())
        if jnp.any(concentration <= 0):
            raise ValueError(
                "DirichletMultinomialNoise: concentration must be positive, "
                f"got {concentration}"
            )

    def sample(
        self,
        name: str,
        probs: ArrayLike,
        total_count: ArrayLike,
        obs: ArrayLike | None = None,
        mask: ArrayLike | None = None,
    ) -> ArrayLike:
        """
        Sample from the Dirichlet-multinomial distribution.

        Parameters
        ----------
        name
            Numpyro sample site name.
        probs
            Category probabilities, the last axis summing to one.
        total_count
            Total count of each row.
        obs
            Observed counts for conditioning.
        mask
            Boolean mask of the rows to include in the likelihood. If
            None, all rows are included.

        Returns
        -------
        ArrayLike
            Dirichlet-multinomial counts.
        """
        concentration = self.concentration_rv()
        with numpyro.handlers.mask(mask=True if mask is None else mask):
            counts: ArrayLike = numpyro.sample(
                name,
                ObservedCellsDirichletMultinomial(
                    concentration=concentration * probs,
                    total_count=total_count,
                ),
                obs=obs,
            )
        return counts

docs.title: ObservedCellsDirichletMultinomial
docs.text:
Bases: DirichletMultinomial

Dirichlet-multinomial whose log density skips cells with no count.

With concentration \(\alpha\), \(A = \sum_k \alpha_k\) and \(n = \sum_k x_k\),

\[\log p(x) = \log B_1(A, n) - \sum_k \log B_1(\alpha_k, x_k), \qquad \log B_1(a, x) = \log\Gamma(1 + x) + \log\Gamma(a) - \log\Gamma(a + x),\]

as numpyro.distributions.DirichletMultinomial. A cell with \(x_k = 0\) adds \(\log\Gamma(\alpha_k) - \log\Gamma(\alpha_k) = 0\) exactly, with zero gradient, so only the non-zero cells are evaluated, as epinowcast scores only the observed cells. Sparse delay tables, such as delays by onset week, then cost a fraction of the dense density.

The value must be concrete, not traced, because its non-zero cells are found with NumPy. Observed data passed to a NumPyro model are. Sampling and every other method are the parent's.

Source code in src/bdbvhubrenewal/model/distributions.py 
class ObservedCellsDirichletMultinomial(dist.DirichletMultinomial):
    r"""Dirichlet-multinomial whose log density skips cells with no count.

    With concentration $\alpha$, $A = \sum_k \alpha_k$ and $n = \sum_k x_k$,

    $$\log p(x) = \log B_1(A, n) - \sum_k \log B_1(\alpha_k, x_k),
    \qquad \log B_1(a, x) = \log\Gamma(1 + x) + \log\Gamma(a)
    - \log\Gamma(a + x),$$

    as `numpyro.distributions.DirichletMultinomial`. A cell with
    $x_k = 0$ adds $\log\Gamma(\alpha_k) - \log\Gamma(\alpha_k) = 0$
    exactly, with zero gradient, so only the non-zero cells are evaluated,
    as epinowcast scores only the observed cells. Sparse delay tables,
    such as delays by onset week, then cost a fraction of the dense
    density.

    The value must be concrete, not traced, because its non-zero cells
    are found with NumPy. Observed data passed to a NumPyro model are.
    Sampling and every other method are the parent's.
    """

    def log_prob(self, value: ArrayLike) -> Array:
        """Log density of a concrete count table.

        Parameters
        ----------
        value : ArrayLike
            Counts, shape `batch_shape + (K,)`.

        Returns
        -------
        Array
            Log density, shape `batch_shape`.
        """
        x = np.asarray(value)
        alpha = jnp.broadcast_to(self.concentration, x.shape)
        k = x.shape[-1]
        rows, cols = np.nonzero(x.reshape(-1, k))
        a = alpha.reshape(-1, k)[rows, cols]
        xk = x.reshape(-1, k)[rows, cols]
        cells = gammaln(1 + xk) + gammaln(a) - gammaln(a + xk)
        n = x.sum(-1)
        total = alpha.sum(-1)
        by_row = jax.ops.segment_sum(
            cells, rows, num_segments=x.size // k
        ).reshape(n.shape)
        return gammaln(1 + n) + gammaln(total) - gammaln(total + n) - by_row

docs.text: External Rt estimates as a tempered pseudo-observation of a latent Rt.

docs.title: RtPseudoObservation
docs.text:
Bases: RandomVariable

External Rt estimates as a tempered pseudo-observation.

For groups \(G\) of provinces (the nation, or BVDOutbreakSize patches) and the day \(s_b\) of the external estimate, the model's group Rt is infection weighted over the week of \(s_b\),

\[R_G(s_b) = \frac{\sum_{p \in G} I_p R_p(s_b)}{\sum_{p \in G} I_p},\]

and the summaries enter as

\[\mu_N \sim N(\log R_N(s_b), \sigma_N / \sqrt{\alpha}), \qquad d_k \sim N(\log R_k(s_b) - \log R_N(s_b), \tau_k / \sqrt{\alpha}).\]

This is a power prior on the external summary with tempering \(\alpha\). With \(\alpha = 0\) nothing is added, so the model is unchanged. PyRenew routes only infections to observation processes, so this is a RandomVariable that the latent process calls, as it holds both Rt and infections. Its sites are {name}_log_rt_model, {name}_z and {name}_rt_obs.

Source code in src/bdbvhubrenewal/model/rt_observation.py 
class RtPseudoObservation(RandomVariable):
    r"""External Rt estimates as a tempered pseudo-observation.

    For groups $G$ of provinces (the nation, or BVDOutbreakSize patches)
    and the day $s_b$ of the external estimate, the model's group Rt is
    infection weighted over the week of $s_b$,

    $$R_G(s_b) = \frac{\sum_{p \in G} I_p R_p(s_b)}{\sum_{p \in G} I_p},$$

    and the summaries enter as

    $$\mu_N \sim N(\log R_N(s_b), \sigma_N / \sqrt{\alpha}), \qquad
    d_k \sim N(\log R_k(s_b) - \log R_N(s_b), \tau_k / \sqrt{\alpha}).$$

    This is a power prior on the external summary with tempering
    $\alpha$. With $\alpha = 0$ nothing is added, so the model is
    unchanged. PyRenew routes only infections to observation processes,
    so this is a `RandomVariable` that the latent process calls, as it
    holds both Rt and infections. Its sites are `{name}_log_rt_model`,
    `{name}_z` and `{name}_rt_obs`.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        alpha: float,
        day: int,
        groups: ArrayLike,
        values: ArrayLike,
        scales: ArrayLike,
        kinds: ArrayLike,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the pseudo-observation.

        Parameters
        ----------
        name
            Prefix for the sites.
        alpha
            Tempering, in [0, 1].
        day
            $s_b$ as a day index from the first data day.
        groups
            Boolean membership, `(G, P)`.
        values
            Log-scale summaries, `(G,)`.
        scales
            Their SDs, positive, `(G,)`.
        kinds
            0 for the national level, 1 for a deviation from it, `(G,)`.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `alpha` is outside [0, 1], `day` is negative, the shapes do
            not match, a scale is not positive or a kind is not 0 or 1.
        """
        groups = jnp.asarray(groups, dtype=float)
        values = jnp.asarray(values, dtype=float)
        scales = jnp.asarray(scales, dtype=float)
        kinds = jnp.asarray(kinds, dtype=int)
        if not 0.0 <= float(alpha) <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError(f"alpha must be in [0, 1], got {alpha}.")
        if int(day) < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"day must be non-negative, got {day}.")
        if groups.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError(
                f"groups must have shape (G, P), got {groups.shape}."
            )
        n_groups = groups.shape[0]
        for label, x in (
            ("values", values),
            ("scales", scales),
            ("kinds", kinds),
        ):
            if x.shape != (n_groups,):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{label} must have shape ({n_groups},), got {x.shape}."
                )
        if bool(jnp.any(scales <= 0)):
            raise ValueError("scales must be positive.")
        if not bool(jnp.all((kinds == 0) | (kinds == 1))):
            raise ValueError("kinds must be 0 (national) or 1 (deviation).")
        super().__init__(name=name)
        self.alpha = float(alpha)
        self.day = int(day)
        self.groups = groups
        self.values = values
        self.scales = scales
        self.kinds = kinds

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Return string representation."""
        return (
            f"RtPseudoObservation(name={self.name!r}, alpha={self.alpha}, "
            f"day={self.day}, n_groups={self.groups.shape[0]})"
        )

    def log_group_rt(
        self,
        rt: Array,
        infections: Array,
        n_init: int,
        fractions: Array | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
        """Return log $R_G(s_b)$ for each group and for the nation.

        Infections are per resident, so the weights are scaled by the
        population `fractions` to be proportional to counts.

        Parameters
        ----------
        rt
            Daily Rt by province.
        infections
            Daily infections per resident by province.
        n_init
            Seeding days at the start of the axis.
        fractions
            Population share of each province.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple[Array, Array]
            `(G,)` group values and the national scalar.
        """
        week = n_init + 7 * (self.day // 7)
        w = infections[week : week + 7].sum(axis=0)
        if fractions is not None:
            w = w * fractions
        r = rt[n_init + self.day]

        def log_rt(member: Array) -> Array:
            return jnp.log((member * w * r).sum(-1) / (member * w).sum(-1))

        return log_rt(self.groups), log_rt(jnp.ones_like(w))

    def sample(
        self,
        rt: Array,
        infections: Array,
        n_init: int,
        fractions: Array | None = None,
        **kwargs: object,
    ) -> None:
        """Add the pseudo-likelihood and record its diagnostics.

        Parameters
        ----------
        rt
            Daily Rt by province.
        infections
            Daily infections per resident by province.
        n_init
            Seeding days at the start of the axis.
        fractions
            Population share of each province.
        **kwargs
            Ignored, for the PyRenew interface.
        """
        group, national = self.log_group_rt(rt, infections, n_init, fractions)
        model = jnp.where(self.kinds == 0, group, group - national)
        numpyro.deterministic(f"{self.name}_log_rt_model", model)
        numpyro.deterministic(
            f"{self.name}_z", (self.values - model) / self.scales
        )
        if self.alpha > 0:
            numpyro.sample(
                f"{self.name}_rt_obs",
                dist.Normal(model, self.scales / jnp.sqrt(self.alpha)),
                obs=self.values,
            )

class ModelConfig:

        delays and missingness, or one total stream.

    depletion : bool

    inactive : {"imports", "none"}
        Importation-only component for provinces with no cases, or none
        (their forecasts are zero).
    report_inactive : bool

        draws go to the national `unassigned` component instead.
    effective_population : float or None

        `None` (default) estimates it with a log-normal prior; a number
        fixes it.

        uniform on $0..L$ (the default), or none. Empirical falls back to
        `PRIOR_PUBLICATION_LAG` for a vintage with no earlier pair of
        delay files. It is not the default: late rows in the delay files
        are mostly onsets recorded later for cases already counted as
        imputed, so it overstates late reporting of the total.
    max_publication_lag : int

    delay_counts : {"multinomial", "dirichlet-multinomial"}

        The Dirichlet-multinomial (default) has $1/\sqrt{\psi} \sim
        \text{HalfNormal}(0.1)$, with $\psi$ capped at $10^4$, so that
        thousands of pooled delays do not make the delay overconfident.

    truncation: bool = True

@dataclass
class Vintage:
    """One data vintage, on weeks starting `start_date` (a Sunday).

    Attributes
    ----------
    start_date : datetime.date
        First day of the first data week. Must be a Sunday.
    cutoff : int
        Data cut-off as a day index from `start_date`.
    known, imputed : numpy.ndarray
        Weekly onset counts, `(n_weeks, P)`, NaN where unobserved.
    delay_counts : numpy.ndarray
        Known-onset cases by onset week and delay, pooled over provinces,
        `(n_weeks, dmax + 1)`.
    hub_delay_pmf : numpy.ndarray
        The hub's imputation delay pmf for this release, `(dmax + 1,)`.
    populations : numpy.ndarray
        Province populations, `(P,)`.
    kernel : numpy.ndarray or None
        Row-normalised importation kernel between modelled provinces.
    horizon_weeks : int
        Forecast horizon in weeks.
    names : list of str
        Modelled province names.
    inactive : numpy.ndarray or None
        Weekly totals in provinces with no cases, `(n_weeks, Q)`.
    inactive_names : list of str
        Their names.
    import_kernel : numpy.ndarray or None
        Kernel rows from modelled to inactive provinces, `(P, Q)`.
    fit_mask : numpy.ndarray or None
        Boolean `(P,)`. False switches a province's likelihood off (it
        stays in the latent process and is still predicted).
    seed_days : numpy.ndarray or None
        Day (from `start_date`) each province's seeding starts: 0 for
        provinces with cases in the first data week, else `seed_lead` days
        before the first case week.
    bvd : dict or None
        External Rt summaries: `day` (index of $s_b$ from the first data
        day), `groups` `(G, P)`, `values`, `scales` and `kinds` `(G,)`.
    publication_lag_pmf : numpy.ndarray or None
        Empirical report to publication lag pmf on $0..180$ days
        (`data.releases.publication_lag_pmf`), or None.
    """

    start_date: dt.date
    cutoff: int
    known: np.ndarray
    imputed: np.ndarray
    delay_counts: np.ndarray
    hub_delay_pmf: np.ndarray
    populations: np.ndarray
    kernel: np.ndarray | None = None
    horizon_weeks: int = 3
    names: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    inactive: np.ndarray | None = None
    inactive_names: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    import_kernel: np.ndarray | None = None
    fit_mask: np.ndarray | None = None
    bvd: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    seed_days: np.ndarray | None = None
    publication_lag_pmf: np.ndarray | None = None

    @property
    def n_weeks(self) -> int:
        """Number of data weeks."""
        return int(self.known.shape[0])

    @property
    def n_provinces(self) -> int:
        """Number of provinces."""
        return int(self.known.shape[1])

def generation_interval(
    mean: float = GI_MEAN, sd: float = GI_SD, length: int = GEN_INT_LENGTH
) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Double interval censored Gamma generation interval on lags 1..length.

    The daily pmf on $0..L$ from `censored_pmf`, truncated at $L$. The
    renewal uses lags 1 to $L$, so lag 0 (about 0.05% of the mass) is
    dropped and the rest renormalised, as BVDOutbreakSize left-truncates
    its generation interval at one day. Computed once, in float64.
    Matches `primarycensored::dpcens(1:L, ..., L = 1, D = L + 1)`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mean, sd : float
        Gamma mean and SD in days. Default to `GI_MEAN` and `GI_SD`.
    length : int
        Longest lag in days. Defaults to `GEN_INT_LENGTH`.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Pmf on lags 1..length (PyRenew order, element 0 at lag 1).
    """
    with jax.enable_x64():
        pmf = np.asarray(censored_pmf("gamma", mean, sd / mean, length))[1:]
    return np.asarray(pmf / pmf.sum(), dtype=float)

def incubation_period(
    mean: float = INCUBATION_MEAN,
    sd: float = INCUBATION_SD,
    length: int = INCUBATION_LENGTH,
) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Double interval censored log-normal incubation period on 0..length.

    The daily pmf from infection to onset, from `censored_pmf`, truncated
    at $L$ and renormalised. Computed once, in float64.
    Matches `primarycensored::dpcens(0:L, plnorm, D = L + 1)`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mean, sd : float
        Log-normal mean and SD in days. Default to `INCUBATION_MEAN` and
        `INCUBATION_SD`.
    length : int
        Longest lag in days. Defaults to `INCUBATION_LENGTH`.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Pmf on lags 0..length.
    """
    with jax.enable_x64():
        pmf = np.asarray(censored_pmf("lognormal", mean, sd / mean, length))
    return np.asarray(pmf, dtype=float)

def seed_lead(incubation: np.ndarray) -> int:
    """Days to seed a late province before its first case week.

    The lead that puts the most onsets in the first case week from a week
    of constant seeding: the argmax over $L$ of the mass of the week-long
    seed convolved with the incubation pmf on days $L$ to $L + 6$ after
    the seed starts. At the prior mean incubation period it is 5 days,
    with 67% of onsets in the week and 9% before it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    incubation : numpy.ndarray
        Incubation pmf on lags 0..H.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        The lead in days, at most 6 so the seed starts after the
        previous case week began.
    """
    onsets = np.convolve(np.full(7, 1 / 7), incubation)
    in_week = [onsets[lead : lead + 7].sum() for lead in range(7)]
    return int(np.argmax(in_week))

def fit_weeks(data: Vintage, config: ModelConfig) -> int:
    """Weeks on the fit axis: the data weeks, extended to the BVD day.

    The BVD pseudo-observation sits on $s_b$, which can fall after the
    cut-off; the fit axis then runs to the end of that week (with no
    data) so the observation informs Rt there.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : Vintage
        The model inputs at one vintage.
    config : ModelConfig
        The model configuration.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Number of weeks.
    """
    if config.bvd and data.bvd is not None:
        return max(data.n_weeks, int(data.bvd["day"]) // 7 + 1)
    return data.n_weeks

def capped_concentration(
    name: str, inv_sqrt_rv: DistributionalVariable, floor: float
) -> TransformedVariable:
    r"""Concentration $1 / (x^2 + c)$ from $x = 1 / \sqrt{\text{conc}}$.

    The prior on $x$ shrinks towards the Poisson or multinomial limit, as
    EpiNow2's `obs_opts`, and the floor $c$ caps the concentration at
    $1 / c$: as the concentration grows the float32 log density loses
    precision, which stalls NUTS.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        Name of the concentration.
    inv_sqrt_rv : DistributionalVariable
        $x$.
    floor : float
        $c$.

    Returns
    -------
    TransformedVariable
        The concentration.
    """
    capped = ComposeTransform(
        [PowerTransform(2.0), AffineTransform(floor, 1.0), PowerTransform(-1.0)]
    )
    return TransformedVariable(name, inv_sqrt_rv, capped)

def build_model(data: Vintage, config: ModelConfig = MAIN) -> MultiSignalModel:
    """Build the province model for one vintage.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data : Vintage
        The vintage.
    config : ModelConfig
        Structural choices.

    Returns
    -------
    MultiSignalModel
        Model with one observation, `onsets`.
    """
    n_prov = data.n_provinces
    mixing = None
    if config.coupling == "gravity" and data.kernel is not None:
        mixing = Importation(
            "mixing",
            DeterministicVariable("kernel", data.kernel),
            DistributionalVariable("importation", dist.Beta(1, 100)),
        )

    effective_population = None
    if config.depletion:
        effective_population = (
            DistributionalVariable(
                "effective_population", dist.LogNormal(np.log(0.05), 0.75)
            )
            if config.effective_population is None
            else DeterministicVariable(
                "effective_population", config.effective_population
            )
        )

    builder = PyrenewBuilder()
    builder.configure_latent(
        MetapopulationInfections,
        name="latent",
        gen_int_rv=DeterministicPMF("gen_int", generation_interval()),
        # The seed is the infections per day that will be confirmed, on
        # the first data day, turned into infections per resident.
        I0_rv=TransformedVariable(
            "I0",
            DistributionalVariable(
                "initial_infections",
                dist.LogNormal(0.0, 1.5).expand([n_prov]),
            ),
            AffineTransform(0.0, 1 / (ALPHA0 * data.populations)),
        ),
        log_rt_time_0_rv=_pooled("log_rt0", n_prov, 0.0, 0.5, 0.3),
        baseline_rt_process=_named_walk(
            "rt_sd",
            0.2,
            fit_weeks(data, config),
            forecast_half_life=FORECAST_RT_HALF_LIFE,
        ),
        subpop_rt_deviation_process=_named_walk(
            "rt_dev_sd", 0.1, fit_weeks(data, config), ar=True
        ),
        mixing_rv=mixing,
        effective_population_rv=effective_population,
        seed_days=data.seed_days,
        rt_observation=RtPseudoObservation(
            "bvd", alpha=config.bvd_alpha, **data.bvd
        )
        if config.bvd and data.bvd is not None
        else None,
    )

    # Only the product of ascertainment and the effective population is
    # identified (see NOTES.md), so the starting ascertainment is fixed and
    # the effective population carries the level.
    ascertainment = IndependentAscertainment(
        name="ascertainment",
        rate_rvs={"onsets": DeterministicVariable("alpha0", ALPHA0)},
        temporal_processes={
            "onsets": _named_walk("alpha_sd", 0.03, fit_weeks(data, config))
        },
    )
    builder.add_ascertainment(ascertainment)

    pad = GEN_INT_LENGTH  # The model axis starts GEN_INT_LENGTH days early.

    def fixed(name: str, daily: np.ndarray) -> FixedTimeVarying:
        return FixedTimeVarying(
            name, np.vstack([np.repeat(daily[:1], pad, 0), daily])
        )

    if config.streams == "total":
        if config.truncation:
            rows = data.hub_delay_pmf
        else:
            rows = np.eye(1, config.dmax + 1)[0]
        delay = fixed("delay", np.tile(rows, (7 * data.n_weeks, 1)))
        missing = None
    elif not config.truncation:
        raise ValueError("Split streams always use right truncation.")
    else:
        missing = MissingOnsetFraction(
            "missing_fraction",
            # Non-centred: the imputed share pins these offsets only
            # weakly, and centred they form a funnel (R-hat 1.68).
            _pooled("logit_pi0", n_prov, -2.0, 1.0, 0.5, centred=False),
            _named_walk("pi_sd", 0.3, fit_weeks(data, config)),
            _named_walk("pi_dev_sd", 0.1, fit_weeks(data, config)),
        )

    if missing is not None:
        delay = HazardDelay(
            "delay",
            config.dmax,
            DistributionalVariable("delay_hazard0", dist.Normal(-2.0, 1.0)),
            # Real fits put the step SD at about 0.2 (2026-10-24: 90% CrI
            # 0.16 to 0.25), in the tail of a scale of 0.1, hence 0.4.
            NonCentredRandomWalk(
                DistributionalVariable("delay_smooth_sd", dist.HalfNormal(0.4))
            ),
            _named_walk("delay_sd", 0.15, fit_weeks(data, config)),
        )
    imports = None
    if config.inactive == "imports" and data.import_kernel is not None:
        imports = DistributionalVariable(
            "import_scale", dist.LogNormal(np.log(1e-3), 2.0)
        )

    n_lag = config.max_publication_lag + 1
    lag: DistributionalVariable | np.ndarray = np.ones(1)
    if config.publication_lag == "estimated":
        lag = DistributionalVariable(
            "onsets_publication_lag", dist.Dirichlet(np.ones(n_lag))
        )
    elif config.publication_lag == "fixed":
        lag = np.full(n_lag, 1 / n_lag)
    elif config.publication_lag == "empirical":
        lag = np.asarray(
            PRIOR_PUBLICATION_LAG
            if data.publication_lag_pmf is None
            else data.publication_lag_pmf,
            dtype=float,
        )

    builder.add_observation(
        OnsetStreams(
            name="onsets",
            temporal_pmf_rv=CensoredPMF(
                "infection_to_onset",
                "lognormal",
                # BVDOutbreakSize's priors (onset_incidence_model).
                DistributionalVariable(
                    "incubation_mean",
                    dist.TruncatedNormal(
                        INCUBATION_MEAN, INCUBATION_MEAN_SD, low=1.0
                    ),
                ),
                DistributionalVariable(
                    "incubation_sd",
                    dist.TruncatedNormal(
                        INCUBATION_SD, INCUBATION_SD_SD, low=1.0
                    ),
                ),
                INCUBATION_LENGTH,
            ),
            ascertainment_rate_rv=ascertainment.for_signal("onsets"),
            missing_fraction_rv=missing,
            delay_rv=delay,
            known_noise=_nb_noise("known"),
            imputed_noise=None if missing is None else _nb_noise("imputed"),
            import_scale_rv=imports,
            start_dow=SUNDAY,
            publication_lag=lag,
            delay_noise=_dm_noise()
            if config.delay_counts == "dirichlet-multinomial"
            else MultinomialNoise(),
            # The axis starts on a Sunday with whole weeks.
            weekly_axis=True,
        )
    )
    model = builder.build()
    model.config = config
    if model.latent.n_initialization_points != pad:
        raise ValueError(
            "The model axis must start a whole number of weeks early."
        )
    return model

def model_args(
    model: MultiSignalModel,
    data: Vintage,
    forecast: bool = False,
    as_of: int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Arguments for `model.run` and `Predictive` for one vintage.

    The model axis runs from `n_init` days before `start_date` to the end
    of the forecast horizon. Weekly data are padded with NaN for the
    seeding weeks and the horizon.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : MultiSignalModel
        The model, from `build_model`.
    data : Vintage
        The model inputs at one vintage.
    forecast : bool, default False
        Extend the axis by the horizon and pass the data as the vintage,
        not as observations, to draw forecasts.
    as_of : int, optional
        With `forecast`, a later cut-off in days from `start_date`, to
        draw counts as reported by it.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Keyword arguments for `MultiSignalModel.sample`.
    """
    if data.start_date.weekday() != SUNDAY:
        raise ValueError("start_date must be a Sunday.")
    n_init = model.latent.n_initialization_points
    # The fit runs on the data weeks only; the forecast pass extends the
    # axis by the horizon and draws the new steps from their priors.
    extra = fit_weeks(data, model.config) - data.n_weeks
    horizon = max(data.horizon_weeks, extra) if forecast else extra
    n_weeks = data.n_weeks + horizon

    def pad(x: np.ndarray) -> Array:
        lead = np.full((n_init // 7, x.shape[1]), np.nan)
        tail = np.full((horizon, x.shape[1]), np.nan)
        return jnp.asarray(np.vstack([lead, x, tail]))

    obs: dict[str, Any] = {
        "cutoff": n_init + data.cutoff,
        "hub_delay_pmf": jnp.asarray(data.hub_delay_pmf),
        "forecast": forecast,
        **({"as_of": n_init + as_of} if forecast and as_of is not None else {}),
    }
    use_imports = data.import_kernel is not None and (
        model.observations["onsets"].import_scale_rv is not None
    )
    if use_imports:
        obs["import_kernel"] = jnp.asarray(data.import_kernel)
    known, imputed = data.known.copy(), data.imputed.copy()
    if data.fit_mask is not None:
        known[:, ~data.fit_mask] = np.nan
        imputed[:, ~data.fit_mask] = np.nan
    if forecast:
        obs["vintage"] = jnp.stack([pad(known), pad(imputed)])
    else:
        obs |= {
            "known": pad(known),
            "imputed": pad(imputed),
            "delay_counts": jnp.nan_to_num(pad(data.delay_counts)),
        }
        if use_imports and data.inactive is not None:
            obs["inactive"] = pad(data.inactive)
    pops = np.asarray(data.populations, dtype=float)
    return {
        "n_days_post_init": 7 * n_weeks,
        "population_size": float(pops.sum()),
        "subpop_fractions": jnp.asarray(pops / pops.sum()),
        "obs_start_date": data.start_date,
        "onsets": obs,
    }

def fit(
    model: MultiSignalModel,
    data: Vintage,
    num_warmup: int = 500,
    num_samples: int = 500,
    num_chains: int = 1,
    seed: int = 0,
    target_accept: float = 0.9,
    max_tree_depth: int = 10,
) -> MultiSignalModel:
    """Fit by NUTS and return the model with its MCMC attached.

    As `MultiSignalModel.run`, but keeping `EXTRA_FIELDS` for the
    diagnostics. Chains run in parallel when devices allow.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : MultiSignalModel
        The model, from `build_model`.
    data : Vintage
        The model inputs at one vintage.
    num_warmup, num_samples : int, default 500
        Warm-up and kept iterations per chain.
    num_chains : int, default 1
        Number of chains.
    seed : int, default 0
        Random seed.
    target_accept : float, default 0.9
        NUTS target acceptance probability.
    max_tree_depth : int, default 10
        NUTS maximum tree depth.

    Returns
    -------
    MultiSignalModel
        The same model, with `model.mcmc` holding the posterior.
    """
    args = model_args(model, data)
    model.validate_data(
        **{k: v for k, v in args.items() if k != "population_size"}
    )
    kernel = NUTS(
        model.sample,
        target_accept_prob=target_accept,
        max_tree_depth=max_tree_depth,
        init_strategy=init_to_median(num_samples=15),
    )
    model.mcmc = MCMC(
        kernel,
        num_warmup=num_warmup,
        num_samples=num_samples,
        num_chains=num_chains,
        progress_bar=False,
    )
    model.mcmc.run(random.key(seed), extra_fields=EXTRA_FIELDS, **args)
    return model

seed_from_imports(
    imports: ndarray,
    rt: ndarray,
    gen_int: ndarray,
    start: int,
    rng: Generator,
) -> np.ndarray

Draw onsets in idle provinces: importations that may spread.

For one posterior draw, importations are \(m_q(t) \sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_q(t))\) from day start (the day after the cut-off; before it these provinces are observed with no cases). Each also seeds local transmission at the national reproduction number, weighted by infections, \(\ell_q(t) \sim \text{Poisson}\big(R(t) \sum_\tau g(\tau) y_q(t - \tau)\big)\) with \(y = m + \ell\). Susceptible depletion is ignored because these provinces have had no cases. \(R(t)\) is dated by infection and \(y\) by onset, so local spread here runs about an incubation period early. Their counts are near zero.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default imports ndarray

Expected importations \(\mu\), (n, Q).

required rt ndarray

National \(R(t)\), (n,).

required gen_int ndarray

Generation interval, element 0 at lag 1.

required start int

First day of local spread (the day after the cut-off).

required rng Generator

Random numbers.

required

Returns:

Type Description ndarray

Onsets \(y\), (n, Q).

Source code in src/bdbvhubrenewal/model/model.py 
def seed_from_imports(
    imports: np.ndarray,
    rt: np.ndarray,
    gen_int: np.ndarray,
    start: int,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Draw onsets in idle provinces: importations that may spread.

    For one posterior draw, importations are
    $m_q(t) \sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_q(t))$ from day `start` (the day
    after the cut-off; before it these provinces are observed with no
    cases). Each also seeds local transmission at the national
    reproduction number, weighted by infections,
    $\ell_q(t) \sim \text{Poisson}\big(R(t) \sum_\tau g(\tau)
    y_q(t - \tau)\big)$ with $y = m + \ell$. Susceptible depletion is
    ignored because these provinces have had no cases.
    $R(t)$ is dated by infection and $y$ by onset, so local spread here
    runs about an incubation period early. Their counts are near zero.

    Parameters
    ----------
    imports : numpy.ndarray
        Expected importations $\mu$, `(n, Q)`.
    rt : numpy.ndarray
        National $R(t)$, `(n,)`.
    gen_int : numpy.ndarray
        Generation interval, element 0 at lag 1.
    start : int
        First day of local spread (the day after the cut-off).
    rng : numpy.random.Generator
        Random numbers.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Onsets $y$, `(n, Q)`.
    """
    # Up to the cut-off these provinces are observed with no cases.
    y = rng.poisson(np.maximum(imports, 0.0)).astype(float)
    y[:start] = 0.0
    g = np.asarray(gen_int)
    for t in range(start, y.shape[0]):
        lags = y[max(0, t - g.size) : t][::-1]
        force = g[: lags.shape[0]] @ lags
        y[t] += rng.poisson(rt[t] * force)
    return np.asarray(y, dtype=float)

These score forecasts against a later vintage as reported, like for like.

def forecast_trajectories(
    model: MultiSignalModel,
    data: Vintage,
    n_trajectories: int = 100,
    seed: int = 1,
    posterior: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    as_of: Sequence[int] = (),
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Draw joint trajectories of final weekly onsets (known plus imputed).

    Each trajectory uses one posterior draw for every province and week,
    so national counts are the sum over provinces within a trajectory.
    Provinces with no cases get `seed_from_imports` draws when the model
    has the importation component.
    Those draws use the national Rt, dated by infection, on an onset-dated
    import series.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : MultiSignalModel
        A fitted model, from `fit`.
    data : Vintage
        The model inputs it was fitted to.
    n_trajectories : int, default 100
        Number of trajectories.
    seed : int, default 1
        Random seed.
    posterior : dict, optional
        Posterior draws to use instead of `model.mcmc`.
    as_of : sequence of int
        Later cut-offs, in days from `start_date`, to draw counts as
        reported by.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        `province`: `(n_trajectories, n_weeks + horizon, P)`,
        `inactive`: `(n_trajectories, n_weeks + horizon, Q)` (Q may be 0),
        `national`: the sum over both, `insample`, the predictive
        draws of the fitted streams at the vintage (see `ppc_draws`),
        `draw`, the index of the posterior draw behind each trajectory,
        and `as_reported`: for each later cut-off in `as_of` (days from
        `start_date`), the counts as reported by it, with the same
        posterior draws, as `{"province", "national"}`. These score
        forecasts against a later vintage as reported, like for like.
    """
    if posterior is None:
        posterior = model.mcmc.get_samples()
    n_draws = next(iter(posterior.values())).shape[0]
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    keep = rng.choice(n_draws, n_trajectories, replace=n_draws < n_trajectories)
    thinned = {k: v[keep] for k, v in posterior.items()}
    pred = Predictive(model.sample, posterior_samples=thinned)(
        random.key(seed), **model_args(model, data, forecast=True)
    )
    n_init = model.latent.n_initialization_points
    n_lead = n_init // 7
    province = np.asarray(pred["onsets_final_total"])[:, n_lead:]
    n_weeks = province.shape[1]
    inactive = np.zeros((n_trajectories, n_weeks, len(data.inactive_names)))
    if "onsets_expected_imports_daily" in pred:
        mu = np.asarray(pred["onsets_expected_imports_daily"])[:, n_init:]
        # National Rt weighted by infections (counts), not the geometric
        # mean of the province values.
        rt_p = np.asarray(pred["latent::rt_subpop"])[:, n_init:]
        w = np.asarray(pred["latent_infections_by_subpop"])[:, n_init:]
        rt = (rt_p * w).sum(-1) / np.maximum(w.sum(-1), 1e-12)
        g = np.asarray(model.latent.gen_int_rv())
        for k in range(n_trajectories):
            y = seed_from_imports(mu[k], rt[k], g, data.cutoff + 1, rng)
            inactive[k] = y[: 7 * n_weeks].reshape(n_weeks, 7, -1).sum(1)
    sites = [
        s for s in ("known", "imputed", "total") if f"onsets_{s}_obs" in pred
    ]
    insample = {
        s: np.asarray(pred[f"onsets_{s}_obs"])[:, 0, n_lead:] for s in sites
    }
    as_reported = {}
    for cut in as_of:
        later = Predictive(model.sample, posterior_samples=thinned)(
            random.key(seed + cut),
            **model_args(model, data, forecast=True, as_of=cut),
        )
        prov = np.asarray(later["onsets_final_total"])[:, n_lead:]
        # Provinces with no cases: their draws up to the later cut-off.
        idle = inactive.copy()
        first = (cut // 7) + 1
        idle[:, first:] = 0.0
        as_reported[cut] = {
            "province": prov,
            "inactive": idle,
            "national": prov.sum(axis=2) + idle.sum(axis=2),
        }
    return {
        "province": province,
        "inactive": inactive,
        "national": province.sum(axis=2) + inactive.sum(axis=2),
        "insample": insample,
        "draw": keep,
        "as_reported": as_reported,
    }

def province_distances(locations: tuple[str, ...]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Great-circle distances in km between province centres.

    Parameters
    ----------
    locations : tuple of str
        Province codes.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Symmetric, zero diagonal.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a province has no centre.
    """
    centres = province_centres().set_index("location").reindex(list(locations))
    if centres[["latitude", "longitude"]].isna().any().any():
        raise ValueError("Missing province centre.")
    lat = np.radians(centres["latitude"].to_numpy(float))
    lon = np.radians(centres["longitude"].to_numpy(float))
    a = (
        np.sin((lat[:, None] - lat[None, :]) / 2) ** 2
        + np.cos(lat[:, None])
        * np.cos(lat[None, :])
        * np.sin((lon[:, None] - lon[None, :]) / 2) ** 2
    )
    return np.asarray(2 * 6371 * np.arcsin(np.sqrt(a)), dtype=float)

def gravity_kernel(
    locations: tuple[str, ...], table: pd.DataFrame, decay_km: float = 300.0
) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Row-normalised gravity kernel between provinces.

    $K_{qp} \propto N_p \exp(-D_{qp} / \text{decay})$ for $q \ne p$,
    with populations $N$ from
    `table` and great-circle distances $D$ between the centres in
    `province_centres()`, which cover all 26 provinces.

    Parameters
    ----------
    locations : tuple of str
        Province codes.
    table : pandas.DataFrame
        Locations with a population column, as from `load_locations`.
    decay_km : float, default 300.0
        Distance scale of the decay.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Rows sum to one, zero diagonal.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a province has no centre or population, or the kernel is not
        finite.
    """
    pops = table.set_index("location")["population"].reindex(list(locations))
    if pops.isna().any():
        raise ValueError("Missing province population.")
    dist = province_distances(locations)
    k = pops.to_numpy(float)[None, :] * np.exp(-dist / decay_km)
    np.fill_diagonal(k, 0.0)
    k = k / k.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(k)):
        raise ValueError("Importation kernel is not finite.")
    return np.asarray(k, dtype=float)

def bvd_rows(
    estimates: pd.DataFrame,
    timeseries: pd.DataFrame,
    draws: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Tidy BVDOutbreakSize summaries of one release into model rows.

    Reads `province_estimates.csv`, `province_timeseries.csv` and,
    optionally, `posterior_draws.csv`. The national term uses the draws
    when given (mean and SD of log `R_T`), otherwise the `National` row
    of the time series at `as_of`. Each patch carries the time series'
    own national row as its reference, so the deviation uses one table.
    Pooled patches (`pooled = 1`) share one row and list their members.

    Parameters
    ----------
    estimates : pandas.DataFrame
        `province_estimates.csv`.
    timeseries : pandas.DataFrame
        `province_timeseries.csv`.
    draws : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        `posterior_draws.csv`.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `group`, `members`, `as_of`, `log_mean`, `log_sd`,
        `ref_log_mean`, `ref_log_sd`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        On an unknown BVD patch key.
    """
    as_of = str(estimates["as_of"].iloc[0])
    nat = timeseries.loc[
        (timeseries["area"] == "National")
        & (timeseries["date"] == as_of)
        & (timeseries["series"] == "rt")
    ].iloc[0]
    ref_mean = float(np.log(nat["median"]))
    ref_sd = float(np.log(nat["upper_90"] / nat["lower_90"]) / (2 * Z90))
    if draws is not None:
        log_rt = np.log(draws["R_T"].to_numpy(float))
        nat_mean, nat_sd = float(log_rt.mean()), float(log_rt.std(ddof=1))
    else:
        nat_mean, nat_sd = ref_mean, ref_sd
    rows = [("national", "", as_of, nat_mean, nat_sd, nat_mean, nat_sd)]
    unknown = set(estimates["province"]) - set(BVD_PROVINCES)
    if unknown:
        raises = sorted(unknown)
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown BVD patch keys {raises}.")
    by_patch = estimates.groupby("patch", sort=False)
    for patch, g in by_patch:
        members = ";".join(BVD_PROVINCES[k] for k in g["province"])
        row = g.iloc[0]
        rows.append(
            (
                str(patch),
                members,
                as_of,
                float(np.log(row["R_T_median"])),
                float(np.log(row["R_T_upper"] / row["R_T_lower"]) / (2 * Z90)),
                ref_mean,
                ref_sd,
            )
        )
    return pd.DataFrame(
        rows,
        columns=[
            "group",
            "members",
            "as_of",
            "log_mean",
            "log_sd",
            "ref_log_mean",
            "ref_log_sd",
        ],
    )

def bvd_inputs(
    rows: pd.DataFrame,
    names: list[str],
    start: dt.date,
    masked: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Map tidy BVD rows onto the modelled provinces.

    Groups with no modelled member are dropped. Leaving a province out
    drops the national term and its patch, since both carry its data.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rows : pandas.DataFrame
        Rows from `bvd_rows`.
    names : list of str
        Modelled province codes, in model order.
    start : datetime.date
        First day of the model axis.
    masked : tuple of str
        Provinces left out of the fit.

    Returns
    -------
    dict or None
        `day`, `groups`, `values`, `scales` and `kinds` for
        `RtPseudoObservation`, or None if nothing is left.
    """
    day = (pd.Timestamp(rows["as_of"].iloc[0]).date() - start).days
    groups, values, scales, kinds = [], [], [], []
    for row in rows.to_dict("records"):
        log_mean, log_sd = float(row["log_mean"]), float(row["log_sd"])
        if row["group"] == "national":
            if masked:
                continue
            member = np.ones(len(names), bool)
            value, scale, kind = log_mean, log_sd, 0
        else:
            codes = str(row["members"]).split(";")
            if set(codes) & set(masked):
                continue
            ref_mean, ref_sd = (
                float(row["ref_log_mean"]),
                float(row["ref_log_sd"]),
            )
            member = np.array([p in codes for p in names])
            value = log_mean - ref_mean
            scale = float(np.sqrt(max(log_sd**2 - ref_sd**2, BVD_TAU_MIN**2)))
            kind = 1
        if member.any():
            groups.append(member)
            values.append(value)
            scales.append(scale)
            kinds.append(kind)
    if not groups:
        return None
    return {
        "day": day,
        "groups": np.array(groups),
        "values": np.array(values),
        "scales": np.array(scales),
        "kinds": np.array(kinds),
    }

def vintage_from_tables(
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    delays: pd.DataFrame | None,
    vintage: str,
    locations: tuple[str, ...],
    table: pd.DataFrame,
    config: ModelConfig = MAIN,
    horizon_weeks: int = 3,
    masked: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    bvd: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    publication_lag: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> Vintage:
    """Build a `Vintage` from the target and delay rows of one vintage.

    The active set is the provinces in `locations` with any case in this
    vintage (every province if `config.active == "all"`). The week grid
    starts one week before national weekly onsets first reach
    `START_COUNT` and ends with the week holding the vintage's last report
    day (`data.releases.last_report`), which is also the cut-off.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Rows as in `bdbvhubrenewal.data.tidy_target`.
    delays : pandas.DataFrame or None
        Delay rows (`location`, `onset_week`, `delay`) at this vintage.
    vintage : str
        The `as_of` date.
    locations : tuple of str
        Provinces.
    table : pandas.DataFrame
        Locations table (`bdbvhubrenewal.data.load_locations`).
    config : ModelConfig
        Model configuration.
    horizon_weeks : int
        Forecast weeks after the vintage week.
    masked : tuple of str
        Provinces whose likelihood is switched off (leave one out). They
        stay in the latent process and their delays are left out.
    bvd : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        BVDOutbreakSize rows from `bvd_rows` for the release chosen for
        this vintage (`ForecastTask.auxiliary["bvd"]`).
    publication_lag : numpy.ndarray, optional
        Empirical report to publication lag pmf
        (`data.releases.publication_lag_pmf`).

    Returns
    -------
    Vintage
        Model inputs.
    """
    rows = target.loc[
        (target["vintage"] == vintage) & target["location"].isin(locations)
    ]
    wide = rows.pivot_table(
        index="target_end_date",
        columns="location",
        values=["observed", "imputed", "total"],
        aggfunc="sum",
    ).fillna(0)
    totals_wide = cast(pd.DataFrame, wide["total"])
    cases = totals_wide.sum(axis=0)
    if config.active == "all":
        active = tuple(locations)
    else:
        active = tuple(p for p in locations if cases.get(p, 0) > 0)
    idle = tuple(p for p in locations if p not in active)
    national = totals_wide.reindex(columns=list(active)).fillna(0).sum(axis=1)
    counts_by_week = national.to_numpy()
    threshold = min(START_COUNT, counts_by_week.max())
    big = int(np.argmax(counts_by_week >= threshold))
    first = _saturday(str(national.index[max(0, big - 1)]))
    start = first - dt.timedelta(days=6)
    cutoff = (last_report(vintage, str(rows["kind"].iloc[0])) - start).days
    n_weeks = cutoff // 7 + 1
    weeks = [
        (first + dt.timedelta(weeks=i)).isoformat() for i in range(n_weeks)
    ]

    def grid(column: str, locs: tuple[str, ...]) -> np.ndarray:
        out = cast(pd.DataFrame, wide[column]).reindex(
            index=weeks, columns=list(locs)
        )
        return out.fillna(0).to_numpy(dtype=float)

    counts = np.zeros((n_weeks, config.dmax + 1))
    if delays is not None and len(delays):
        # Known onsets count every case, so negative delays go to 0 and
        # delays past dmax to dmax, the last cell of the hazard pmf,
        # rather than leaving the delay counts short of the known stream.
        keep = delays.loc[
            (
                delays["location"].isin(active)
                if active != (NATIONAL,)
                else delays["location"].ne("")
            )
            & ~delays["location"].isin(masked)
        ]
        week = np.array(
            [
                (pd.Timestamp(w).date() - first).days // 7
                for w in keep["onset_week"]
            ],
            dtype=int,
        )
        ok = (week >= 0) & (week < n_weeks)
        delay = np.clip(keep["delay"].to_numpy(), 0, config.dmax)
        np.add.at(counts, (week[ok], delay[ok]), 1)

    known, imputed = grid("observed", active), grid("imputed", active)
    totals = known + imputed
    pops = table.set_index("location").loc[list(active), "population"]
    names = list(active)
    if config.national:
        known = known.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
        imputed = imputed.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
        pops = pd.Series([pops.sum()])
        names = [active[0] if len(active) == 1 else NATIONAL]
    kernel = None if len(names) == 1 else gravity_kernel(active, table)
    import_kernel, inactive = None, None
    if idle and not config.national:
        import_kernel = gravity_kernel(active + idle, table)[
            : len(active), len(active) :
        ]
        inactive = grid("total", idle)
    return Vintage(
        start_date=start,
        cutoff=cutoff,
        known=known,
        imputed=imputed,
        delay_counts=counts,
        hub_delay_pmf=hub_delay_pmf(vintage, config.dmax),
        populations=pops.to_numpy(dtype=float),
        kernel=kernel,
        horizon_weeks=horizon_weeks,
        names=names,
        inactive=inactive,
        inactive_names=[] if config.national else list(idle),
        import_kernel=import_kernel,
        fit_mask=np.array([p not in masked for p in names]),
        bvd=None
        if bvd is None or config.national
        else bvd_inputs(bvd, names, start, masked),
        seed_days=None if config.national else _seed_days(totals),
        publication_lag_pmf=publication_lag,
    )

def idle_draws(
    counts: np.ndarray, n_weeks: int, n: int, rng: np.random.Generator
) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Draws for a province with too few cases for its own fit.

    Callers floor them at the count reported (`renewalsp`).

    Weekly counts are Poisson with rate $\lambda \sim
    \text{Gamma}(1/2 + \sum y, w)$ over the $w$ weeks seen (Jeffreys
    prior), so each trajectory has one rate.

    Parameters
    ----------
    counts : numpy.ndarray
        Weekly counts seen so far.
    n_weeks : int
        Weeks to draw.
    n : int
        Number of draws.
    rng : numpy.random.Generator
        Random number generator.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Draws, `(n, n_weeks)`.
    """
    shape = 0.5 + np.nansum(counts)
    rate = rng.gamma(shape, 1.0 / max(len(counts), 1), size=n)
    return rng.poisson(rate[:, None] * np.ones((1, n_weeks))).astype(float)

def model_colour(name: str, models: Sequence[str], mode: str = "light") -> str:
    """Return a model's fixed colour.

    A model in `MODEL_STYLE` has its own colour. Others, such as test
    stand-ins, take the colours after the last one `MODEL_STYLE` uses, in
    their order in `models`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        The model.
    models : sequence of str
        All models shown.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        A hex colour.
    """
    palette = MODEL_COLOURS[mode]
    if name in MODEL_STYLE:
        slot = MODEL_STYLE[name][0]
        return THEMES[mode]["data"] if slot is None else palette[slot]
    others = [m for m in models if m not in MODEL_STYLE]
    return palette[(_FREE_SLOT + others.index(name)) % len(palette)]

def bar_style(colour: str, dash: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Bar keywords: filled when solid, hatched in the colour otherwise.

    Bars cannot show a dash, so a variant is hatched to keep it apart
    from its parent.
    """
    if not dash:
        return {"color": colour}
    return {"facecolor": "none", "edgecolor": colour, "hatch": "////"}

def save_light_dark(
    make: Callable[..., Figure], path: Path | str
) -> list[Path]:
    """Save a figure in light and dark versions.

    Parameters
    ----------
    make : callable
        Takes the keyword `mode` (`"light"` or `"dark"`) and returns a
        figure.
    path : pathlib.Path or str
        Output path for the light version, such as `figures/x.svg`. The
        dark version gets a `-dark` suffix.

    Returns
    -------
    list of pathlib.Path
        The two paths written.
    """
    out = Path(path)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    paths = [out, out.with_name(f"{out.stem}-dark{out.suffix}")]
    for mode, p in zip(("light", "dark"), paths, strict=True):
        with theme(mode):
            fig = make(mode=mode)
            fig.savefig(p, bbox_inches="tight")
        plt.close(fig)
    return paths

def plot_downward_updates(
    target: pd.DataFrame, zones: pd.DataFrame, mode: str = "light"
) -> Figure:
    """Plot how often and how much counts fell between releases.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Real target rows.
    zones : pandas.DataFrame
        Health zone counts, with columns `vintage`, `location`,
        `target_end_date` and `total`.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        Columns for the country, the provinces and the health zones, and
        rows for the share of place-weeks that fell and the falls as a
        share of all change, by the week's age at the earlier release.
        One line per pair of consecutive releases.
    """
    nat = target["location"] == "CD"
    updates = pd.concat(
        [
            release_updates(target.loc[nat]).assign(scale="Country"),
            release_updates(target.loc[~nat]).assign(scale="Provinces"),
            release_updates(zones).assign(scale="Health zones"),
        ]
    )
    edges = list(AGE_BINS)
    labels = [
        str(lo) if hi - lo == 1 else f"{lo}-{hi - 1}"
        for lo, hi in pairwise(edges)
    ] + [f"{edges[-1]}+"]
    updates["age"] = pd.cut(
        updates["weeks_before"],
        [*edges, np.inf],
        right=False,
        labels=labels,
    )
    updates["pair"] = updates["previous"] + " to " + updates["vintage"]
    summary = downward_summary(updates, ("scale", "pair", "age"))
    pairs = sorted(summary["pair"].unique())
    palette = MODEL_COLOURS[mode]
    scales = ["Country", "Provinces", "Health zones"]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        2,
        3,
        figsize=(9.6, 5.2),
        sharex=True,
        sharey="row",
        squeeze=False,
        layout="constrained",
    )
    x = np.arange(len(labels))
    for col, scale in enumerate(scales):
        for i, pair in enumerate(pairs):
            pick = (summary["scale"] == scale) & (summary["pair"] == pair)
            r = summary.loc[pick].set_index("age").reindex(labels)
            for row, metric in enumerate(("share_fell", "downward_share")):
                axes[row][col].plot(
                    x,
                    r[metric],
                    marker="o",
                    ms=4,
                    lw=1.2,
                    color=palette[i % len(palette)],
                    label=pair,
                )
        axes[0][col].set_title(scale)
        axes[1][col].set_xticks(x, labels)
        axes[1][col].set_xlabel("Weeks old at the earlier release")
    axes[0][0].set_ylabel("Share of place-weeks\nthat fell")
    axes[1][0].set_ylabel("Falls as a share\nof all change")
    handles, names = axes[0][0].get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(
        handles,
        names,
        loc="outside lower center",
        ncol=len(pairs),
        title="Releases compared",
        title_fontsize=8,
    )
    return fig

def baseline_share(
    daily: pd.DataFrame, vintage: str, locations: Sequence[str]
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return randomwalknowcast's share reported by age at one release.

    The share is one over the growth to final of `plot_delay_check`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    daily : pandas.DataFrame
        Daily onsets by release, as for `make_tasks`.
    vintage : str
        The release.
    locations : sequence of str
        Places.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `age` (days since onset) and `share`.
    """
    from bdbvhubrenewal.data.snapshots import snapshot_arrays
    from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.chain import Settings, build_origin

    snap = snapshot_arrays(daily, vintage, tuple(locations))
    origin = build_origin(snap, Settings(), errors=False)
    age = int(snap.cut[origin.o]) - np.arange(snap.week.size)
    seen = (age >= 0) & (age < origin.settings.max_delay)
    return pd.concat(
        [
            pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "location": loc,
                    "age": age[seen],
                    "share": 1 / origin.growth[j, seen],
                }
            ).sort_values("age")
            for j, loc in enumerate(snap.locations)
        ],
        ignore_index=True,
    )

def plot_renewal_delay(
    summary: pd.DataFrame,
    baseline: pd.DataFrame,
    names: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    mode: str = "light",
) -> Figure:
    """Plot the renewal models' learnt delay at their latest origin.

    Parameters
    ----------
    summary : pandas.DataFrame
        `delay-summary.csv` rows (`bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.renewal.
        delay_summary` with `model`, `vintage` and `location`).
    baseline : pandas.DataFrame
        `baseline_share` at the same release, with the country as
        `NATIONAL` for the fits pooled over provinces.
    names : mapping, optional
        Location names by code.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        A row per fit: pooled over provinces, then each province a
        single-patch model fits. Left: the share of onsets in the last week
        reported by each day since onset, to the day before the longest
        delay, with randomwalknowcast's share for the same place. Right:
        the mean delay by onset week. Lines are medians and bands 90%
        intervals.
    """
    names = dict(names or {})
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    latest = summary.groupby("model")["vintage"].transform("max")
    rows = summary.loc[summary["vintage"] == latest]
    models = list(dict.fromkeys(rows["model"]))
    places = list(dict.fromkeys(rows["location"]))
    places.sort(key=lambda p: (p != "pooled", names.get(p, p)))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        len(places),
        2,
        figsize=(7.2, 2.1 * len(places)),
        squeeze=False,
        layout="constrained",
    )
    last_day = int(pd.to_numeric(rows["x"], errors="coerce").max())
    for (left, right), place in zip(axes, places, strict=True):
        here = rows.loc[rows["location"] == place]
        fitted = list(dict.fromkeys(here["model"]))
        where = NATIONAL if place == "pooled" else place
        title = (
            "All provinces" if place == "pooled" else names.get(place, place)
        )
        left.set_title(f"{title}: {', '.join(fitted)}", fontsize=8, loc="left")
        base = baseline.loc[baseline["location"] == where]
        left.plot(
            base["age"],
            base["share"],
            color=ink["data"],
            ls="--",
            lw=1,
            label="randomwalknowcast",
        )
        lines = []
        for model in fitted:
            fit = here.loc[here["model"] == model]
            colour = model_colour(model, models, mode)
            share = fit.loc[fit["quantity"] == "reported_share"]
            day = pd.to_numeric(share["x"])
            share = share.loc[day < last_day]
            day = day.loc[share.index]
            delay = fit.loc[fit["quantity"] == "mean_delay"]
            week = pd.to_datetime(delay["x"])
            for ax, x, q in ((left, day, share), (right, week, delay)):
                ax.fill_between(x, q["q5"], q["q95"], color=colour, alpha=0.12)
                lines.append((ax, x, q["q50"], colour, model))
        # Later models are drawn first and wider, so a line that coincides
        # with another stays visible under it.
        width = {m: 1.2 + 1.2 * i for i, m in enumerate(fitted)}
        for ax, x, y, colour, model in reversed(lines):
            ax.plot(x, y, color=colour, lw=width[model], label=model)
        left.set_ylim(0, 1)
        left.set_ylabel("Share reported")
        right.set_ylabel("Mean delay (days)")
        _date_axis(right)
    axes[-1][0].set_xlabel("Days since onset, last onset week")
    vintage = ", ".join(sorted(rows["vintage"].astype(str).unique()))
    fig.suptitle(f"Fits at {vintage}", fontsize=9)
    handles: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for ax in axes[:, 0]:
        for h, label in zip(*ax.get_legend_handles_labels(), strict=True):
            handles.setdefault(label, h)
    fig.legend(
        list(handles.values()),
        list(handles),
        loc="outside lower center",
        ncol=len(handles),
        fontsize=7,
        frameon=False,
    )
    return fig
