def plot_simulation(parameters: pd.DataFrame, mode: str = "light") -> Figure:
    """Plot the true parameters of a simulated outbreak.

    Parameters
    ----------
    parameters : pandas.DataFrame
        `SimulatedOutbreak.parameters`.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        Panels for onsets, Rt, susceptible fraction, ascertainment,
        missing fraction and mean delay.
    """
    panels = [
        ("onsets", "Daily onsets"),
        ("rt", "Rt"),
        ("susceptible_fraction", "Susceptible fraction"),
        ("ascertainment", "Ascertainment"),
        ("missing", "Share missing onset"),
        ("delay_mean", "Mean delay (days)"),
    ]
    fig, axes = _grid(len(panels), 3, width=3.0, height=2.2)
    palette = MODEL_COLOURS[mode]
    locs = list(parameters["location"].unique())
    for ax, (col, title) in zip(axes, panels, strict=True):
        shared = col in ("ascertainment", "missing", "delay_mean")
        for i, loc in enumerate(locs[:1] if shared else locs):
            p = parameters.loc[parameters["location"] == loc]
            ax.plot(p["date"], p[col], color=palette[i], lw=1.5, label=loc)
        ax.set_title(title)
        _date_axis(ax)
    axes[0].legend()
    return fig

def plot_location_grid(
    forecasts: pd.DataFrame,
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    locations: Sequence[str],
    models: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    truth_vintage: str | None = None,
    max_horizon: int | None = None,
    weeks_before: int = 10,
    ncol: int = 2,
    mode: str = "light",
    complete_after_weeks: int = 3,
) -> Figure:
    """Plot one origin's forecasts as a grid with a panel per location.

    Parameters
    ----------
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `run_forecasts` for one origin.
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Target rows holding the origin and the truth vintage.
    locations : sequence of str
        Locations to show, one panel each.
    models : sequence of str, optional
        Models in registry order. Defaults to those in `forecasts`.
    truth_vintage : str, optional
        Vintage drawn as later data. Defaults to the latest real vintage.
    max_horizon : int, optional
        Last horizon drawn. `-1` shows the nowcast alone, without the
        reference week or the forecast weeks.
    weeks_before : int
        Weeks of data shown before the reference date.
    ncol : int
        Panels per row.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.
    complete_after_weeks : int
        Weeks after which a week of the later data counts as complete.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        Per panel, the data at the origin (dashed), the later data
        (solid) and each model's trajectories, intervals and median.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from bdbvhubrenewal.reporting.plots import (
    ...     plot_location_grid, save_light_dark
    ... )
    >>> fig = plot_location_grid(forecasts, real, ["CD", "CD-IT"])
    >>> save_light_dark(
    ...     lambda mode: plot_location_grid(
    ...         forecasts, real, ["CD"], mode=mode
    ...     ),
    ...     "figures/grid.svg",
    ... )
    """
    fc = forecasts
    if max_horizon is not None:
        fc = fc.loc[fc["horizon"] <= max_horizon]
    models = list(models or fc["model"].unique())
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    truth_v = truth_vintage or real["vintage"].max()
    vintage = fc["vintage"].iloc[0]
    ref = pd.Timestamp(fc["reference_date"].iloc[0])
    end = pd.Timestamp(fc["target_end_date"].max())
    start = ref - pd.Timedelta(weeks=weeks_before)
    names = _names(real)
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    cut = _incomplete_after(truth_v, complete_after_weeks)
    fig, axes = _grid(len(locations), ncol, width=3.6, height=2.5)
    shown_data = [(truth_v, "-", f"Data {truth_v}")]
    if vintage != truth_v:
        shown_data.append((vintage, "--", "Data at the origin"))
    for ax, loc in zip(axes, locations, strict=True):
        top: list[float] = []
        for v, style, lab in shown_data:
            rows = real.loc[(real["vintage"] == v) & (real["location"] == loc)]
            x = pd.to_datetime(rows["target_end_date"])
            sel = (x >= start) & (x <= end)
            top.append(float(rows["total"][sel].max()) if sel.any() else 0.0)
            if style == "-":
                _plot_data(
                    ax,
                    x[sel],
                    rows["total"][sel],
                    cut,
                    ink["data"],
                    lab,
                    ls=style,
                    lw=1.2,
                )
            else:
                ax.plot(
                    x[sel],
                    rows["total"][sel],
                    color=ink["data"],
                    ls=style,
                    lw=1.2,
                    label=lab,
                )
        for m in models:
            s = fc.loc[(fc["location"] == loc) & (fc["model"] == m)]
            if not s.empty:
                _draw_forecast(
                    ax, s, model_colour(m, models, mode), model_dash(m), m
                )
                _fit_y(ax, s, top)
        ax.axvline(mdates.date2num(ref), color=ink["muted"], lw=0.8, ls=":")
        _shade_incomplete(ax, cut, mode)
        ax.set_title(f"{names.get(loc, loc)} ({loc})")
        ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.WeekdayLocator(interval=4))
        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%d %b"))
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Cases by onset week")
    _legend_below(fig, axes[0])
    return fig

def plot_delay_check(
    daily: pd.DataFrame,
    vintage: str,
    locations: Sequence[str],
    mode: str = "light",
) -> Figure:
    r"""Plot the delay and spread each place uses at one release.

    Parameters
    ----------
    daily : pandas.DataFrame
        Daily onsets by release, as for `make_tasks`.
    vintage : str
        The release, the origin of the nowcast.
    locations : sequence of str
        Places to show.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        Left, the growth $G$ from each age in days to final, chained over
        the release gap, on a log scale. Middle, the dispersion
        $1 / \phi_k$ of the new reports by weeks back, with the number of
        errors behind it. Right, the removal rate $b_k$.
        A place's label says at how many ages it uses its own delay
        factor and not its parent's.
    """
    from bdbvhubrenewal.data.snapshots import snapshot_arrays
    from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.chain import Settings, build_origin

    snap = snapshot_arrays(daily, vintage, tuple(locations))
    origin = build_origin(snap, Settings(), errors=True)
    assert origin.size is not None
    assert origin.removal is not None
    assert origin.obs_n is not None
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    palette = MODEL_COLOURS[mode]
    age = int(snap.cut[origin.o]) - np.arange(snap.week.size)
    seen = (age >= 0) & (age < origin.settings.max_delay)
    fig, (left, mid, right) = plt.subplots(
        1, 3, figsize=(9.6, 3.2), layout="constrained"
    )
    drawn: set[tuple[float, ...]] = set()
    for i, loc in enumerate(locations):
        j = snap.locations.index(loc)
        own = origin.fit.own[j]
        kind = f"own at {int(own.sum())} of {own.size} ages"
        colour = palette[i % len(palette)]
        order = np.argsort(age[seen])
        left.plot(
            age[seen][order],
            origin.growth[j, seen][order],
            color=colour,
            lw=1.2,
            label=f"{loc} ({kind})",
        )
        row = tuple(np.round([*origin.size[j], *origin.removal[j]], 6))
        if row not in drawn:
            drawn.add(row)
            k = np.arange(origin.size.shape[1])
            style = {"color": colour, "ms": 3, "lw": 1}
            label = f"{loc} and places using it"
            mid.plot(k, 1 / origin.size[j], "o-", label=label, **style)
            right.plot(k, origin.removal[j], "o-", **style)
    left.set_yscale("log")
    left.set_xlabel("Age of the onset day (days)")
    left.set_ylabel("Growth to final")
    for ax in (mid, right):
        ax.set_xlabel("Weeks back")
    mid.set_ylabel("Dispersion of new reports, 1 / size")
    right.set_ylabel("Removal rate")
    n_err = int(origin.obs_n.max())
    mid.set_title(f"At most {n_err} errors behind a fit", fontsize=8)
    mid.legend(fontsize=7, frameon=False)
    left.axhline(1, color=ink["muted"], lw=0.8, ls=":")
    left.legend(fontsize=7, frameon=False)
    return fig

def plot_forecasts(
    forecasts: pd.DataFrame,
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    location: str,
    models: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    kind: str = "real",
    truth_vintage: str | None = None,
    weeks_before: int = 10,
    mode: str = "light",
    complete_after_weeks: int = 3,
) -> Figure:
    """Plot forecasts against data at the time and later data, by date.

    Parameters
    ----------
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `bdbvhubrenewal.evaluation.backtest.run_forecasts`.
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Target rows holding each forecast's vintage and the truth vintage.
    location : str
        Location to show.
    models : sequence of str, optional
        Models in registry order. Defaults to those in `forecasts`.
    kind : str
        Vintage kind to show.
    truth_vintage : str, optional
        Vintage drawn as later data. Defaults to the latest real vintage.
    weeks_before : int
        Weeks of data shown before each forecast.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.
    complete_after_weeks : int
        Weeks after which a week of the later data counts as complete.
        Later weeks are shaded and their points drawn hollow.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        One panel per reference date: data at the time (dashed), later
        data (solid) and each model's sample trajectories, 50% and 90%
        intervals and median.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from bdbvhubrenewal.reporting.plots import plot_forecasts
    >>> fig = plot_forecasts(forecasts, real, "CD")  # from `run_forecasts`
    >>> fig.savefig("national.png")
    """
    fc = forecasts.loc[
        (forecasts["location"] == location) & (forecasts["kind"] == kind)
    ]
    models = list(models or fc["model"].unique())
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    truth_v = truth_vintage or real["vintage"].max()
    truth = real.loc[
        (real["vintage"] == truth_v) & (real["location"] == location)
    ]
    refs = sorted(fc["reference_date"].unique())
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    cut = _incomplete_after(truth_v, complete_after_weeks)
    fig, axes = _grid(len(refs), 4, width=3.0, height=2.3)
    for ax, ref in zip(axes, refs, strict=True):
        top: list[float] = []
        f_ref = fc.loc[fc["reference_date"] == ref]
        vintage = f_ref["vintage"].iloc[0]
        start = pd.Timestamp(ref) - pd.Timedelta(weeks=weeks_before)
        end = pd.Timestamp(f_ref["target_end_date"].max())
        at_time = target.loc[
            (target["kind"] == kind)
            & (target["vintage"] == vintage)
            & (target["location"] == location)
        ]
        shown = [(truth, "-", f"Data {truth_v}")]
        if vintage != truth_v:
            shown.append((at_time, "--", "Data at the time"))
        for rows, style, lab in shown:
            x = pd.to_datetime(rows["target_end_date"])
            sel = (x >= start) & (x <= end)
            top.append(float(rows["total"][sel].max()) if sel.any() else 0.0)
            if style == "-":
                _plot_data(
                    ax,
                    x[sel],
                    rows["total"][sel],
                    cut,
                    ink["data"],
                    lab,
                    ls=style,
                    lw=1.2,
                )
                continue
            ax.plot(
                x[sel],
                rows["total"][sel],
                color=ink["data"],
                ls=style,
                lw=1.2,
                label=lab,
            )
        drawn = False
        for m in models:
            s = f_ref.loc[f_ref["model"] == m]
            if not s.empty:
                _draw_forecast(
                    ax, s, model_colour(m, models, mode), model_dash(m), m
                )
                _fit_y(ax, s, top)
                drawn = True
        if not drawn:
            ax.text(
                0.5,
                0.92,
                "No forecast from this origin",
                transform=ax.transAxes,
                ha="center",
                fontsize=7,
                color=ink["muted"],
            )
        ax.axvline(
            mdates.date2num(pd.Timestamp(ref)),
            color=ink["muted"],
            lw=0.8,
            ls=":",
        )
        _shade_incomplete(ax, cut, mode)
        ax.set_title(f"{location}, origin {vintage}")
        ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.WeekdayLocator(interval=4))
        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%d %b"))
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Cases by onset week")
    _legend_below(fig, axes[0])
    return fig

def plot_nowcast(
    location: str,
    vintage: str | None = None,
    models: Sequence[str] = ("randomwalk",),
    target: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    delays: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    forecasts: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    weeks_before: int = 16,
    mode: str = "light",
    complete_after_weeks: int = 3,
    data_dir: Path | str | None = None,
    config_path: Path | str = "config/backtest.toml",
    ax: Axes | None = None,
) -> Figure:
    """Plot the nowcast and forecast for one location from one vintage.

    If `forecasts` is not given, the models are run on the vintage.
    This is the figure the submission pull request embeds.

    Parameters
    ----------
    location : str
        Location to show, such as `"CD-IT"` or `"CD"`.
    vintage : str, optional
        Real vintage to forecast from. Defaults to the latest.
    models : sequence of str
        Registered models to show.
    target, delays : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        Tidy tables. Loaded from `data_dir` if not given.
    forecasts : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        Output of `run_forecasts` for this vintage.
    weeks_before : int
        Weeks of data shown before the forecast.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.
    complete_after_weeks : int
        Weeks after which a week counts as complete.
        Later weeks are shaded and their bars drawn hollow.
    data_dir : pathlib.Path or str, optional
        Directory of the tidy tables.
    config_path : pathlib.Path or str
        Backtest settings, for horizons and samples.
    ax : matplotlib.axes.Axes, optional
        Axes to draw on, for a grid of locations. A new figure if None.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        Observed, imputed and total cases by onset week, and each model's
        sample trajectories, 50% and 90% intervals and median.
    """
    from bdbvhubrenewal.data import load_daily, load_delays, load_target
    from bdbvhubrenewal.evaluation.backtest import (
        load_config,
        make_tasks,
        run_forecasts,
    )
    from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.base import get_model

    target = load_target(data_dir) if target is None else target
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    vintage = vintage or str(real["vintage"].max())
    rows = real.loc[real["vintage"] == vintage]
    if forecasts is None:
        delays = load_delays(data_dir) if delays is None else delays
        config = load_config(config_path)
        daily = load_daily(data_dir)
        tasks = make_tasks(rows, delays, config, daily=daily)
        forecasts = run_forecasts([get_model(m) for m in models], tasks)
    fc = forecasts.loc[
        (forecasts["location"] == location) & (forecasts["vintage"] == vintage)
    ]
    ref = pd.Timestamp(fc["reference_date"].iloc[0])
    data = rows.loc[rows["location"] == location].copy()
    data["date"] = pd.to_datetime(data["target_end_date"])
    start = ref - pd.Timedelta(days=7 * weeks_before)
    data = data.loc[data["date"] >= start]
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    if ax is None:
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.6), layout="constrained")
    else:
        fig = cast(Figure, ax.get_figure())
    cut = _incomplete_after(vintage, complete_after_weeks)
    done = data["date"] <= cut
    for part, hollow in ((data.loc[done], False), (data.loc[~done], True)):
        for col, colour, label, base in (
            ("observed", ink["axis"], "Known onset", None),
            ("imputed", ink["muted"], "Imputed onset", "observed"),
        ):
            ax.bar(
                part["date"],
                part[col],
                width=5,
                bottom=None if base is None else part[base],
                color="none" if hollow else colour,
                edgecolor=colour,
                label=label if not hollow else None,
            )
    for m in models:
        s = fc.loc[fc["model"] == m]
        _draw_forecast(
            ax, s, model_colour(m, list(models), mode), model_dash(m), m
        )
    ax.axvline(mdates.date2num(ref), color=ink["muted"], lw=0.8, ls=":")
    _shade_incomplete(ax, cut, mode)
    names = _names(rows)
    ax.set_title(
        f"{names.get(location, location)} ({location}): vintage {vintage}, "
        f"reference date {ref.date()}"
    )
    ax.set_ylabel("Confirmed cases by onset week")
    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%d %b"))
    ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper left")
    return fig

def comparison_label(model: str, source: str) -> str:
    """Label a model in the hub comparison.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : str
        Hub model id or our registry name.
    source : str
        `hub`, `submitted` (our file in the hub, by hub id), or the kind of
        vintage our main build used.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        A hub team's id, `<hub id> (submitted)` or `<model> (main build)`.
    """
    if source == "hub":
        return model
    if source == "submitted":
        return f"{model} (submitted)"
    return f"{model} (main build)"

def comparison_colours(
    ours: Mapping[str, str],
    submitted: Mapping[str, str],
    teams: Sequence[str],
) -> dict[str, tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """Return the light colour, dark colour and dash of each comparison series.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ours : mapping of str to str
        Label of each of our main builds to its registry name.
    submitted : mapping of str to str
        Label of each of our submitted series to the registry name of the
        model it submits, whose colour it takes, dashed.
    teams : sequence of str
        Every hub team.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        Label to its light colour, dark colour and SVG dash: our main
        builds in their `model_style`, our submitted series in their
        model's colour dashed, and the hub teams solid in the greys of
        `hub_styles`.
    """
    from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.base import list_models

    registry = [s.name for s in list_models()]
    out = {lab: model_style(m, registry) for lab, m in ours.items()}
    out |= {
        lab: (*model_style(m, registry)[:2], DASHES["dashed"])
        for lab, m in submitted.items()
    }
    grey = {mode: hub_styles(teams, mode) for mode in ("light", "dark")}
    out |= {t: (grey["light"][t][0], grey["dark"][t][0], "") for t in teams}
    return out

def hub_styles(teams: Sequence[str], mode: str) -> dict[str, tuple[str, str]]:
    """Give each hub team a grey and a marker, fixed by its sorted place.

    Parameters
    ----------
    teams : sequence of str
        Hub team names.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    dict of str to tuple of str
        Each team's colour and marker.
    """
    greys = HUB_GREYS[mode]
    markers = "os^Dv"
    return {
        team: (greys[i % len(greys)], markers[i // len(greys) % len(markers)])
        for i, team in enumerate(sorted(teams))
    }

def plot_hub_round(
    quantiles: pd.DataFrame,
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    reference_date: str,
    colours: Mapping[str, tuple[str, str, str]],
    locations: Sequence[str] = ("CD",),
    complete_after_weeks: int = 3,
    weeks_before: int = 8,
    mode: str = "light",
    shown: Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> Figure:
    """Plot our and the hub teams' intervals for one round against the data.

    Our series are in the top row, in their `comparison_colours`, and the
    hub teams in the bottom row, in greys with a marker each. Colours and
    markers do not depend on the round.

    Parameters
    ----------
    quantiles : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `bdbvhubrenewal.evaluation.hubcompare.forecast_quantiles`,
        with every round, so a team keeps its style across rounds.
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Target rows; the latest real vintage is drawn as data.
    reference_date : str
        The round.
    locations : sequence of str
        Locations to show, one column each, if any model forecast them.
    complete_after_weeks : int
        Weeks after which a week of the data counts as complete.
        Later weeks are shaded and their points drawn hollow.
    weeks_before : int
        Weeks of data shown before the reference date.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.
    colours : mapping of str to (str, str, str)
        Our series' labels (`comparison_label`) to their light
        colour, dark colour and dash, in the order drawn. Every series of
        ours in the round needs one.
    shown : sequence of str, optional
        Labels of our series to draw. Defaults to all of ours in the
        round.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        Per week and model, the median (point), 50% interval (thick line)
        and 90% interval (thin line), side by side, over the latest release,
        with the legend below the panels.
    """
    styles = hub_styles(
        sorted(set(quantiles.loc[quantiles["source"] == "hub", "model"])), mode
    )
    q = quantiles.loc[quantiles["reference_date"].astype(str) == reference_date]
    q = q.assign(
        label=[
            comparison_label(m, s)
            for m, s in zip(q["model"], q["source"], strict=True)
        ]
    )
    hub = q["source"] == "hub"
    if shown is not None:
        q = q.loc[hub | q["label"].isin(list(shown))]
        hub = q["source"] == "hub"
    here = set(q.loc[~hub, "label"])
    pick = 0 if mode == "light" else 1
    rows = [
        {
            lab: (c[pick], "o", c[2])
            for lab, c in colours.items()
            if lab in here
        },
        {lab: (*styles[lab], "") for lab in sorted(set(q.loc[hub, "label"]))},
    ]
    locs = [loc for loc in locations if loc in set(q["location"])]
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    latest = real["vintage"].max()
    names = _names(real)
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    cut = _incomplete_after(latest, complete_after_weeks)
    n_col = max(len(locs), 1)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        2,
        n_col,
        figsize=(4.0 * n_col, 5.6),
        squeeze=False,
        sharex=True,
        sharey="col",
        layout="constrained",
    )
    ref = pd.Timestamp(reference_date)
    start = ref - pd.Timedelta(weeks=weeks_before)
    for j, loc in enumerate(locs):
        ql = q.loc[q["location"] == loc]
        data = real.loc[(real["vintage"] == latest) & (real["location"] == loc)]
        x = pd.to_datetime(data["target_end_date"])
        end = pd.to_datetime(ql["target_end_date"]).max()
        sel = (x >= start) & (x <= end)
        for i, (ax, style) in enumerate(zip(axes[:, j], rows, strict=True)):
            _plot_data(
                ax,
                x[sel],
                data["total"][sel],
                cut,
                ink["data"],
                f"Data {latest}",
                lw=1.2,
                zorder=3,
            )
            width = 5.0 / max(len(style), 1)
            for k, (lab, (colour, marker, dash)) in enumerate(style.items()):
                m = ql.loc[ql["label"] == lab]
                offset = pd.Timedelta(days=(k - (len(style) - 1) / 2) * width)
                xm = pd.to_datetime(m["target_end_date"]) + offset
                ls = mpl_dash(dash)
                ax.vlines(
                    xm, m["q05"], m["q95"], color=colour, lw=1, alpha=0.7, ls=ls
                )
                ax.vlines(xm, m["q25"], m["q75"], color=colour, lw=3, ls=ls)
                ax.plot(
                    xm,
                    m["q50"],
                    marker,
                    ms=4,
                    ls="",
                    label=lab,
                    **point_style(colour, dash),
                )
            ax.axvline(mdates.date2num(ref), color=ink["muted"], lw=0.8, ls=":")
            _shade_incomplete(ax, cut, mode)
            title = ("Ours", "Hub teams")[i]
            ax.set_title(f"{names.get(loc, loc)} ({loc}): {title}", fontsize=9)
            ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.AutoDateLocator(maxticks=5))
            ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%d %b"))
    for ax in axes[:, 0]:
        ax.set_ylabel("Confirmed cases by onset week")
    seen: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for ax in axes[:, 0]:
        for h, lab in zip(*ax.get_legend_handles_labels(), strict=True):
            seen.setdefault(lab, h)
    fig.legend(
        list(seen.values()),
        list(seen),
        loc="outside lower center",
        ncol=min(len(seen), 4),
        fontsize=7,
        frameon=False,
    )
    return fig

def read_submission(path: Path | str, vintage: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Read a hub submission file as forecasts for `plot_nowcast`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : pathlib.Path or str
        A hub file with sample output.
    vintage : str
        The data vintage it was made from.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `model` (`"submission"`), `vintage`, `reference_date`,
        `location`, `target_end_date`, `sample` and `value`.
    """
    table = pd.read_csv(path)
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "model": "submission",
            "vintage": vintage,
            "reference_date": table["reference_date"].astype(str),
            "location": table["location"].astype(str),
            "target_end_date": table["target_end_date"].astype(str),
            "sample": table["output_type_id"].astype("int64"),
            "value": table["value"].astype(float),
        }
    )

def plot_submission(
    submission: Path | str,
    vintage: str,
    target: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    n_provinces: int = 3,
    data_dir: Path | str | None = None,
) -> Figure:
    """Plot what was submitted: the national total and the largest provinces.

    Draws the samples in the file, not a re-run of the model, with the
    data of the vintage behind them. Light mode, about 1600 by 1000 pixels
    at 100 dpi, for the submission pull request.

    Parameters
    ----------
    submission : pathlib.Path or str
        The hub file.
    vintage : str
        The data vintage the file was made from.
    target : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        Tidy target table. Loaded from `data_dir` if not given.
    n_provinces : int
        Provinces shown beside the national total, largest median first.
    data_dir : pathlib.Path or str, optional
        Directory of the tidy tables.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        A grid with one panel per location.
    """
    from bdbvhubrenewal.data import load_target
    from bdbvhubrenewal.data.zones import province_of

    target = load_target(data_dir) if target is None else target
    fc = read_submission(submission, vintage)
    provinces = fc["location"].map(province_of) == fc["location"]
    sizes = (
        fc.loc[provinces & (fc["location"] != "CD")]
        .groupby("location")["value"]
        .median()
        .sort_values(ascending=False)
    )
    locations = [
        loc
        for loc in ["CD", *sizes.index[:n_provinces]]
        if loc in set(fc["location"])
    ]
    ncol = 2
    nrow = max(1, -(-len(locations) // ncol))
    with theme("light"):
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(
            nrow, ncol, figsize=(16, 5 * nrow), layout="constrained"
        )
        flat = list(np.atleast_1d(axes).ravel())
        for loc, ax in zip(locations, flat, strict=False):
            plot_nowcast(
                loc,
                vintage=vintage,
                models=("submission",),
                target=target,
                forecasts=fc,
                ax=ax,
            )
        for ax in flat[len(locations) :]:
            ax.set_visible(False)
    return fig

def plot_scores(
    scores: pd.DataFrame,
    by: str = "horizon",
    metric: str = "wis",
    models: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    mode: str = "light",
    colours: Mapping[str, tuple[str, str, str]] | None = None,
) -> Figure:
    """Plot mean scores by horizon or location, one panel per vintage kind.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `score_forecasts`.
    by : str
        `"horizon"` or `"location"`.
    metric : str
        A score column, such as `"wis"`, `"log_wis"`, `"coverage_90"` or
        `"bias"`.
    models : sequence of str, optional
        Models in registry order.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.
    colours : mapping of str to (str, str, str), optional
        Model to its light colour, dark colour and dash. Defaults to
        `model_style`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        Mean score by `by`, with the number of forecasts in the title.
    """
    models = list(models or scores["model"].unique())
    kinds = [k for k in ("real", "simulated") if k in set(scores["kind"])]
    fig, axes = _grid(len(kinds), 3, width=3.6, height=2.6)
    for ax, kind in zip(axes, kinds, strict=True):
        s = scores.loc[scores["kind"] == kind]
        mean = s.groupby(["model", by])[metric].mean().unstack(0)
        if by == "location":
            order = s.groupby("location")["truth"].sum().sort_values()
            mean = mean.reindex(order.index[::-1])
        x = np.arange(len(mean))
        width = 0.8 / max(1, len(models))
        for i, m in enumerate(models):
            if m not in mean.columns:
                continue
            col, dash = (
                (colours[m][0 if mode == "light" else 1], colours[m][2])
                if colours
                else (model_colour(m, models, mode), model_dash(m))
            )
            if by == "horizon":
                ax.plot(
                    mean.index,
                    mean[m],
                    color=col,
                    ls=mpl_dash(dash),
                    marker=_KIND_MARKERS[kind],
                    ms=5,
                    label=m,
                )
            else:
                ax.bar(
                    x + i * width,
                    mean[m],
                    width,
                    label=m,
                    **bar_style(col, dash),
                )
        if by != "horizon":
            ax.set_xticks(
                x + width * (len(models) - 1) / 2,
                [str(v).removeprefix("CD-") for v in mean.index],
            )
        if metric.startswith("coverage"):
            level = 0.5 if metric.endswith("50") else 0.9
            ax.axhline(level, color=THEMES[mode]["muted"], lw=1, ls=":")
        if metric == "bias":
            ax.axhline(0, color=THEMES[mode]["muted"], lw=1, ls=":")
        ax.set_title(
            f"{kind}: {s[['vintage']].nunique().iloc[0]} vintages, n {len(s)}"
        )
        ax.set_xlabel(by.capitalize())
    axes[0].set_ylabel(_METRIC_LABELS.get(metric, metric))
    axes[0].legend()
    return fig

def plot_scenarios(
    scores: pd.DataFrame,
    models: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    mode: str = "light",
    metric: str = "wis",
) -> Figure:
    """Plot mean WIS by horizon on the simulated scenarios.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        Scenario scores with `scenario`, `location`, `model`, `horizon`,
        `wis`, `truth_view` and `complete`.
    models : sequence of str, optional
        Models in registry order.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        One panel per scenario, scored against the final data on complete
        weeks. National is solid, provinces dashed and zones dotted.
    """
    models = list(models or scores["model"].unique())
    final = scores.loc[(scores["truth_view"] == "final") & scores["complete"]]
    scenarios = list(final["scenario"].unique())
    fig, axes = _grid(len(scenarios), 3, width=3.6, height=2.6)
    for ax, scenario in zip(axes, scenarios, strict=True):
        s = final.loc[final["scenario"] == scenario]
        levels = (
            s["level"]
            if "level" in s
            else np.where(s["location"] == "CD", "national", "province")
        )
        for level, style in (
            ("national", "-"),
            ("province", "--"),
            ("zone", ":"),
        ):
            part = s.loc[levels == level]
            mean = part.groupby(["model", "horizon"])[metric].mean().unstack(0)
            for m in models:
                if m not in mean.columns:
                    continue
                ax.plot(
                    mean.index,
                    mean[m],
                    color=model_colour(m, models, mode),
                    ls=style,
                    marker="o",
                    ms=4,
                    label=f"{m}, {level}",
                )
        ax.set_title(scenario.removeprefix("calibrated_"))
        ax.set_xlabel("Horizon")
    axes[0].set_ylabel(_METRIC_LABELS.get(metric, metric))
    axes[0].legend(fontsize=7)
    return fig

def plot_scores_by_truth(
    scores: pd.DataFrame,
    metric: str = "wis",
    models: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    mode: str = "light",
) -> Figure:
    """Plot how each forecast's mean score moves as the truth is revised.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scores : pandas.DataFrame
        Scores with `model`, `vintage`, `truth_vintage` and `metric`.
    metric : str
        A score column.
    models : sequence of str, optional
        Models in registry order, one panel each.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        Mean score against the truth vintage, one line per forecast
        vintage.
    """
    models = list(models or scores["model"].unique())
    models = [m for m in models if m in set(scores["model"])]
    fig, axes = _grid(len(models), 3, width=3.6, height=2.6)
    vintages = sorted(set(scores["vintage"]))
    for ax, m in zip(axes, models, strict=True):
        s = scores.loc[scores["model"] == m]
        mean = s.groupby(["vintage", "truth_vintage"])[metric].mean()
        for v in vintages:
            if v not in mean.index.get_level_values(0):
                continue
            line = mean.loc[v]
            ax.plot(
                pd.to_datetime(line.index),
                line.to_numpy(),
                color=model_colour(v, vintages, mode),
                marker="o",
                ms=5,
                label=f"Forecast from {v}",
            )
        ax.set_title(m)
        ax.set_xlabel("Truth vintage")
        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%d %b"))
    axes[0].set_ylabel(_METRIC_LABELS.get(metric, metric))
    axes[0].legend(fontsize=7)
    return fig

def plot_release_nowcasts(
    quantiles: pd.DataFrame,
    releases: pd.DataFrame,
    locations: Sequence[str],
    models: Sequence[str],
    mode: str = "light",
) -> Figure:
    """Plot each model's final forecast of the recent weeks by origin.

    Parameters
    ----------
    quantiles : pandas.DataFrame
        `evaluation.nowcast.ReleaseBacktest.quantiles`.
    releases : pandas.DataFrame
        Real target rows with `vintage`, `location`, `target_end_date`
        and `total`.
    locations : sequence of str
        Places to show, one column each.
    models : sequence of str
        Models to show.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        One panel per origin and place. Lines are the counts each release
        reports, bars the 50% and 90% intervals.
    """
    final = quantiles.loc[quantiles["target"] == "complete"]
    final = final.loc[final["model"].isin(models)]
    origins = sorted(final["origin"].unique())
    fig, axes = _grid(
        len(origins) * len(locations), len(locations), width=3.4, height=2.6
    )
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    shades = np.linspace(0.4, 1.0, len(releases["vintage"].unique()))
    # Each model's bars sit side by side within the week.
    width, mid = 5.6 / len(models), (len(models) - 1) / 2
    for i, origin in enumerate(origins):
        for j, loc in enumerate(locations):
            ax = axes[i * len(locations) + j]
            weeks = final.loc[
                (final["origin"] == origin) & (final["location"] == loc)
            ]["target_end_date"]
            lo = pd.Timestamp(weeks.min()) - pd.Timedelta(days=7)
            for v, a in zip(
                sorted(releases["vintage"].unique()), shades, strict=True
            ):
                r = releases.loc[
                    (releases["vintage"] == v) & (releases["location"] == loc)
                ]
                x = pd.to_datetime(r["target_end_date"])
                keep = (x >= lo) & (x <= pd.Timestamp(origin) + pd.Timedelta(7))
                ax.plot(
                    x[keep],
                    r["total"][keep],
                    color=ink["data"],
                    alpha=a,
                    lw=1.2,
                    label=f"Release {v}",
                )
            for m_i, m in enumerate(models):
                rows = final.loc[
                    (final["origin"] == origin)
                    & (final["location"] == loc)
                    & (final["model"] == m)
                ]
                colour = model_colour(m, models, mode)
                _draw_bars(ax, rows, colour, model_dash(m), (m_i - mid) * width)
            ax.set_title(f"{loc}, origin {origin}")
            _date_axis(ax)
            ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(
                mdates.WeekdayLocator(byweekday=5, interval=2)
            )
            ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%d %b"))
    axes[0].set_ylabel("Cases by onset week")
    handles, labels = axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
    for m in models:
        colour = model_colour(m, models, mode)
        dash = mpl_dash(model_dash(m))
        handles.append(axes[0].plot([], [], color=colour, lw=4, ls=dash)[0])
        labels.append(f"{m} (50% and 90%)")
    fig.legend(
        handles,
        labels,
        fontsize=7,
        loc="outside lower center",
        ncols=min(len(labels), 5),
    )
    return fig

def plot_relative_overall(
    table: pd.DataFrame,
    models: Sequence[str],
    baseline: str = "randomwalk",
    mode: str = "light",
    x: str = "pool",
    metrics: Mapping[str, tuple[str, float | None]] = OVERALL_METRICS,
    colours: Mapping[str, tuple[str, str, str]] | None = None,
) -> Figure:
    """Plot each model's overall scores by pool, a panel per metric.

    Parameters
    ----------
    table : pandas.DataFrame
        `relative_wis` output by `x`, for one target.
    models : sequence of str
        Models in registry order. Those absent from a pool are skipped.
    baseline : str
        The model WIS is relative to, named in the labels.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.
    x : str
        The column of the groups, `national`, `provinces` and `zones`.
    metrics : mapping of str to (str, float or None)
        Metric column to its label and reference line, as
        `OVERALL_METRICS`.
    colours : mapping of str to (str, str, str), optional
        Model to its light colour, dark colour and dash. Defaults to each
        model's `model_style`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        A panel of bars grouped by pool per metric, each with a dotted line
        at its reference.
    """
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    pick = 0 if mode == "light" else 1
    have_pools = set(table[x])
    pools = [p for p in ("national", "provinces", "zones") if p in have_pools]
    fig, axes = _grid(len(metrics), 3, width=3.4, height=2.6)
    width = 0.8 / len(models)
    for i, m in enumerate(models):
        rows = table.loc[table["model"] == m].set_index(x)
        have = [p for p in pools if p in rows.index]
        shift = (i - (len(models) - 1) / 2) * width
        at = [pools.index(p) + shift for p in have]
        style = colours[m] if colours else model_style(m, models)
        for ax, key in zip(axes, metrics, strict=True):
            ax.bar(
                at,
                rows.loc[have, key],
                width,
                label=m,
                **bar_style(style[pick], style[2]),
            )
    for ax, (key, (label, ref)) in zip(axes, metrics.items(), strict=True):
        if ref is not None:
            ax.axhline(ref, color=ink["muted"], lw=1, ls=":")
        if key.startswith("rel_"):
            label = f"{label} to {baseline}"
        if key.startswith("coverage"):
            ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
        if key == "bias":
            ax.set_ylim(-1, 1)
        ax.set_ylabel(label)
        ax.set_axisbelow(True)
        ax.set_xticks(range(len(pools)), [p.capitalize() for p in pools])
        ax.set_xlim(-0.5, len(pools) - 0.5)
    handles, labels = axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(
        handles,
        labels,
        fontsize=7,
        loc="outside lower center",
        ncols=min(len(models), 5),
    )
    return fig

def plot_truth_changes(
    target: pd.DataFrame,
    names: Mapping[str, str],
    weeks: int = 16,
    mode: str = "light",
) -> Figure:
    """Plot each place's weekly counts in every release and their changes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        Real target rows with every release.
    names : mapping of str to str
        Place names by id.
    weeks : int
        Weeks shown, up to the latest release's last week.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        Per place with cases in the weeks shown, most first, the count by
        onset week with one line per release,
        from the oldest (faint) to the newest (strong), and under it the
        change from the previous release by week, with a line at 0.
    """
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    releases = sorted(set(real["vintage"]))
    shades = np.linspace(0.3, 1.0, len(releases))
    # Newer releases are stronger: darker on light, lighter on dark.
    cmap = plt.get_cmap("Blues")
    colours = [cmap(v if mode == "light" else 1.25 - v) for v in shades]
    end = pd.to_datetime(real["target_end_date"]).max()
    start = end - pd.Timedelta(weeks=weeks)
    wide = real.assign(
        target_end_date=pd.to_datetime(real["target_end_date"])
    ).pivot_table(
        index=["location", "target_end_date"],
        columns="vintage",
        values="total",
    )
    recent = wide.loc[wide.index.get_level_values(1) > start]
    latest = recent[releases[-1]].groupby(level=0).sum()
    latest = latest.loc[latest > 0].sort_values(ascending=False, kind="stable")
    locations = list(latest.index)
    ncol = min(4, len(locations))
    nrow = int(np.ceil(len(locations) / ncol))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        2 * nrow,
        ncol,
        figsize=(3.4 * ncol, 3.6 * nrow),
        squeeze=False,
        layout="constrained",
        gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": [2, 1] * nrow},
    )
    for k in range(nrow * ncol):
        row, col = 2 * (k // ncol), k % ncol
        top, low = axes[row, col], axes[row + 1, col]
        if k >= len(locations):
            top.set_visible(False)
            low.set_visible(False)
            continue
        loc = locations[k]
        rows = wide.loc[loc]
        rows = rows.loc[rows.index > start]
        change = rows.diff(axis=1)
        for i, vin in enumerate(releases):
            top.plot(
                rows.index, rows[vin], color=colours[i], lw=1.4, label=str(vin)
            )
            if i:
                low.plot(rows.index, change[vin], color=colours[i], lw=1.2)
        low.axhline(0, color=ink["muted"], lw=1, ls=":")
        top.set_title(names.get(loc, loc), fontsize=9)
        top.set_xticklabels([])
        for ax in (top, low):
            ax.set_xlim(start, end + pd.Timedelta(days=3))
            ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.MonthLocator())
            ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%b"))
        if k % ncol == 0:
            top.set_ylabel("Count by onset week")
            low.set_ylabel("Change")
    handles, labels = axes[0, 0].get_legend_handles_labels()
    fig.legend(
        handles,
        labels,
        title="Release",
        fontsize=7,
        title_fontsize=8,
        loc="outside lower center",
        ncols=len(releases),
    )
    return fig

def plot_place_summary(
    table: pd.DataFrame,
    models: Sequence[str],
    colours: Mapping[str, tuple[str, str, str]],
    names: Mapping[str, str],
    mode: str = "light",
) -> Figure:
    """Plot relative WIS per place and model, a row per place, by scale.

    The axis is on the log scale, so places whose scores are near zero do
    not set it. Scores of 0 are left out.

    Parameters
    ----------
    table : pandas.DataFrame
        `relative_wis` output by `pool` and `location`.
    models : sequence of str
        Models in order. Those absent from a place are skipped.
    colours : mapping of str to (str, str, str)
        Model to its light colour, dark colour and dash.
    names : mapping of str to str
        Place names by id. Places not named show their code.
    mode : str
        `"light"` or `"dark"`.

    Returns
    -------
    matplotlib.figure.Figure
        A panel per scale below national (provinces, health zones), with
        a row per place, by name, and a dot per model.
    """
    ink = THEMES[mode]
    pick = 0 if mode == "light" else 1
    titles = {"provinces": "Provinces", "zones": "Health zones"}
    pools = [p for p in titles if p in set(table["pool"])]
    rows = [table.loc[table["pool"] == p, "location"].nunique() for p in pools]
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        1,
        len(pools),
        figsize=(4.4 * len(pools), 0.9 + 0.2 * max(rows)),
        squeeze=False,
        layout="constrained",
    )
    for ax, pool in zip(axes[0], pools, strict=True):
        sub = table.loc[table["pool"] == pool]
        places = sorted(set(sub["location"]), key=lambda x: names.get(x, x))
        y = {loc: i for i, loc in enumerate(places)}
        for m in models:
            own = sub.loc[(sub["model"] == m) & (sub["rel_wis"] > 0)]
            if own.empty:
                continue
            ax.plot(
                own["rel_wis"],
                own["location"].map(y),
                "o",
                ms=4,
                ls="",
                label=m,
                **point_style(colours[m][pick], colours[m][2]),
            )
        ax.axvline(1.0, color=ink["muted"], lw=1, ls=":")
        ax.set_xscale("log")
        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:g}"))
        ax.set_yticks(range(len(places)), [names.get(p, p) for p in places])
        ax.set_ylim(len(places) - 0.5, -0.5)
        ax.set_title(titles[pool], fontsize=9)
        ax.set_xlabel("Relative WIS")
        ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    handles: dict[str, Artist] = {}
    for ax in axes[0]:
        for hd, lb in zip(*ax.get_legend_handles_labels(), strict=True):
            handles.setdefault(lb, hd)
    labels = [m for m in models if m in handles]
    fig.legend(
        [handles[m] for m in labels],
        labels,
        fontsize=7,
        loc="outside lower center",
        ncols=min(len(labels), 5),
    )
    return fig

def make_report(
    figures: Path | str = "docs/figures",
    generated: Path | str = "docs/generated",
    data_dir: Path | str = "data",
    results: Path | str = "results",
    output: Path | str = "results",
    config_path: Path | str = "config/backtest.toml",
    hub_comparison: Path | str = "results/hub-comparison",
) -> None:
    """Write every docs figure and table.

    Parameters
    ----------
    figures : pathlib.Path or str
        Where SVGs go.
    generated : pathlib.Path or str
        Where Markdown tables go.
    data_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        The tidy data.
    results : pathlib.Path or str
        Where the backtest score tables are.
    output : pathlib.Path or str
        Where the backtest forecasts are.
    config_path : pathlib.Path or str
        Backtest settings.
    hub_comparison : pathlib.Path or str
        Output of `bdbvhubrenewal compare-hub`, if it has been run.
    """
    fig, gen = Path(figures), Path(generated)
    res, out = Path(results), Path(output)
    config = load_config(config_path)
    target = load_target(data_dir)
    delays = load_delays(data_dir)
    real = target.loc[target["kind"] == "real"]
    latest = real["vintage"].max()
    latest_delays = delays.loc[delays["vintage"] == delays["vintage"].max()]
    write_store_note(res, gen)

    # Data page.
    save_light_dark(
        lambda mode: plot_target(real, mode=mode), fig / "target.svg"
    )
    save_light_dark(
        lambda mode: plot_revisions(real, mode=mode), fig / "revisions.svg"
    )
    save_light_dark(
        lambda mode: plot_imputed_share(real, mode=mode),
        fig / "imputed-share.svg",
    )
    save_light_dark(
        lambda mode: plot_imputed_by_release(real, mode=mode),
        fig / "imputed-by-release.svg",
    )
    save_light_dark(
        lambda mode: plot_newly_missing(real, mode=mode),
        fig / "newly-missing.svg",
    )
    zones = load_health_zones(data_dir)
    save_light_dark(
        lambda mode: plot_downward_updates(real, zones, mode=mode),
        fig / "downward-updates.svg",
    )
    _write(gen / "downward-updates.md", _downward_table(real, zones))
    save_light_dark(
        lambda mode: plot_delay_distribution(latest_delays, mode=mode),
        fig / "delay-distribution.svg",
    )
    save_light_dark(
        lambda mode: plot_delays_over_time(delays, mode=mode),
        fig / "delays-time.svg",
    )
    summary = real.groupby("vintage").agg(
        weeks=("target_end_date", "nunique"),
        first_week=("target_end_date", "min"),
        last_week=("target_end_date", "max"),
    )
    nat = (
        real.loc[real["location"] == NATIONAL]
        .groupby("vintage")[["observed", "imputed", "total"]]
        .sum()
    )
    prov = real.loc[(real["location"] != NATIONAL) & (real["total"] > 0)]
    summary["provinces_with_cases"] = prov.groupby("vintage")[
        "location"
    ].nunique()
    summary = summary.join(nat).reset_index()
    summary["delay_rows"] = summary["vintage"].map(
        delays.groupby("vintage").size()
    )
    _write(gen / "vintages.md", _table(summary))
    coherence = national_coherence(real)
    by_vintage = (
        coherence.assign(with_gap=coherence["gap"] != 0)
        .pivot_table(
            index="vintage",
            columns="stream",
            values="with_gap",
            aggfunc="sum",
        )[list(COHERENCE_STREAMS)]
        .rename(columns=lambda s: f"{s} weeks with a gap")
        .reset_index()
    )
    _write(gen / "national-coherence.md", _table(by_vintage))
    dsum = delay_summary(latest_delays, by=("location_name",))
    _write(gen / "delays.md", _table(dsum.sort_values("n", ascending=False)))
    new = newly_missing(real)
    new = new.loc[new["location"] == NATIONAL]
    _write(gen / "newly-missing.md", _table(new.drop(columns=["kind"])))
    outbreak = simulate_outbreak()
    save_light_dark(
        lambda mode: plot_simulation(outbreak.parameters, mode=mode),
        fig / "simulation.svg",
    )

    # Backtest and comparison pages.
    names = [s.name for s in list_models()]
    _release_section(fig, gen, res, real, names)
    _backtest_page(fig, gen, res, out, config, target, names, data_dir)
    _comparison_page(fig, gen, Path(hub_comparison), target)

    # Nowcast page: latest real vintage, every registered model.
    rows = real.loc[real["vintage"] == latest]
    daily = load_daily(data_dir)
    tasks = make_tasks(rows, delays, config, history=real, daily=daily)
    forecasts_now = _nowcast_forecasts(tasks, latest, res)
    _nowcast_page(fig, gen, target, forecasts_now, names, config, latest)
    _zone_nowcast_section(
        fig, gen, data_dir, target, tasks[0], forecasts_now, config, names
    )
    groups = _nowcast_groups(target, sorted(set(forecasts_now["location"])))
    save_light_dark(
        partial(
            plot_delay_check, daily, latest, [*groups["main"], *groups["other"]]
        ),
        fig / "delay-check.svg",
    )
    # Written by `fit-store load` from the stored fits.
    learnt = pd.read_csv(res / DELAY_SUMMARY_FILE)
    fitted = sorted(set(learnt["location"]) - {"pooled"})
    baseline = baseline_share(
        daily, str(learnt["vintage"].max()), [NATIONAL, *fitted]
    )
    save_light_dark(
        partial(plot_renewal_delay, learnt, baseline, _location_names(real)),
        fig / "renewal-delay.svg",
    )

docs.title: bdbvhubrenewal.submission
docs.text:
Submission: what goes to the hub and how it is checked.

  • hub: the hub file writer and the model metadata.
  • metadata: the metadata text of each model that may be submitted.
  • validate: the hub's own checks in Python (bdbvhubrenewal validate).

docs.title: bdbvhubrenewal.submission.hub
docs.text:
Write hub submissions and model metadata.

A submission is a CSV with columns reference_date, forecast_date, target, target_end_date, location, output_type, output_type_id and value. Every row is one week of one sample trajectory. forecast_date is the day the PR is opened. A resubmission in the same week keeps the file on the hub's main branch unchanged and appends rows with one new forecast_date. The round BDBV 2026 nowcasting and forecasting takes exactly 100 samples for each (reference_date, location, target), and each sample index covers the same target weeks within a location.

submission.validate checks the written files as hubValidations does. The authoritative check is still hubValidations (task validate-hub).

def model_abbr_for(model: str, path: Path | str = SUBMISSION_CONFIG) -> str:
    """Return the hub abbreviation a model submits under.

    A model with its own entry under `[models]` in `config/hub.toml` is a
    hub model of its own. Every other model submits under the
    `[submission]` abbreviation, one value not derived from a model key,
    so every renewal variant and every fallback submits under one id.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : str
        The model key, such as `"randomwalknowcast"`.
    path : pathlib.Path or str
        The configuration file.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The abbreviation, such as `"baseline"`.
    """
    with Path(path).open("rb") as fh:
        config = tomllib.load(fh)
    own = config.get("models", {}).get(model, {})
    return str(own.get("model_abbr") or config["submission"]["model_abbr"])

    -------
    str

    ------
    ValueError
        If either part is not 1 to 14 letters, digits or underscores.

        if not _ID_PART.match(part):
            raise ValueError(

Turn forecast samples into the hub's submission table.

The table meets every guarantee in docs/submission/hub-spec.md: sample ids 1..n_samples reused in every location, one row per id for every week, the same weeks for every location, whole non-negative counts and the national value as the sum of the provinces for each sample. Any national rows in samples are replaced.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default samples DataFrame

required reference_date date or str

The round's reference date.

required target str

The target name.

Health-zone samples (columns as samples), such as from forecasters.zones.ZoneAllocator. They must sum to the rounded province samples, sample by sample, and are not added to the national value.

None n_samples int

Returns:

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If a province or zone does not have sample ids 1..n_samples, a sample lacks a week, locations cover different weeks, or the zones do not sum to their provinces.

Examples:

...     model_id, to_hub_table, write_submission
... )
>>> samples = forecasts.query("model == 'randomwalknowcast'")
>>> table = to_hub_table(samples, task.reference_date)
>>> write_submission(table, "output/submission", model_id("rwnowcast"))
Source code in src/bdbvhubrenewal/submission/hub.py 
def to_hub_table(
    samples: pd.DataFrame,
    reference_date: dt.date | str,
    target: str = "wk inc confirmed cases",
    *,
    unassigned: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    zones: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    n_samples: int = 100,
    forecast_date: dt.date | str | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Turn forecast samples into the hub's submission table.

    The table meets every guarantee in `docs/submission/hub-spec.md`:
    sample ids `1..n_samples` reused in every location, one row per id for every
    week, the same weeks for every location, whole non-negative counts
    and the national value as the sum of the provinces for each sample.
    Any national rows in `samples` are replaced.

    Parameters
    ----------
    samples : pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date`, `sample` (an integer
        index, one joint draw across weeks and provinces) and `value`.
    reference_date : datetime.date or str
        The round's reference date.
    target : str
        The target name.
    unassigned : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        A modelled component of the national count not assigned to any
        province, with columns `target_end_date`, `sample` and `value`.
        It is added to the national sum. Missing rows count as zero.
    zones : pandas.DataFrame, optional
        Health-zone samples (columns as `samples`), such as from
        `forecasters.zones.ZoneAllocator`. They must sum to the rounded
        province samples, sample by sample, and are not added to the
        national value.
    n_samples : int
        Number of samples each location must have.
    forecast_date : datetime.date or str, optional
        The day the PR is opened. The default is today (UTC), see
        `run_date`. The hub requires it to be on or before the
        reference date and within a day of the validation date.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `HUB_COLUMNS`, sorted by location, sample and week.
        Values are rounded to whole cases before the national sum, so the
        national value is exactly the sum of the written province values.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a province or zone does not have sample ids `1..n_samples`, a
        sample lacks a week, locations cover different weeks, or the
        zones do not sum to their provinces.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from bdbvhubrenewal.submission.hub import (
    ...     model_id, to_hub_table, write_submission
    ... )
    >>> samples = forecasts.query("model == 'randomwalknowcast'")
    >>> table = to_hub_table(samples, task.reference_date)
    >>> write_submission(table, "output/submission", model_id("rwnowcast"))
    """
    ref = as_date(reference_date).isoformat()
    fdate = as_date(forecast_date or run_date()).isoformat()
    prov = samples.loc[samples["location"] != NATIONAL].copy()
    if prov.empty:
        raise ValueError("No province samples to write.")
    prov["target_end_date"] = prov["target_end_date"].astype(str)
    prov["location"] = prov["location"].astype(str)
    prov["sample"] = prov["sample"].astype("int64")
    prov["value"] = prov["value"].clip(lower=0).round()
    zone = _zone_rows(prov, zones)
    ids = set(range(1, n_samples + 1))
    weeks = sorted(set(prov["target_end_date"]))
    for loc, rows in pd.concat([prov, zone]).groupby("location"):
        if set(rows["sample"]) != ids:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{loc}: sample ids must be 1 to {n_samples}, the same in "
                "every location."
            )
        if sorted(set(rows["target_end_date"])) != weeks:
            raise ValueError(f"{loc}: every location needs the same weeks.")
        if (
            len(rows) != n_samples * len(weeks)
            or rows.duplicated(["sample", "target_end_date"]).any()
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                f"{loc}: every sample needs exactly one row for each week."
            )
    national = (
        prov.groupby(["target_end_date", "sample"])["value"].sum().reset_index()
    )
    if unassigned is not None and not unassigned.empty:
        extra = (
            unassigned.assign(
                target_end_date=unassigned["target_end_date"].astype(str),
                sample=unassigned["sample"].astype("int64"),
                value=unassigned["value"].clip(lower=0).round(),
            )
            .groupby(["target_end_date", "sample"])["value"]
            .sum()
        )
        national = national.set_index(["target_end_date", "sample"])
        national["value"] = national["value"].add(extra, fill_value=0)
        national = national.reset_index()
    national["location"] = NATIONAL
    both = pd.concat([prov, national, zone], ignore_index=True)
    out = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "reference_date": ref,
            "forecast_date": fdate,
            "target": target,
            "target_end_date": both["target_end_date"],
            "location": both["location"],
            "output_type": OUTPUT_TYPE,
            "output_type_id": both["sample"].astype("int64"),
            "value": both["value"].astype("int64"),
        }
    )
    return out.sort_values(
        ["location", "output_type_id", "target_end_date"]
    ).reset_index(drop=True)[list(HUB_COLUMNS)]

def write_submission(
    table: pd.DataFrame,
    root: Path | str,
    mid: str,
) -> Path:
    """Write a submission table to its place under `root`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    table : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `to_hub_table`.
    root : pathlib.Path or str
        Root of the hub checkout or an output directory.
    mid : str
        The model id.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path
        The path written.
    """
    refs = table["reference_date"].unique()
    if len(refs) != 1:
        raise ValueError("A submission must have one reference date.")
    if len(table["forecast_date"].unique()) != 1:
        raise ValueError("A submission must have one forecast date.")
    path = submission_path(root, str(refs[0]), mid)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    write_csv(table, path)
    return path

def render_model_metadata(
    model_abbr: str,
    model_name: str,
    methods: str,
    methods_long: str,
    data_inputs: str,
    model_version: str | None = None,
    overrides: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build a model metadata record in the hub's field order.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model_abbr : str
        Model abbreviation (the part after `seabbs-`).
    model_name : str
        Full model name, under 50 characters.
    methods : str
        Short description, at most 200 characters.
    methods_long : str
        Full description.
    data_inputs : str
        The data the model uses.
    model_version : str, optional
        A version identifier, such as a git SHA.
    overrides : mapping, optional
        Any fields to replace in `METADATA_DEFAULTS`.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        The metadata record.
    """
    base = {**METADATA_DEFAULTS, **(overrides or {})}
    record: dict[str, Any] = {
        "team_name": base["team_name"],
        "team_abbr": base["team_abbr"],
        "model_name": model_name,
        "model_abbr": model_abbr,
        "model_contributors": base["model_contributors"],
        "license": base["license"],
        "model_details": {
            "data_inputs": data_inputs,
            "methods": methods,
            "methods_long": methods_long,
        },
    }
    if model_version is not None:
        record["model_version"] = model_version
    for key in (
        "website_url",
        "repo_url",
        "team_funding",
        "ensemble_of_hub_models",
    ):
        record[key] = base[key]
    return record

        The path written.

    path = Path(directory) / f"{record['team_abbr']}-{record['model_abbr']}.yml"

    )

docs.title: bdbvhubrenewal.submission.validate
docs.text:
Validate BDBV Modeling Hub submissions against the hub's own config.

The hub's rules are read at run time from a local clone of InsightNet-US/BDBV-Modeling-Hub (hub-config/tasks.json, hub-config/admin.json and hub-config/model-metadata-schema.json), so the validator follows config changes such as new reference dates.

Checks mirror the names used by the R package hubValidations so results can be compared one to one. Two checks are Python only and stricter than hubValidations 3.0.0: spl_id_type (sample ids must be integers when the config says so) and readme_horizon (a warning when a target_end_date is not a Saturday within the README's window).

Usage::

bdbvhubrenewal validate --hub PATH [--metadata-dir DIR]
    [--now ISO8601 | --skip-window] [--json OUT] FILE...

@dataclass
class Report:
    """The checks run on one file.

    Attributes
    ----------
    file : str
        The file checked.
    checks : list of Check
        Each check's outcome, in the order run.
    """

    file: str
    checks: list[Check] = field(default_factory=list)

    def add(
        self,
        check: str,
        ok: bool,
        message: str,
        halt: bool = False,
        fail_message: str | None = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Record a check that passes when `ok` is true.

        Parameters
        ----------
        check : str
            Check name, as in hubValidations.
        ok : bool
            Whether the check passed.
        message : str
            Message to record.
        halt : bool, default False
            Record a failure as `error`, which stops later checks.
        fail_message : str, optional
            Message to record instead when the check fails.

        Returns
        -------
        bool
            `ok`.
        """
        status = "pass" if ok else ("error" if halt else "fail")
        self.checks.append(
            Check(check, status, message if ok else fail_message or message)
        )
        return ok

    def skip(self, check: str, message: str) -> None:
        """Record a check that was not run.

        Parameters
        ----------
        check : str
            Check name.
        message : str
            Why it was skipped.
        """
        self.checks.append(Check(check, "skip", message))

    def warn(self, check: str, message: str) -> None:
        """Record a warning, which does not fail the file.

        Parameters
        ----------
        check : str
            Check name.
        message : str
            The warning.
        """
        self.checks.append(Check(check, "warn", message))

    @property
    def failed(self) -> list[Check]:
        """The checks with status `fail` or `error`.

        Returns
        -------
        list of Check
            The failed checks.
        """
        return [c for c in self.checks if c.status in ("fail", "error")]

    @property
    def valid(self) -> bool:
        """Whether no check failed.

        Returns
        -------
        bool
            True if the file passes.
        """
        return not self.failed

@dataclass
class Hub:
    """The hub's configuration, read from a local clone.

    Attributes
    ----------
    path : pathlib.Path
        Root of the clone.
    rounds : list of Round
        The rounds in `hub-config/tasks.json`.
    admin : dict
        `hub-config/admin.json`.
    metadata_schema : dict or None
        `hub-config/model-metadata-schema.json`, if present.
    """

    path: Path
    rounds: list[Round]
    admin: dict[str, Any]
    metadata_schema: dict[str, Any] | None

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: str | Path) -> Hub:
        """Read the hub configuration from a clone.

        Parameters
        ----------
        path : str or pathlib.Path
            Root of a clone of the hub repository.

        Returns
        -------
        Hub
            The configuration.

        Examples
        --------
        >>> from bdbvhubrenewal.submission.validate import Hub, validate_file
        >>> hub = Hub.load("../BDBV-Modeling-Hub")
        >>> report = validate_file("model-output/x/2026-11-07-x.csv", hub)
        >>> report.valid, [c.check for c in report.failed]
        """
        p = Path(path)
        tasks = json.loads((p / "hub-config" / "tasks.json").read_text())
        admin = json.loads((p / "hub-config" / "admin.json").read_text())
        schema_p = p / "hub-config" / "model-metadata-schema.json"
        schema = json.loads(schema_p.read_text()) if schema_p.exists() else None
        rounds = []
        for i, r in enumerate(tasks["rounds"]):
            mts = []
            for mt in r["model_tasks"]:
                tids = {
                    k: TaskId(
                        _vals(v.get("required")), _vals(v.get("optional"))
                    )
                    for k, v in mt["task_ids"].items()
                }
                ots = {
                    k: _parse_output_type(k, v)
                    for k, v in mt["output_type"].items()
                }
                mts.append(ModelTask(tids, ots))
            rounds.append(
                Round(
                    index=i,
                    name=r.get("round_name", f"round {i + 1}"),
                    round_id_from_variable=bool(r["round_id_from_variable"]),
                    round_id=r["round_id"],
                    model_tasks=mts,
                    submissions_due=r["submissions_due"],
                )
            )
        return cls(p, rounds, admin, schema)

    @property
    def timezone(self) -> ZoneInfo:
        """The hub's time zone, from `admin.json`.

        Returns
        -------
        zoneinfo.ZoneInfo
            The time zone, UTC if none is set.
        """
        return ZoneInfo(self.admin.get("timezone", "UTC"))

    @property
    def file_formats(self) -> list[str]:
        """The file formats the hub accepts.

        Returns
        -------
        list of str
            Such as `["csv"]`.
        """
        return list(self.admin.get("file_format", ["csv"]))

    def find_round(self, round_id: str) -> Round | None:
        """Find the round a round id belongs to.

        Parameters
        ----------
        round_id : str
            Round id, the reference date.

        Returns
        -------
        Round or None
            The round, or None if no round has that id.
        """
        for r in self.rounds:
            if round_id in r.round_ids:
                return r
        return None

    def all_round_ids(self) -> list[str]:
        """List every round id in the configuration.

        Returns
        -------
        list of str
            Round ids, sorted within each round.
        """
        out: list[str] = []
        for r in self.rounds:
            out += sorted(r.round_ids)
        return out

    def submission_window(
        self, rnd: Round, round_id: str
    ) -> tuple[datetime, datetime]:
        """Open and close times of the submission window, in hub time.

        Matches hubValidations: the window opens at 00:00:00 on the start
        day and closes at 23:59:59 on the end day.

        Parameters
        ----------
        rnd : Round
            The round, from `find_round`.
        round_id : str
            Round id, the reference date.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple of datetime.datetime
            Opening and closing times.
        """
        due = rnd.submissions_due
        tz = self.timezone
        if "relative_to" in due:
            ref = date.fromisoformat(round_id)
            start_d = ref + timedelta(days=int(due["start"]))
            end_d = ref + timedelta(days=int(due["end"]))
        else:
            start_d = date.fromisoformat(str(due["start"]))
            end_d = date.fromisoformat(str(due["end"]))
        return (
            datetime.combine(start_d, time(0, 0, 0), tz),
            datetime.combine(end_d, time(23, 59, 59), tz),
        )
