def validate_submission(
    file: str | Path,
    hub: Hub,
    metadata_dirs: Iterable[Path] = (),
    now: datetime | None = None,
    skip_window: bool = False,
    previous: str | Path | None = None,
) -> Report:
    """Run all model-output checks on one file.

    The hub's `forecast_date` checks run first. The standard checks then
    see only the new rows, without `forecast_date`, as in the hub's own
    workflow.

    Parameters
    ----------
    file : str or pathlib.Path
        The model-output CSV.
    hub : Hub
        The hub configuration.
    metadata_dirs : iterable of pathlib.Path
        Directories to look for the model's metadata in.
    now : datetime.datetime, optional
        Time to check the submission window against. Defaults to now.
    skip_window : bool, default False
        Skip the window check and the check that the new forecast date
        is recent.
    previous : str or pathlib.Path, optional
        The file now on the hub's main branch at the same path, if any.

    Returns
    -------
    Report
        The checks and their outcomes.
    """
    fp = Path(file)
    rep = Report(str(file))

    # File-level checks.
    meta = parse_file_name(fp.name)
    if not rep.add(
        "file_name",
        meta is not None,
        f'File name "{fp.name}" is valid.',
        halt=True,
        fail_message=f'File name "{fp.name}" must be '
        "<round_id>-<team>-<model>.<ext>.",
    ):
        return rep
    assert meta is not None
    model_id = f"{meta['team']}-{meta['model']}"
    round_id = meta["round_id"]
    rep.add(
        "file_location",
        fp.parent.name == model_id,
        "File directory name matches `model_id` in file name.",
        fail_message=f'File should be in directory "{model_id}", '
        f'not "{fp.parent.name}".',
    )
    rnd = hub.find_round(round_id)
    if not rep.add(
        "round_id_valid",
        rnd is not None,
        "`round_id` is valid.",
        halt=True,
        fail_message=f'`round_id` "{round_id}" is not in '
        "hub-config/tasks.json.",
    ):
        return rep
    assert rnd is not None
    if not rep.add(
        "file_format",
        meta["ext"] in hub.file_formats,
        "File is accepted hub format.",
        halt=True,
        fail_message=f'Extension "{meta["ext"]}" not in {hub.file_formats}.',
    ):
        return rep
    clock = now or datetime.now(hub.timezone)
    if clock.tzinfo is None:
        clock = clock.replace(tzinfo=hub.timezone)
    dirs = [*metadata_dirs, hub.path / "model-metadata"]
    rep.add(
        "metadata_exists",
        find_metadata(model_id, dirs) is not None,
        "Metadata file exists.",
        fail_message=f"No metadata file {model_id}.yml or .yaml.",
    )
    if skip_window:
        rep.skip("submission_time", "Submission window check skipped.")
    else:
        start, end = hub.submission_window(rnd, round_id)
        t = clock
        rep.add(
            "submission_time",
            start <= t <= end,
            "Submission time is within the submission window.",
            fail_message=f"Time {t.isoformat()} is outside window "
            f"{start.isoformat()} to {end.isoformat()}.",
        )

    # Read.
    try:
        with fp.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
            reader = csv.DictReader(fh)
            cols = list(reader.fieldnames or [])
            rows: list[Row] = [dict(r) for r in reader]
    except (OSError, csv.Error, UnicodeDecodeError) as e:
        rep.add(
            "file_read",
            False,
            "",
            halt=True,
            fail_message=f"File could not be read: {e}",
        )
        return rep
    date_ids = _date_task_ids(rnd)
    bad_read = []
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, start=2):
        if None in r or any(v is None for v in r.values()):
            bad_read.append(f"line {i}: wrong number of fields")
            continue
        v = r.get("value", "")
        if v not in NA_STRINGS and not _is_number(v):
            bad_read.append(f'line {i}: `value` "{v}" is not numeric')
        for c in date_ids & set(cols):
            if r[c] not in NA_STRINGS and not DATE_RE.match(r[c]):
                bad_read.append(f'line {i}: `{c}` "{r[c]}" is not a date')
    if not rep.add(
        "file_read",
        not bad_read,
        "File could be read.",
        halt=True,
        fail_message="File could not be read with the hub schema: "
        + "; ".join(bad_read[:5]),
    ):
        return rep

    # The hub's own forecast_date checks, then the standard ones on the
    # rows this submission adds, without that column. Files of the
    # round's first, cumulative target have neither column and are not
    # subject to them.
    if FORECAST_DATE in cols or "target_end_date" in cols:
        prev_cols: list[str] | None = None
        prev_rows: list[Row] | None = None
        if previous is not None:
            try:
                prev_cols, prev_rows = read_rows(previous)
            except (OSError, csv.Error, UnicodeDecodeError) as e:
                rep.add(
                    "forecast_date_preserved",
                    False,
                    "",
                    halt=True,
                    fail_message=f"The hub's copy could not be read: {e}",
                )
                return rep
        today = None if skip_window else clock.astimezone(hub.timezone).date()
        problems, new_idx = forecast_date_problems(
            rows, cols, prev_rows, prev_cols, today
        )
        for check, message in problems:
            rep.add(check, False, "", halt=True, fail_message=message)
        if problems:
            return rep
        rep.add(
            "forecast_date",
            True,
            "`forecast_date` is valid and adds one new date.",
        )
        rows = [
            {k: v for k, v in rows[i].items() if k != FORECAST_DATE}
            for i in new_idx
        ]
        cols = [c for c in cols if c != FORECAST_DATE]

    # Round id column.
    ric = rnd.round_id
    if rnd.round_id_from_variable:
        if not rep.add(
            "valid_round_id_col",
            ric in cols,
            "`round_id_col` name is valid.",
            halt=True,
            fail_message=f'Column "{ric}" missing.',
        ):
            return rep
        ids = sorted({r[ric] for r in rows})
        if not rep.add(
            "unique_round_id",
            len(ids) == 1,
            f'`round_id` column "{ric}" has a single value.',
            halt=True,
            fail_message=f'Column "{ric}" contains {len(ids)} '
            f"values: {', '.join(ids)}.",
        ):
            return rep
        if not rep.add(
            "match_round_id",
            ids[0] == round_id,
            "`round_id` column matches the file name.",
            halt=True,
            fail_message=f"`round_id` value {ids[0]} does not "
            f'match file name "{round_id}".',
        ):
            return rep

    # Columns.
    expected = [*rnd.task_id_names, *STD_COLS]
    missing = [c for c in expected if c not in cols]
    extra = [c for c in cols if c not in expected]
    msg = []
    if missing:
        msg.append(f"Missing column(s): {', '.join(missing)}.")
    if extra:
        msg.append(f"Unexpected column(s): {', '.join(extra)}.")
    if not rep.add(
        "colnames",
        not msg,
        "Column names are valid.",
        halt=True,
        fail_message=" ".join(msg),
    ):
        return rep

    # Valid values and combinations.
    mt_idx = [_row_model_task(r, rnd) for r in rows]
    bad_rows = [r for r, m in zip(rows, mt_idx, strict=True) if m is None]
    if not rep.add(
        "valid_vals",
        not bad_rows,
        "`tbl` contains valid values/value combinations.",
        halt=True,
        fail_message=_invalid_values(
            bad_rows, rnd, [*rnd.task_id_names, "output_type"]
        ),
    ):
        return rep

    # Unique rows.
    key_cols = [*rnd.task_id_names, "output_type", "output_type_id"]
    keys = Counter(tuple(norm(r[c]) for c in key_cols) for r in rows)
    dups = sum(n - 1 for n in keys.values() if n > 1)
    rep.add(
        "rows_unique",
        dups == 0,
        "All task id/output type/output type id combinations are unique.",
        fail_message=f"{dups} duplicated row(s).",
    )

    _check_req_vals(rep, rows, rnd, mt_idx)
    _check_values(rep, rows, rnd, mt_idx)
    _check_non_desc(rep, rows, rnd)
    if any(r["output_type"] == "sample" for r in rows):
        _check_samples(rep, rows, rnd, mt_idx)
    else:
        for c in (
            "spl_mt_unique",
            "spl_compound_taskid_set",
            "spl_compound_tid",
            "spl_non_compound_tid",
            "spl_n",
        ):
            rep.skip(c, "No samples found.")
    _check_readme_horizon(rep, rows, round_id)
    return rep

def validate_metadata(file: str | Path, hub: Hub) -> Report:
    """Run the model metadata checks on one YAML file.

    Parameters
    ----------
    file : str or pathlib.Path
        The metadata file.
    hub : Hub
        The hub configuration, with its metadata schema.

    Returns
    -------
    Report
        The checks and their outcomes.
    """
    fp = Path(file)
    rep = Report(str(file))
    if not rep.add(
        "metadata_file_ext",
        fp.suffix in (".yml", ".yaml"),
        'Metadata file extension is "yml" or "yaml".',
        halt=True,
    ):
        return rep
    try:
        data = yaml.safe_load(fp.read_text())
    except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError) as e:
        rep.add(
            "metadata_file_read",
            False,
            "",
            halt=True,
            fail_message=f"Could not read YAML: {e}",
        )
        return rep
    if hub.metadata_schema is None:
        rep.skip("metadata_matches_schema", "No metadata schema in hub.")
    else:
        errs = _schema_errors(data, hub.metadata_schema)
        if not rep.add(
            "metadata_matches_schema",
            not errs,
            "Metadata file contents are consistent with schema.",
            halt=True,
            fail_message="; ".join(errs),
        ):
            return rep
    mid = f"{data.get('team_abbr')}-{data.get('model_abbr')}"
    rep.add(
        "metadata_file_name",
        fp.stem == mid,
        "Metadata file name matches `model_id`.",
        halt=True,
        fail_message=f'File name "{fp.name}" but `model_id` is "{mid}".',
    )
    return rep

docs.title: bdbvhubrenewal.submission.fitting
docs.text:
Fit configurations for the automated submission workflow.

The submission CI (ci/, see ci/INTEGRATION.md) fits each candidate of its fallback chain with bdbvhubrenewal fit --config <name> and then forecasts from the saved fit with bdbvhubrenewal nowcast --config <name> --fit <dir>. A fit configuration says how to do both.

The chain is bvd (the renewalbvd variant), renewalsp (single patch per location), main (the renewal variant), then the random walks. The renewal configurations run the PyRenew model through bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.renewal.fit_renewal, which samples, draws the trajectories and writes ppc.json. randomwalk needs no fit.

A fit function gets the forecast task, the sampler settings from ci/policy.toml and the fit directory. It writes whatever the forecast needs into the directory and returns the diagnostics.json record. It may append progress lines to progress.log. The forecast function gets the task and the directory and returns province samples (columns SAMPLE_COLUMNS), optionally with an unassigned frame for a national component not assigned to any province.

def randomwalk_config(name: str, model: str = "randomwalk") -> FitConfig:
    """Build a fit configuration that runs a registered sample-free model.

    There is nothing to fit. `fit` records the task and writes
    not-applicable diagnostics and posterior predictive checks, and
    `forecast` runs the model on the task.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        The configuration name.
    model : str
        The registered model to run.

    Returns
    -------
    FitConfig
        The configuration.
    """
    reason = f"{model} has no sampler and no posterior"

    def fit(
        task: ForecastTask, sampler: Mapping[str, Any], fit_dir: Path
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        del task, sampler
        _write_json(
            fit_dir / "ppc.json", _ppc_not_available(model, name, reason)
        )
        return no_sampler_diagnostics(model, name, reason)

    def forecast(task: ForecastTask, fit_dir: Path) -> Forecast:
        del fit_dir
        return Forecast(get_model(model).forecast(task))

    return FitConfig(
        name=name,
        description=f"{model} model, nothing to fit",
        fit=fit,
        forecast=forecast,
        model=model,
    )

def run_fit(
    config: FitConfig,
    task: ForecastTask,
    sampler: Mapping[str, Any],
    fit_dir: Path | str,
    *,
    model: str,
) -> FitResult:
    """Fit a configuration and write the fit directory.

    Writes `fit.json` (the configuration, model, vintage, reference date,
    sampler settings), `diagnostics.json` and
    `progress.log`. The diagnostics are written whether or not the fit
    converged; the CI's gate judges them.

    Parameters
    ----------
    config : FitConfig
        The configuration.
    task : ForecastTask
        The forecast task built from the vintage.
    sampler : mapping
        Sampler settings, the candidate's `sampler` table in
        `ci/policy.toml`.
    fit_dir : pathlib.Path or str
        Where to write.
    model : str
        The model name the CI passed (`--model`), recorded as is.

    Returns
    -------
    FitResult
        The directory and the diagnostics.
    """
    out = Path(fit_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    progress = out / "progress.log"
    with progress.open("a") as fh:
        fh.write(f"config={config.name} vintage={task.vintage} start\n")
    start = time.monotonic()
    diag = config.fit(task, sampler, out)
    diag.setdefault("schema_version", DIAGNOSTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION)
    diag.setdefault("config", config.name)
    diag.setdefault("runtime_seconds", round(time.monotonic() - start, 3))
    _write_json(out / "diagnostics.json", diag)
    _write_json(
        out / FIT_RECORD,
        {
            "model": model,
            "config": config.name,
            "description": config.description,
            "vintage": task.vintage,
            "reference_date": task.reference_date.isoformat(),
            "sampler": dict(sampler),
        },
    )
    with progress.open("a") as fh:
        fh.write(f"config={config.name} done\n")
    return FitResult(out, diag)

def run_forecast(
    config: FitConfig, task: ForecastTask, fit_dir: Path | str | None
) -> Forecast:
    """Forecast from a fit, checking the fit matches the task.

    Parameters
    ----------
    config : FitConfig
        The configuration.
    task : ForecastTask
        The forecast task.
    fit_dir : pathlib.Path or str, optional
        The fit directory written by `run_fit`. Required unless the
        configuration needs no fit, as the random walk configurations do not.

    Returns
    -------
    Forecast
        Province samples and any unassigned national component.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the fit is of another configuration or vintage.
    """
    path = Path(fit_dir) if fit_dir is not None else Path()
    if fit_dir is not None:
        record = read_fit(path)
        if record["config"] != config.name:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The fit in {fit_dir} is of config {record['config']!r}, "
                f"not {config.name!r}."
            )
        if record["vintage"] != task.vintage:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The fit in {fit_dir} is of vintage {record['vintage']}, "
                f"not {task.vintage}."
            )
    result = config.forecast(task, path)
    check_samples(result.samples, task)
    return result

docs.title: bdbvhubrenewal.submission.rounds
docs.text:
Docs pages for the submitted rounds, from the submission ledger.

The submission workflow records every live round on the submission-ledger branch: state.json holds each round's outcome, and archive/<reference_date>/<run>/ holds the files of each run (the hub file, the plot, the provenance and the pull request body).

Each round records every hub model it submitted under models, keyed by hub model id, with the folder of that model's archived files. make_round_pages turns that into one page per round at docs/submission/rounds/<reference_date>.md, served at /submission/rounds/<reference_date>/, which the hub pull requests link to, with one tab per hub model id. The index is the submission log, one table per hub model id, and a snippet on the latest submission goes to the Nowcast page. A new hub model id appears without code changes.

A round's page is frozen once its hub pull request has merged: freeze_round writes it to pages/ on the ledger branch, once, and later docs builds copy that file as it is. Rounds not yet frozen are built from the ledger at each docs build.

def latest_run(round_dir: Path) -> Path | None:
    """Return the newest run folder of a round's archive.

    Parameters
    ----------
    round_dir : pathlib.Path
        `archive/<reference_date>/` on the ledger branch.

    Returns
    -------
    pathlib.Path or None
        The run folder with the largest run id, or None if there is none.
    """
    runs = [p for p in round_dir.iterdir() if p.is_dir()]
    if not runs:
        return None

    def key(p: Path) -> tuple[int, str]:
        return (int(p.name), p.name) if p.name.isdigit() else (-1, p.name)

    return max(runs, key=key)

def round_page(
    reference_date: str, entry: dict[str, Any], ledger: Path, out: Path
) -> str:
    """Return the Markdown page of one round, with one tab per hub model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reference_date : str
        The round.
    entry : dict
        The round's record in the ledger's `state.json`.
    ledger : pathlib.Path
        A checkout of the `submission-ledger` branch.
    out : pathlib.Path
        Folder of the page, where each model's plot is copied.

    Returns
    -------
    str
        The page.
    """
    lines = [f"# Round {reference_date}", ""]
    lines.append(
        f"Nowcasts and forecasts submitted to the BDBV Modeling Hub for the "
        f"round with reference date {reference_date}."
    )
    lines.append("{ .page-subtitle }")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append(f"Data vintage (`as_of`): {entry.get('as_of') or 'n/a'}.")
    lines.append("")
    for model_id, model in sorted(entry.get("models", {}).items()):
        lines += [f'=== "{model_id}"', ""]
        section = _model_section(reference_date, model_id, model, ledger, out)
        text = "\n".join(section).splitlines()
        lines += [f"    {x}" if x else "" for x in text]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

def freeze_round(ledger: Path | str, reference_date: str) -> bool:
    """Write a round's page to the ledger's `pages/`, unless it is there.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ledger : pathlib.Path or str
        A checkout of the `submission-ledger` branch.
    reference_date : str
        The round, which must be in the ledger's `state.json`.

    Returns
    -------
    bool
        True if the page was written, False if it was already frozen.
    """
    ledger = Path(ledger)
    out = ledger / FROZEN
    if (out / f"{reference_date}.md").exists():
        return False
    entry = _read(ledger / "state.json")["rounds"][reference_date]
    out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    _render(ledger, reference_date, entry, out)
    return True

Write the round pages, the submission log and the latest snippet.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ledger Path or str or None

A checkout of the submission-ledger branch. None, or a folder without state.json, means no round has been submitted.

required docs Path or str

The docs folder. Pages go to submission/rounds/ inside it.

'docs' generated Path or str

Where the latest-submission.md snippet goes.

'docs/generated' pr_state callable

Returns a hub pull request's state from its URL.

gh_pr_state

Returns:

Type Description list of str

The reference dates with a page, newest first.

Source code in src/bdbvhubrenewal/submission/rounds.py 
def make_round_pages(
    ledger: Path | str | None,
    docs: Path | str = "docs",
    generated: Path | str = "docs/generated",
    pr_state: Callable[[str], str] = gh_pr_state,
) -> list[str]:
    """Write the round pages, the submission log and the latest snippet.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ledger : pathlib.Path or str or None
        A checkout of the `submission-ledger` branch. None, or a folder
        without `state.json`, means no round has been submitted.
    docs : pathlib.Path or str
        The docs folder. Pages go to `submission/rounds/` inside it.
    generated : pathlib.Path or str
        Where the `latest-submission.md` snippet goes.
    pr_state : callable
        Returns a hub pull request's state from its URL.

    Returns
    -------
    list of str
        The reference dates with a page, newest first.
    """
    out = Path(docs) / "submission" / "rounds"
    if out.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    root = Path(ledger or ".")
    state = _read(root / "state.json") if ledger else {}
    rounds: dict[str, Any] = state.get("rounds", {})
    done = sorted(rounds, reverse=True)
    frozen = root / FROZEN
    for ref in done:
        if (frozen / f"{ref}.md").exists():
            for f in frozen.glob(f"{ref}*"):
                shutil.copy(f, out / f.name)
        else:
            _render(root, ref, rounds[ref], out)
    index = ["# Submission log", ""]
    if done:
        index += [
            "Every round each hub model was submitted for, newest first.",
            "The round links to its page.",
            "",
        ]
        index += _log(rounds, root, pr_state)
    (out / "index.md").write_text("\n".join(index) + "\n")
    snippet = Path(generated) / "latest-submission.md"
    snippet.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if done:
        ref = done[0]
        models = rounds[ref].get("models", {})
        each = ", ".join(
            f"{model_id} {m.get('status', '')} "
            f"({m.get('produced_by') or 'n/a'})"
            for model_id, m in sorted(models.items())
        )
        snippet.write_text(
            f"**Latest submission:** "
            f"[round {ref}](submission/rounds/{ref}.md): {each}. "
            "[Submission log](submission/rounds/index.md).\n"
        )
    else:
        snippet.write_text("")
    return done

docs.title: BDBV Modeling Hub submission specification
docs.text:
This spec covers the round BDBV 2026 nowcasting and forecasting of InsightNet-US/BDBV-Modeling-Hub. It was derived from the hub at commit 88478a3 (2026-10-27). Line references are to that commit and use these short names.

  • T is hub-config/tasks.json.
  • A is hub-config/admin.json.
  • S is hub-config/model-metadata-schema.json.
  • MO is model-output/README.md.
  • MM is model-metadata/README.md.
  • W is .github/workflows/validate-submission.yaml.

Where the config and the README differ, the config is what CI enforces. Behaviour marked "tested" was checked by running hubValidations 3.0.0 (the version the hub's CI installed on 2026-10-27) on the fixtures in tests/submission/hub_validation/fixtures/. A pinned copy of the three config files is in tests/submission/hub_validation/fixtures/hub-snapshot/hub-config/.

docs.title: 1. File path and name
docs.text:
• Path: model-output/<model_id>/<reference_date>-<model_id>.csv (MO L26–36, L54–66).
  • model_id is <team_abbr>-<model_abbr>, joined by one hyphen. The metadata file is model-metadata/<model_id>.yml (MO L43–45).
  • reference_date is YYYY-MM-DD and must equal the reference_date column (MO L64, L90).
  • Format: csv only (A L14).
  • The directory name must equal the model_id in the file name (hubValidations file_location, tested).
  • team_abbr and model_abbr match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_+]+$ with at most 16 characters each (S L11–26).
  • One file per model per round (hubValidations file_n). A resubmission in the same forecast week keeps the file name and appends rows (section 2a).

docs.title: 2. Columns and types
docs.text:
Exactly these eight columns, in any order, and no others (MO README, tested with invalid_extra_column, invalid_missing_column and valid_reordered_columns).

column type rule reference_date date YYYY-MM-DD a single value per file, equal to the file name date forecast_date date YYYY-MM-DD on or before reference_date in every row, see section 2a target string wk inc confirmed cases target_end_date date YYYY-MM-DD one of the listed Saturdays location string one of 546 listed codes output_type string sample output_type_id integer sample index value double finite, >= 0, not missing

The task id columns are reference_date, location, target and target_end_date (T L147–205). forecast_date is not a task id. There is no horizon column.

docs.title: 2a. forecast_date
docs.text:
The hub announced this column after the commit above. The rules here follow the hub's model-output/README.md and src/validate-submission.R as read on 2026-11-02. Where this page and the hub differ, the hub's text decides.

  • Every row has a nonblank, valid calendar date in exactly YYYY-MM-DD. NA, timestamps and other formats are rejected.
  • Each row's forecast_date is on or before its reference_date.
  • A new file has exactly one forecast_date in all rows. It is within one day of the date when validation runs in Africa/Kinshasa. The hub takes the day once per run, so a later rerun can fail.
  • A resubmission appends rows to the file on the hub's main branch at the same path. Every existing row is kept unchanged, including duplicate rows. Row and column order may change. The parsed cell text must not change, so 1.0 does not become 1.
  • A resubmission adds rows with exactly one forecast_date that is not in the existing file. No new rows, rows added to an existing date and several new dates all fail. Retained dates are not checked for recency.
  • A resubmission does not extend the submission window.
  • The hub copies only the new rows, without forecast_date, into a temporary hub and runs hubValidations on them. The 100 samples per task are counted for each forecast date. Calling hubValidations::validate_submission() on the file directly rejects the column.

This repository sets forecast_date to the day the PR is opened (the run date in UTC). UTC is within a day of Kinshasa, so the recency check holds. After a candidate is chosen, the CI reads the hub's file for the round from raw GitHub (read only) and appends to it. It does so for the model id that is submitted, so a fallback model appends to the file of the submitting id. bdbvhubrenewal validate (submission/validate.py) checks each rule above, with --previous for the hub's copy, and --skip-window also skips the recency check. The R wrapper drops the column and, given the hub's copy, the retained rows, as the hub's script does. If the hub's copy has no forecast_date column it cannot be appended to, as in the hub's script. If the hub's file already holds the run date, the candidate fails and the round is skipped until a later day.

docs.title: reference_date (round id)
docs.text:
• The round id comes from the reference_date column (round_id_from_variable: true, round_id: "reference_date", T L142–143).
  • Accepted values: optional: ["2026-10-31"] at this commit (T L148–151).
  • It is the Saturday ending the epi week in which the file is submitted (MO L84–90).
  • A workflow proposes the next Saturday every Saturday at 08:00 Kinshasa time and opens a PR for human review (.github/workflows/advance-weekly-dates.yaml). A file for a date not yet merged into T fails round_id_valid (tested, invalid_unknown_round).

docs.title: location
docs.text:
• required: null, optional: 546 codes (T L152–155). These are exactly the codes in auxiliary-data/locations.csv: CD, 26 provinces CD-XX and 519 health zones CD-XX-NN.
  • No location is required, so any subset may be submitted (MO L128).

docs.title: target
docs.text:
• optional: ["wk inc confirmed cases"] (T L156–159).
  • Definition: confirmed cases with symptom onset in the Sunday to Saturday epi week ending on target_end_date (T L224–233). The final revised value in target-data/time-series.csv is the target. target_type: continuous, is_step_ahead: true, time_unit: week.

docs.title: target_end_date
docs.text:
• optional: the Saturdays 2026-02-14 to 2026-11-21 (T L160–205).
  • The list is extended by one week each time a reference date is added (MO L102).
  • The README rule is any epi week from 2026-02-14 up to reference_date + 21 days (MO L102). The config enforces this only through the list. For 2026-10-31 the last listed date is exactly reference_date + 3 weeks.
  • Not every week is required (MO L102).
  • Horizon in weeks is (target_end_date - reference_date) / 7. It ranges from -37 (2026-02-14) to +3 for the 2026-10-31 round.

docs.title: 4. Output type sample
docs.text:
Config (T L207–221):

"sample": {
  "output_type_id_params": {
    "type": "integer",
    "min_samples_per_task": 100,
    "max_samples_per_task": 100,
    "compound_taskid_set": ["reference_date", "location", "target"]
  },
  "value": {"type": "double", "minimum": 0},
  "is_required": true
}
  • output_type must be sample (MO L130–132).
  • output_type_id is an integer sample index (T L210, MO L136).
  • Because target_end_date is not in compound_taskid_set, one sample index is one joint trajectory over all target_end_dates for its location (MO L138).
  • Each (reference_date, location, target) has exactly 100 distinct sample indices (T L211–212, MO L136).
  • Each sample index has exactly one row per target_end_date submitted for its location (MO L138).
  • value is a non-negative double (T L215–218). Non-integer values pass (tested, valid_noninteger_values).
  • No duplicate (task ids, output_type, output_type_id) rows (rows_unique).

docs.title: Sample indices in hubValidations (tested)
docs.text:
The README says ids may be reused across locations (1 to 100 in each) or unique across the file (MO L138). hubValidations 3.0.0 treats all rows sharing an output_type_id as one sample and infers the compound task id set from the data. The two schemes then behave differently.

  • Reused ids (as in the only accepted round-2 file, OHTJHU-BM). A configured compound task id that varies within a sample is dropped, so the inferred set is [reference_date, target]. hubValidations accepts this as "coarser" than the configured set. Each id is then a draw that is joint across locations. Every id must cover the identical set of (location, target_end_date) pairs (spl_non_compound_tid). So every location must use the same 100 ids, and every id must have the full week set for each location. Different locations may cover different weeks (tested, location_week_sets_differ is valid).
  • Unique ids per location. The inferred set is the configured one. Every sample must cover the identical set of target_end_dates, so all locations must cover the same weeks (tested, location_week_sets_differ_unique_ids fails spl_non_compound_tid). This is stricter than the README.
  • Mixing the two fails spl_compound_taskid_set (tested, invalid_samples_101).
  • 99 samples in one location with reused ids fails spl_non_compound_tid, not spl_n (tested, invalid_samples_99).
  • A missing week in one trajectory fails spl_non_compound_tid (tested, invalid_ragged_trajectory).

Recommended layout: reuse ids 1..100 in every location, use the same set of weeks for every location, and make sample k of CD the sum of sample k of the provinces. This passes under either reading and matches the joint meaning hubValidations gives reused ids.

docs.title: 5. Submission window
docs.text:
• submissions_due: {relative_to: reference_date, start: -6, end: -4} (T L238–242).
  • Time zone Africa/Kinshasa (A L15), which is WAT, UTC+1, with no daylight saving.
  • hubValidations opens the window at 00:00:00 on the start day and closes it at 23:59:59 on the end day, in hub time. For 2026-10-31 that is Sunday 2026-10-25 00:00:00 WAT (2026-10-24 23:00 UTC) to Tuesday 2026-10-27 23:59:59 WAT (22:59:59 UTC).
  • The check compares the clock at the time the CI job runs (validate_pr(..., skip_submit_window_check = FALSE), W). A re-run or a new push after the window closes fails.
  • validate_pr defaults to file_modification_check = "error" with allow_submit_window_mods = TRUE. So a submitted file can be changed or deleted only inside its window.

docs.title: 6. Model metadata
docs.text:
Schema (S), with additionalProperties: true at the top level (S L120).

Required (S L121–129):

field rule team_name string team_abbr string, ^[a-zA-Z0-9_+]+$, at most 16 characters model_name string model_abbr string, ^[a-zA-Z0-9_+]+$, at most 16 characters model_contributors array of objects with name, affiliation, orcid (^\d{4}-\d{4}-\d{4}-[\dX]{4}$), email (format email), twitter; no sub-field is required license one of CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY_SA-4.0, PPDL, ODC-by, ODbL, OGL-3.0 model_details object with required data_inputs (string) and methods (string, at most 200 characters); optional methods_long; no other keys

Optional: model_version, website_url (uri), repo_url (uri), citation, team_funding, ensemble_of_hub_models (boolean).

Checks run by submission.validate.validate_metadata (tested): the extension is yml or yaml, the contents match the schema, and the file name equals <team_abbr>-<model_abbr>. hubValidations enforces format: email (tested, invalid_bad_email).

docs.title: 7. Round rules
docs.text:
• Two rounds share round_id: reference_date (T L4–140 and L141–243). Round 1, BVBD 2026 cumulative outbreak size estimate, is closed in practice but its reference dates stay in T (MO L234–250). Its window is −7 to +28 days around each reference date (T L135–139).
  • A file belongs to the round whose reference dates include its date. The two lists do not overlap.
  • One model task per round, so spl_mt_unique is trivial here.

docs.title: 8. Ambiguities and inconsistencies
docs.text:
1. Reused versus unique sample ids. The README allows both, but with unique ids hubValidations also requires every location to cover the same weeks. See section 4.
  2. Joint meaning of reused ids. compound_taskid_set says samples are independent across locations, but reusing ids makes hubValidations treat them as joint across locations. Nothing says whether the hub will use cross-location joint structure (for example to aggregate health zones).
  3. Sample id type is not enforced. The config says integer, but 100.5 passes hubValidations 3.0.0 because the hub-wide output_type_id column is typed double (round 1 has quantile levels). submission/validate.py fails it as spl_id_type.
  4. Horizon rule is README-only. "Up to three weeks after the reference date" is enforced only by the length of the target_end_date list. If the list ever runs ahead of the reference dates, later weeks would pass. submission/validate.py warns (readme_horizon) but does not fail.
  5. Values need not be integers. The target is a count, but value is double.
  6. Target wording. The target says "laboratory-confirmed cases", but the observed counts include onsets imputed by back-sampling a delay (target-data README).
  7. Timing of new reference dates. The next reference_date is proposed on Saturday at 08:00 WAT by a bot PR that needs human review. If it is not merged before a submission, round_id_valid fails.
  8. Window check time. The check uses the time the CI job runs, not the PR opening time. A late re-run fails, and whether maintainers merge such PRs is not stated.
  9. Name lengths. MO L35 says team and model "less than 15 characters", MO L66 says "less than 16" and S allows up to 16. MM says team and model names under 50 characters, which S does not enforce. Use at most 14 characters for each abbreviation to satisfy all three.
  10. Required contributor fields. MM says name, affiliation and email are required for each contributor. S requires none of them (tested, valid_no_email passes).
  11. Schema quirk. In S L53 "additionalProperties": false sits inside the contributor properties. It is read as a property named additionalProperties, so contributor objects may carry any extra keys.
  12. License wording. MM suggests cc-by-4.0 in lower case, which fails the enum (tested, invalid_license_lowercase). The enum entry CC-BY_SA-4.0 looks like a typo for CC-BY-SA-4.0.
  13. Metadata README leftovers. MM mentions influenza hospital admissions and links to FluSight's licence list. These are template text.

docs.title: 9. Fixtures
docs.text:
tests/submission/hub_validation/fixtures/manifest.json lists every fixture, its expected failing checks for Python and R and, for real files, the source path and commit.

Real submissions copied from the hub:

file source commit note model-output/OHTJHU-BM/2026-10-31-OHTJHU-BM.csv d1ddf9d the only round-2 file at d1ddf9d, written before the hub added forecast_date; 62 locations, 9 weeks, reused ids model-output/epiforecasts-renewal/2026-10-12-epiforecasts-renewal.csv 6b9254a round 1, quantile, mean and median model-output/MOBS-GLEAM_BDBV/2026-06-28-MOBS-GLEAM_BDBV.csv 01f8a71 round 1, columns out of order model-metadata/OHTJHU-BM.yml d1ddf9d model-metadata/epiforecasts-renewal.yml 4174b51 contributors without email model-metadata/MOBS-GLEAM_BDBV.yml ae5ffd8 block-style list

Constructed fixtures are written by tests/submission/hub_validation/make_fixtures.py. Each invalid file changes one thing in valid_basic.

docs.title: Opting in
docs.text:
The steps to start submitting a hub model.

There are three hub models. Each is opted in on its own in config/hub.toml.

hub model model falls back to needs seabbs-rwnowcast random walk on a nowcast (randomwalknowcast) nothing (round skipped) nothing more seabbs-randomwalk the random walk (randomwalk) nothing nothing more seabbs-renewal the renewal chain the next model in the chain in ci/policy.toml [submission] model in config/hub.toml

DRY_RUN is the global switch. Until it is false, a scheduled run builds and checks an opted-in model but pushes nothing. A manual dispatch with dry_run=false pushes whatever DRY_RUN is.

task submission-preflight checks every step it can and lists what is missing. Run it after each part, logged in to gh as seabbs.

docs.title: Once
docs.text:
1. As seabbs-bot, fork the hub. gh repo fork InsightNet-US/BDBV-Modeling-Hub --clone=false
  2. As seabbs-bot, turn off Actions in the fork. gh api -X PUT repos/seabbs-bot/BDBV-Modeling-Hub/actions/permissions -F enabled=false
  3. As seabbs-bot, create a classic token: Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic). Scopes public_repo and workflow only, 90-day expiry. Fine-grained tokens cannot open pull requests on a repository the bot does not belong to. workflow is needed because each branch carries the hub's own workflow changes.
  4. Restrict the hub-submission environment to main. gh api -X PUT repos/seabbs/BDBVHubRenewal/environments/hub-submission -F 'deployment_branch_policy[protected_branches]=false' -F 'deployment_branch_policy[custom_branch_policies]=true' gh api -X POST repos/seabbs/BDBVHubRenewal/environments/hub-submission/deployment-branch-policies -f name=main -f type=branch
  5. Store the token in that environment. gh secret set HUB_SUBMIT_TOKEN --env hub-submission -R seabbs/BDBVHubRenewal
  6. Make the default workflow token read-only. gh api -X PUT repos/seabbs/BDBVHubRenewal/actions/permissions/workflow -f default_workflow_permissions=read -F can_approve_pull_request_reviews=false
  7. Set the locations each file must hold. gh variable set EXPECTED_LOCATIONS -R seabbs/BDBVHubRenewal -b "CD,CD-IT,CD-NK,CD-HU,CD-TO"
  8. Commit an edit to the cron lines of .github/workflows/submit.yml as yourself (/commit --as-me), so failure emails reach you.
  9. Tell Justin Lessler and Claire Smith that weekly pull requests will come from seabbs-bot. A maintainer must approve the hub's checks on the first one.

docs.title: For each hub model
docs.text:
1. Review its metadata in hub/model-metadata/<hub model>.yml, including the contributor list, licence and model name.
  2. Set submit = true for it in config/hub.toml and push to main. For seabbs-renewal, also set [submission] model.
  3. Dry run, and read the pull request body in the job summary. gh workflow run submit.yml -R seabbs/BDBVHubRenewal
  4. Inside the window (Sunday to Tuesday, Kinshasa time), do one supervised live run. gh workflow run submit.yml -R seabbs/BDBVHubRenewal -f dry_run=false
  5. Go live. gh variable set DRY_RUN -R seabbs/BDBVHubRenewal -b false

To pause, set DRY_RUN back to true, set submit = false, or run gh workflow disable submit.yml -R seabbs/BDBVHubRenewal. Renew the token before it expires (step 5 of Once).

docs.title: Submission workflow
docs.text:
How a round goes from new hub data to a pull request.

.github/workflows/submit.yml runs while the hub's window is open (Sunday to Tuesday, Kinshasa time) and on demand. It submits only the hub models opted in (Opting in), and pushes nothing while DRY_RUN is on.

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text: job what it does detect Stops unless the open round has new hub data, or if its PR is already open or merged. A change to the model code on main since the round's PR reruns it and updates the PR, as does a manual dispatch. freeze Freezes the page of every round once each hub model's pull request is merged or closed. release Makes a GitHub release round-<reference date> of every round whose window has closed and whose hub pull requests are all merged or closed, at the commit it was submitted from. Zenodo archives each release with a DOI. prepare Pins the data, builds randomwalk and randomwalknowcast, and decides which hub models run. baseline The baseline hub model: checks and submits randomwalknowcast, or skips the round if it is ruled out. fit The renewal hub model: fits bvd, renewalsp and main in parallel. gate, submit Walks the chain, validates, and opens or updates the pull request. record Live runs only: writes the round, and each hub model's submission under its id, to the submission-ledger branch. outcome Fails the run if a round was skipped or a job broke.

docs.title: renewal chain
docs.text:
The first candidate that clears the checks is submitted, under seabbs-renewal.

The chain runs from the most to the least complex renewal model, then the random walks.

  1. bvd: renewalbvd, the renewal model informed by BVDOutbreakSize Rt.
  2. renewalsp: independent single-patch fits.
  3. main: renewal, the province renewal model.
  4. randomwalknowcast: random walk on a nowcast.
  5. randomwalk.

[submission] model in config/hub.toml says where the chain starts. Every fit is 2 chains of 500 warm-up, run in parallel, with no refit. renewalbvd takes 1000 draws at target acceptance 0.95, and the others 500 at 0.9. Fit timeouts are set against the window's close ([timing] in ci/policy.toml).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
An invalid file, a fit past the convergence failure thresholds or a forecast far from the recent data rules a candidate out. Thresholds are in ci/policy.toml.

check rules out warns max R-hat > 1.1 > 1.05 min bulk and tail ESS < 25 < 100 divergent share > 5% > 1% 90% predictive coverage < 0.70 schema, values, 100 samples per trajectory any hub validation (Python and hubValidations) any error plausible (median and 97.5% quantile against the recent maximum) any national equals the provinces plus the unassigned part in national.json any bounds, growth, against observed, random walk and last week yes

The hub specification lists the hub's rules.

docs.title: Pull request
docs.text:
It goes from seabbs-bot/BDBV-Modeling-Hub, branch <model_id>-<reference_date>, into the hub's main. The body shows what was submitted, one status line, the plot and a link to the round's page. The details sit in collapsed sections.

Every row carries a forecast_date, the day the PR is opened. If the hub's main already has this model's file for the round, the gate reads it (read only) and writes the file the PR holds as the hub's rows unchanged plus the new rows with one new forecast_date (hub specification). The same file goes through both validators. The submit step stops, without pushing, if the hub's file changed after the gate.

A round's page is frozen once its pull request merges, and later docs builds do not change it (Submission log).

Submission of seabbs-renewal for 2026-11-07, from data as of 2026-11-01, for 187 locations.

Signed off by Sam Abbott (@seabbs).

Model: BVDOutbreakSize-informed renewal model (renewalbvd), the first model in our chain and the first to clear its checks.
